item.title: Constraints on the Higgs boson total width from on-shell signal–background interference in H→γγ
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
ATLAS extracts a direct, coupling-independent bound on Γ_H from the interference between the resonant gg→H→γγ amplitude and the continuum diphoton background, which distorts the m_γγ lineshape — an antisymmetric peak shift (~-70 MeV at the SM width) plus a ~-1.7% yield reduction, both scaling as √(μ Γ_H/Γ_H^SM). Using the full 140 fb⁻¹ Run 2 dataset in two p_T^γγ categories, with m_H externally constrained from H→ZZ^*→4ℓ and μ profiled, they set an observed (expected) 95% CL limit Γ_H<307 (258) MeV, ~75× the SM value; the best fit is Γ̂H=13⁺⁷⁵-13 MeV and μ=1.08±0.12. Statistics-only, the limit tightens to 105 (87) MeV.

Why it matters: unlike the off-shell ZZ/WW method (ATLAS combined Γ_H=3.6⁺².1_-1.6 MeV), this probe makes no assumption that on- and off-shell couplings coincide, so it remains valid under exotic or invisible decays — a genuinely orthogonal handle even at ~30× weaker sensitivity. The caveat is explicit and dominant: the measurement is systematics-limited, with the largest single contribution (49 MeV at 68% CL) from the 39% theory uncertainty on the gg-interference K-factor (K_I=1.64, NLO→NNLOsv), followed by the m_H constraint (43 MeV). Because interference scales as √(Γ_H), the K_I uncertainty dominates entirely near the limit. The authors flag that interference calculations matched to parton showers are the needed improvement, and note only two p_T^γγ bins are justified given current modelling.

item.title: Computability of GPDs near x=±ξ in Lattice QCD
item.dc:creator: Yushan Su et al.
item.description:
Su, Ji, Liu, and Zhang argue that the LaMET large-momentum expansion for GPDs does not require the naive EFT condition 2|x±ξ|P^z≫Λ_QCD near the transition points x=±ξ, where one parton momentum vanishes. Their argument parallels DVCS factorization: soft contributions associated with the vanishing scale are power-suppressed, just as photon-DA physics enters DVCS only at O(Λ_QCD²/Q²⁾. The condition reduces to keeping at least one hard scale, 2(|x|+|ξ|)P^z≫Λ_QCD, dramatically enlarging the computable window that would otherwise exclude bands of width ~0.4 around x=±ξ for realistic P^z∼2–3 GeV.

Reanalyzing four existing nonzero-skewness datasets (ETMC20/21/25, MSULat23) with complete one-loop matching and a carefully ordered regulator hierarchy (ϵ_2≪|ϵ_1|→0, the only convergent ordering), they recover GPDs that are continuous at x=±ξ but with discontinuous derivatives — the expected partonic threshold kink from soft-quark zero modes, seen on the lattice for the first time and consistent with polynomiality-preserving GPD models. The previously reported discontinuities are attributed to regulator artifacts in the matching. This yields the first first-principles prediction of GPDs in the distribution-amplitude-like region (|x|<ξ), smoothly connecting quark and antiquark PDF-like regimes — directly relevant to DVCS extractions and the GUMP global-analysis program.

Caveats: the result rests on one-loop matching applied to existing data at coarse pion masses (mostly 260 MeV) and modest momenta, and the region remains uncomputable when both x and ξ are small (near x=0) or near the endpoints x=±1.

item.title: Observation of double ss̅ production in e⁺e⁻ collision at √(s)=3.08 GeV
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
BESIII reports the first systematic observation of double-ss̅ production in the e⁺e⁻ continuum, tagging a prompt ϕ recoiling against a second strangeness-carrying system X(ss̅) ∈{η,η’,K⁺K⁻,K⁺K^-,K⁻K^+,K⁰K̅⁰,K⁰K̅^0}. From 167 pb⁻¹, they measure σ(e⁺e⁻→ϕ+anything)=506.3±6.9±19.7 pb (a first) plus the individual ϕ+X(ss̅) cross sections, with ϕK⁺K^-, ϕK⁻K^+, ϕK⁰K̅⁰, ϕK⁰K̅^0 reported for the first time. After subtracting ISR (ϕγ_ISR) to isolate the QCD-driven part, the ratio is R_ss̅=(40.4±1.7_stat±1.5_syst)%.

Why it matters: this large ratio directly echoes the double-cc̅ surprise seen by Belle and BABAR at 10.6 GeV, where R_cc̅ exceeded early NRQCD predictions and drove years of theory refinement. Extending the phenomenon to the strange sector — in the deep non-perturbative regime — supplies a clean hadronization number that challenges the frameworks tuned to R_cc̅ and opens a window on possible flavor correlations in fragmentation. The synergy of strange and charm “flavor portals” is the framing.

Caveat, stated by the authors: the measurement omits higher-multiplicity final states (e.g. ϕK⁺K⁻π⁰), so R_ss̅ is a lower bound on total double-ss̅ rate; f_ss̅ assumptions for η/η’ and f-states carry model dependence, and several sub-channels have 6–11% systematics dominated by efficiency and background modelling.

item.title: Non-singlet splitting functions at four loops
item.dc:creator: Thomas Gehrmann et al.
item.description:
The full non-singlet splitting functions P_ns⁺, P_ns⁻, and P_ns^s=P_ns^v-P_ns⁻ are now known analytically at four loops for arbitrary Mellin moment n — the reference the field will cite for N³LO evolution. The method computes off-shell quark operator matrix elements for twist-two spin-n operators, using generating functions to keep n arbitrary while retaining standard IBP identities (via Qgraf, Form, Reduze2, and the finite-field Finred code). Rather than fight the elliptic geometries appearing in one color sector, the differential equations in the tracing parameter t are Taylor-expanded about t=0, where the integrals reduce to known four-loop propagator masters; moments up to n∼4000 are then generated and the all-n result reconstructed from an ansatz of harmonic sums up to weight 7. Results confirm all known color coefficients and reproduce independent fixed-moment checks, the four-loop cusp coefficient A_q⁽⁴⁾, and yield fully analytic virtual anomalous dimensions B_q⁽⁴⁾ and B_g⁽⁴⁾ plus the eikonal soft anomalous dimension f_r⁽⁴⁾.

Why it matters: consistent N³LO LHC cross sections require exactly these functions, previously available only as numerical approximations or partial analytics — anchoring today’s precision-QCD theme. Agreement with the Moch–Ruijl–Ueda–Vermaseren–Vogt numerics is good, though P_ns⁽³⁾,+ sits slightly above their error band at small x. One honest wrinkle: the ln⁴ x small-x terms disagree with the resummation prediction of Davies et al., by a piece subleading in N_c and proportional to ζ_2 — possibly an (iπ)² phase effect the authors flag for investigation. The singlet case remains, requiring gauge-variant operator renormalization.

item.title: Enhanced Standard Model bound on charm CP violation from QCD penguins
item.dc:creator: Ali Mohamed et al.
item.description:
Using light-cone sum rules with an auxiliary momentum inserted at the weak vertex (following the B→ππ methodology of Khodjamirian) to avoid parasitic cuts, Mohamed and Piscopo compute for the first time the QCD-penguin operator matrix elements for D⁰→K⁺K⁻ and D⁰→π⁺π⁻ at leading order in α_s. The scalar penguins Q_5,Q_6 are strongly enhanced: -i⟨Q_6⟩_ππ=2.09 GeV³ versus 0.228 for the current-current Q_1^d — roughly a factor of ten. Two sources drive this: quark-condensate contributions arising at tree level (enhanced by 16π² over the loop-induced terms) and an annihilation-type contribution from the u̅ u component entering already at twist three. Recomputed current-current matrix elements agree with the earlier Lenz et al. determination to within 5–10%, and the resulting branching ratios (ℬ(ππ)=1.22×10⁻³, ℬ(KK)=2.44×10⁻³) match HFLAV within their ~100% uncertainties.

Why it matters: the 2019 LHCb ΔA_CP∼10⁻³ needs penguin-to-tree ratios of order unity, an order of magnitude above naive estimates, and whether this fits the SM hinges on hadronic matrix elements. Enhanced penguins narrow the SM-vs-experiment gap — direct progress on the standing charm-CPV puzzle flagged in August. Caveat, stated plainly: the strong phases remain unconstrained at LO α_s, so no quantitative CP-asymmetry prediction follows; the bound assumes maximal phases. The annihilation approximation carries an expected ≥30% error because s_0/m_D²∼20–30% (versus ~3% for B decays).

item.title: Dark Radiation Sticks Together: Dark QCD and the Hubble Tension
item.dc:creator: Matthew R. Buckley et al.
item.description:
Buckley, Fernandez, and Putney propose a confining SU(N_c) dark sector with heavy stable quarks (the dark matter) and light quarks whose confinement at Λ_D∼ MeV turns the dark radiation into light dark pions. Crucially, residual strong interactions make this radiation a viscous imperfect fluid rather than free-streaming — modeled in a modified CLASS with drag (Γ_drag) and relaxation-time equations. The viscosity suppresses high-ℓ CMB oscillations relative to free-streaming ΔN_eff, letting the model raise H_0 without spoiling the high-ℓ multipoles or S_8. A full MCMC over Planck, ACT, DESI DR2, Pantheon+, SH0ES, and BBN yields H_0=71.60±0.63 km/s/Mpc with a residual tension of ∼3σ (Q_DMAP=3.0σ vs 6.0σ for ΛCDM), competitive with Hubble World Cup “finalists.” It also fits DESI BAO better than Planck-only ΛCDM.

Why it matters: this is a genuinely different mechanism for the Hubble tension — not just extra N_eff, but self-interacting radiation whose fluid behavior evades the high-ℓ constraints that cap free-streaming models near 4σ. The large late-time self-interaction cross section (∼Λ_D⁻²) evades Bullet Cluster bounds because hard momentum transfer requires perturbative heavy-quark scattering. Honest caveats: the best-fit Λ_D∼1 MeV produces dark acoustic oscillations in tension with Lyman-α, though Λ_D≳3–5 MeV evades this with negligible fit degradation; and the CLASS modifications were partly LLM-generated.

item.title: Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with Astrophysical Uncertainties and Solar Capture
item.dc:creator: Aditya Ghosh et al.
item.description:
The higgsino reading of LZ’s 248 keV recoil cannot survive the solar-capture bound no matter how the halo is stretched. Ghosh, Chavez, and Kelso compute the expected LZ signal for a 1.1 TeV thermal higgsino (WimPyDD, including the factor-4 cross-section correction of Pospelov–Ramani) across the full Standard Halo Model parameter space and, separately, using N-body hydrodynamical halos that include the LMC’s imprint on the high-speed tail. IceCube/Super-K non-observation of solar annihilation neutrinos requires the inelastic splitting δ≳506–566 keV, which for a 248 keV xenon recoil demands lab-frame speeds v_min∼950–1025 km/s. In the SHM, the δ≳566 keV bound requires v_0≳240 km/s independent of v_esc — well beyond the 2σ range of any measured v_0 (up to 256 km/s), even at optimistic ρ_χ=0.45 GeV cm⁻³ and with a 5%-probability upward fluctuation. In the LMC-aware simulated halo, δ=514 keV is the largest splitting that yields one event in the 200–300 keV window; all curves fall below the fluctuation threshold by δ∼530 keV.

Why it matters: This is exactly the discriminator mode the digest tracks — an attempt to close the last astrophysical escape hatch rather than add another fit. The thermal higgsino is now doubly cornered: kinematics and solar capture together leave no viable window at δ≳566 keV.

Caveat: Only the weaker δ≳506 keV bound (tree-level Z up-scatter, not the loop-induced elastic channel) leaves a sliver of SHM viability, and only when both v_0 and v_esc sit at their upper limits. The LMC-tail extension beyond 950 km/s is a phenomenological exponential, not a simulated result.

item.title: Argon as the test of two interpretations of the LZ 248 keV recoil
item.dc:creator: Howard Baer et al.
item.description:
Baer and Barger reduce the endothermic-vs-exothermic debate to a single already-recorded measurement. Both interpretations require an internal splitting, but they flow energy oppositely. Read exothermically (pseudo-Dirac downscatter releasing |δ|), the event predicts a nuclear-recoil line in argon at E_Ar=|δ| m_χ/(m_χ+m_Ar) — 336 keV for m_χ=200 GeV, ranging 268–525 keV over the exothermic family — at ~3–4 events/tonne-yr, roughly ten times the equivalent xenon rate. Argon wins because its Helm form factor at 336 keV sits in the first diffraction lobe (F²⁼⁰.056) while xenon at 248 keV sits near its second-lobe minimum (F²⁼¹.6×10⁻⁴); the factorized rate ratio returns 9.5 at 200 GeV. Read endothermically (ground-state upscatter by the fast halo tail), argon predicts zero events: the argon threshold speed exceeds the halo maximum (1224 vs 796 km/s at 1.1 TeV). The ratio depends only on two-body kinematics, the two form factors, and the coupling’s charge structure — not the mediator or excited fraction.

Why it matters: DEAP-3600 already holds the data. The published 231-day exposure implies ~7 events (full target) or 1.7 (fiducial) at the benchmark rate; the 813-day first run holds ~25 and 6. A reanalysis for single-scatter nuclear recoils between 200–600 keV (near 85 keV_ee) either finds the line and fixes m_χ from the two line positions, or kills the exothermic reading — no new detector required.

Caveat: The fiducial mass at ~500 photoelectrons is unpublished; expected counts within the WIMP-search fiducial volume are only a few, and background control (shadowed alphas, ³⁹Ar, radiogenic neutrons) rests on DEAP’s own estimates.

item.title: First Observation of D_s⁺→f_0(980)μ⁺ν_μ
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
BESIII observes the semi-muonic decay D_s⁺→f_0(980)μ⁺ν_μ (with f_0→π⁺π⁻) for the first time, using 7.33 fb⁻¹ at E_CM=4.128–4.226 GeV and a double-tag technique (839k single tags across 15 hadronic modes). From 196±22 signal events they measure ℬ=(1.59±0.18_stat±0.11_syst)×10⁻³. Combined with the earlier BESIII electronic-channel result, the LFU ratio ℬ(μ)/ℬ(e)=0.92±0.13_stat±0.08_syst agrees with the SM range 0.94–1.11 — no LFU violation at current precision, and the first such test in a scalar-meson c→s transition. A dynamical fit (simple-pole form factor, relativistic Flatté line shape) yields f_+^f_0(0)|V_cs|=0.490±0.059±0.025; averaging with the electronic channel gives 0.500±0.016±0.020, and with CKMfitter |V_cs| the most precise D_s→f_0 form factor to date, f_+^f_0(0)=0.514±0.017±0.021.

Why it matters: Beyond extending LFU tests into scalar final states, the branching fraction implies a mixing angle ϕ=(28.0±26.6)^∘, favoring an ss̅-dominant f_0(980) in the qq̅ picture. The precise form factor discriminates sharply among models: consistent with CLFD/DR/QCDSR but in up-to-5σ tension with LCSR, LFQM, and CCQM predictions, all of which now incorporate the finite f_0 width. This is the consolidating-null flavor picture the digest notes — LFU intact, precision turned onto hadronic structure.

Caveat: The 13% statistical LFU uncertainty leaves ample room; the extracted ϕ carries a large error. μ/π misidentification is handled by retaining both track pairings and fitting the wrong-combination shape.

item.title: What has the LHC told us about the electroweakino sector of the MSSM?
item.dc:creator: Peter Athron et al.
item.description:
GAMBIT’s most complete collider recast of the MSSM electroweak sector to date: a frequentist global fit over 34 Run 2 LHC searches, 63 Run 2 measurements (via Contur), and LEP cross-section limits, scanning M_1, M_2, μ, tanβ with all other sparticles decoupled. The headline is that a genuine general bound now exists where the 2018 fit found none — for a light bino χ̃_1⁰, exclusion reaches m_χ̃_2⁰≳760 GeV in both the (m_χ̃_2⁰,m_χ̃_1⁰⁾ and chargino planes. Adding a light (m_3/2=1 eV) gravitino pushes exclusions to (m_χ̃_1⁰,m_χ̃_2⁰⁾∼(900,1000) GeV, but a Higgsino-dominated LSP survives down to ≈650 GeV. The much-discussed ATLAS soft-dilepton excess (Δm∼20 GeV) is reproduced as a weak preference near m_χ̃_2⁰≈200 GeV, but the CMS zero-lepton and soft-lepton searches disfavour exactly the ATLAS-preferred region — no scenario fits both simultaneously.

Why it matters: this is the empirical backdrop the month of LZ-higgsino fits has largely ignored. The Higgsino-degenerate corner that survives at ~650 GeV is precisely where compressed dark-matter scenarios live, and closing it at small Δm is conceded to be “very challenging” even at HL-LHC. Honest caveats: signal yields use LO+LL (not NLO) cross-sections, monojet and long-lived-particle searches are omitted, the b-jet regions of ATLAS_2BoostedBosons are not implemented, and the G̃-EWMSSM best fit rests on a 36 fb⁻¹ CMS diphoton excess that newer full-Run-2 photon searches do not corroborate.

item.title: Search for a light pseudoscalar Higgs boson in boosted μμττ final states
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS searches H→aa→μμττ in 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data, where the large m_H–m_a hierarchy collimates each ττ pair. The key methodological advance is dedicated boosted-ditau reconstruction: modified HPS seeding for τ_μτ_h/τ_eτ_h (efficiency gains up to factors of 2–4 at high m_H), plus a new deep-network tagger, DeepDiTau, that classifies AK4 jets as τ_hτ_h at 70% efficiency and ~1% mistag — enabling the high-rate all-hadronic channel for the first time. Combining four ττ channels covers 94% of a→ττ decays. No excess is seen. Model-independent 95% CL limits on σ_H×ℬ/σ_SM reach 5×10⁻⁵ to 2.7×10⁻⁴ for m_a=3.6–21 GeV at m_H=125 GeV, and — for the first time at the LHC in ττ final states — extend to a heavy scalar up to m_H=1 TeV, where limits span 3.5×10⁻⁴ to 1.5×10⁻³ for m_a=3.6–50 GeV.

Why it matters: this is the day’s genuine light-pseudoscalar collider result, complementary to the LZ/axion model-building. It sets the most stringent ℬ(H→aa) limits to date for 3.6<m_a<4.2 GeV in Type-I/II 2HDM+S, improves on prior μμττ results by factors 2–5, and opens the heavy-scalar →aa window entirely. Caveats: sensitivity degrades at low m_a where decay products fully merge, Υ resonances contaminate near m_a≈10 GeV, and above 4.2 GeV the charm-tagging analysis remains stronger.

item.title: Constraints on Galactic Dark Photons from a DALI Prototype
item.dc:creator: Javier De Miguel et al.
item.description:
A proof-of-principle DALI haloscope — a 20-plate yttria-stabilized zirconia Fabry–Pérot resonator read out by an antenna, run at fixed λ/8 spacing with Q_L≈2200 near 6.907 GHz and T_sys≃59 K — reinterprets 36 hours of data (originally an axion search) as a dark-photon search. No magnetic field is needed since kinetic mixing converts dark photons at the dielectric discontinuities. After baseline removal, iterative RFI masking, grand-spectrum stacking with the lab-frame line shape, and an end-to-end injection efficiency of η_e2e≃0.60, no significant excess survives. Fourteen retained clusters all fall below adopted confidence and are flagged for rescan. The result excludes kinetic mixing χ≲6.8×10⁻¹⁴ at 28.54 μeV (6.902 GHz), across 88.1% of the unmasked 28.482–28.610 μeV band at 90% CL — claimed as the strongest laboratory bound in this frequency range.

Why it matters: it fits today’s haloscope theme (alongside DALI’s companion resonator paper), demonstrating that the open Fabry–Pérot architecture — whose cross section decouples from resonance frequency — can deliver competitive high-frequency limits with mature commercial hardware. As a magnet-free dark-photon channel, it is a cheap, fast complement to cavity haloscopes. Caveats are explicit: only a single frequency step (one plate spacing), a scaled-down prototype (~1:100 in area), an undercoupled antenna (β≃0.36), assumption that dark photons saturate the local density with randomly-oriented polarization (κ²⁼¹/3), and a residual 0.09σ baseline systematic.

item.title: Qubit-Qutrit Quantum Tomography of hadronic Λφ and ΛK*⁰ systems
item.dc:creator: Veronica Kanachova et al.
item.description:
Extending collider quantum tomography to unequal-spin final states, Kanachova et al. formalize the spin-½⊗1 density matrix for Λφ and ΛK*⁰ pairs and confront its inescapable incompleteness: the parity-violating Λ→pπ⁻ is fully self-analyzing, but the parity-conserving V→PP decay carries no rank-1 (dipole) analyzer, so only 23 of the 35 spin parameters are measurable — the meson vector polarization Pᵢ (3) and the dipole–dipole correlations Cᵢⱼ (9) drop out identically. The key result is that entanglement can still be certified exactly from this censored data. Zeroing the 12 missing parameters is equivalent to a “partial time reversal” on the meson (𝒰_B∘T_B), and the reconstruction ρ_meas satisfies ρ_meas^{T_B}=𝒰_B(ρ_meas), so the Peres–Horodecki test collapses to a single diagonalization: a negative eigenvalue of ρ_meas certifies entanglement, with no false positives, and no analysis of the same 23 observables can do better. Pure entangled states retain exactly half their negativity; mixed states have quantifiable “blind windows” (e.g. isotropic-noise dilution entangled for p>1/4 but uncertifiable until p>2/5).

Why it matters: this opens a new hadronization probe. Because local dressing cannot create entanglement, surviving correlations lower-bound the quark-pair correlation at production, and comparing degradation in Λφ/ΛK*⁰ (meson channel) against ΛΛ̄ (baryon channel) as a function of ΔR isolates p_meson vs p_baryon — a coherence-transport quantity never measured. Estimators are simple angular moments extractable from existing datasets. Caveat: the theorems’ validity relies on the specific 12-parameter censoring; other 12-subsets give false positives, and much of the numerical verification was AI-assisted (Claude Opus 5) with a stated but unproven pure-state conjecture.

item.title: Positive- and negative-parity charm-strange and bottom-strange mesons from lattice QCD
item.dc:creator: Forrest Guyton et al.
item.description:
Guyton and Meinel deliver a full RBC/UKQCD determination of decay constants, binding energies, and Weinberg compositeness for the lightest scalar, pseudoscalar, vector, and axial-vector Dₛ and Bₛ mesons, using domain-wall light/strange quarks and anisotropic clover charm/bottom on seven ensembles (mπ = 139–431 MeV, a = 0.073–0.114 fm) with combined chiral-continuum extrapolation. For negative-parity states they obtain f_{Dₛ}=251.4(2.1)(0.4)(2.5) MeV, f_{Dₛ}=272.5(4.3)(1.0)(2.7), f_{Bₛ}=228.4(5.8)(0.5)(2.3), f_{Bₛ}=229.2(4.4)(0.8)(2.3) MeV, plus ratios f_{Dₛ}/f_{Dₛ}=1.086(14)(11) and f_{Bₛ}/f_{Bₛ}=1.003(22)(10), consistent with FLAG. The positive-parity sector uses a GEVP with q̄q, derivative, and meson-meson-scattering operators (the latter at both source and sink), Lüscher’s method, and effective-range expansions to extract infinite-volume bound-state masses: m_{Dₛ0}−m_D−m_K=−48(14)(4) MeV, m_{Dₛ1}−m_{D}−m_K=−61(15)(2), m_{Bₛ0}−m_B−m_K=−69(13)(4), m_{Bₛ1}−m_{B}−m_K=−77(10)(5). The charm results agree with experiment (−45.0(6), −44.7(6) MeV). Positive-parity decay constants — including the first-ever lattice f_{Bₛ0*}=207(12)(8)(2) and f_{Bₛ1}=196(16)(11)(2) MeV — are reported.

Why it matters: the below-threshold binding, small positive-parity decay constants, and scattering lengths consistently support a predominantly D⁽⁾K/B⁽⁾K molecular interpretation of the Dₛ0*(2317)-like states, and the negative-parity constants feed dispersive bounds on b→s form factors relevant to the b→sℓℓ anomalies. Caveats acknowledged: two-pion left-hand cuts (which extend above the ground-state energies at low mπ) are neglected, invalidating strict Lüscher/ERE there, and weak-binding corrections to Weinberg’s criterion are expected to be large in some channels.

item.title: Distinguishing a pseudoscalar from a vector t t̄ resonance with top-quark spin correlations at the HL-LHC
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Bellagroudi et al.
item.description:
Bellagroudi and Fassi ask a post-discovery question: given a t t̄ resonance, can dilepton spin correlations separate a CP-odd 2HDM pseudoscalar A (0⁻, spin-singlet ¹S₀, iγ₅ vertex) from a leptophobic topcolor Z′ (1⁻, chiral vector)? Using MadGraph+Pythia+Delphes with matrix-element spin-preserving decays and neutrino-weighting reconstruction, they find a parton-level helicity-correlation gap Δc_hel≃0.43 (A: +0.33, Z′: −0.08), nearly mass-independent, surviving reconstruction with dilution ≈0.66. Normalizing A to CMS HIG-22-013 coupling limits and rate-matching Z′ so the test probes spin structure, the LO t t̄-only baseline gives 2.27σ (400 GeV) and 2.74σ (800 GeV) at 3000 fb⁻¹, using a 4×4 (c_hel, c_han) template likelihood. Reverse non-nested direction agrees; equal-yield tests give 1.86 and 2.70σ (confirming 800 GeV is shape-driven); profiling a Gaussian-constrained SM c_hel nuisance yields 2.07/2.63σ (optimistic) down to 1.67/2.26σ. A g⁴-mapped scan places 5σ at couplings ~22%/16% above reference.

Why it matters: this makes the toponium-vs-scalar interpretation debate quantitative, showing spin correlations can in principle assign resonance spin/parity where a rate excess cannot. The 800 GeV point is the cleanest demonstration; 400 GeV is intrinsically fragile because the near-threshold SM continuum is itself spin-singlet/pseudoscalar-like (the same physics driving threshold entanglement enhancement), and 1500 GeV is unreachable (~12 events). Honest caveats abound: LO normalization, fixed on-shell widths, no non-t t̄ backgrounds, and — critically — omitted signal–continuum interference, plus a single-mode “bracket” nuisance rather than a proper mass-dependent sideband fit.

item.title: Heavy Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event
item.dc:creator: Kevin Langhoff
item.description:
Langhoff performs a 2D likelihood fit of pure-higgsino inelastic scattering to the LZ 248 keV recoil plus the empty high-energy sideband (350–675 keV), then folds in recomputed IceCube solar-capture bounds. The data alone prefer a light branch, m_χ≈(240,450) GeV, but that region is excluded by solar capture (which sets a floor on the splitting δ via neutrinos from captured-higgsino annihilation). The thermal higgsino at 1.1 TeV overfills the sideband (N_SB≳2, Δχ² up to 11). The only corner consistent with the event, the empty sideband and solar capture is m_χ≈(10⁵,10⁶⁾ GeV with δ≈(330,480) keV — where DM dilution (ρ∝1/m_χ) forces small δ and the sideband/ROI event ratio lands near 0.8–1 (versus ∼0.1 light, ≳15 thermal), a testable prediction. Such a heavy higgsino cannot arise from freeze-out, so he builds a proof-of-concept: freeze-out during early matter domination reheating to T_RH≈1 TeV, tied to the μ term via a Kim-Nilles mechanism that also solves strong CP.

Why it matters: it closes today’s headline arc — the ordinary thermal reading is dead, and survival demands a 10⁷ GeV gaugino scale plus a bespoke cosmology, connecting a direct-detection anomaly to axion/strong-CP physics. Caveats are frank: the Δχ² contours are a “heuristic guide” only, the heavy point is not the best fit, results depend on LMC-tail halo modeling, solar-capture curves bracket limiting behavior rather than a precise bound, and the model needs a tuned axion misalignment (θ≲0.05).

item.title: Nucleon Strong-Interaction Size from Charmonium Photoproduction
item.dc:creator: Xiangdong Ji et al.
item.description:
Ji, Joosten, Meziani, and Pefkou extract the nucleon’s overall strong-interaction radius by combining world near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction data (GlueX, Hall C, CLAS12) with a recent Bayesian quark-sector GFF analysis. Fitting the differential cross sections in a holographic-QCD model — A_g(t) dipole, C_g(t) tripole, B_g=0 — yields the gluon stress-energy form factors (χ²/ndf=1.005 after dropping the lowest GlueX energy bin). Energy-momentum conservation then relates the total A,C form factors to the scalar (trace-anomaly) color-field distribution G^s(t), whose Breit-frame radius is ⟨r_s²⟩¹/2=0.94±0.09 fm — larger than the PDG charge radius (0.8409 fm) and larger than the mass radius, defining a gluonic “skin” analogous to the neutron skin in ²⁰⁸Pb.

Why it matters: it delivers a clean, quotable first experimental number for the nucleon’s strong-interaction extent, mapping the color field that generates most of the nucleon mass rather than its charge. The ordering (strong > charge > mass) agrees with lattice and dispersive determinations cited. Caveats are stated plainly: the identification of the photoproduction amplitude with the gluonic SET is framework-dependent (open-charm and alternative production mechanisms may contaminate), B_g=0 is an assumption, and the result inherits both statistical and model uncertainty. SoLID and EIC/ePIC are projected to improve precision by up to an order of magnitude.

item.title: Can Elastic Neutrino Scattering Account for the LZ230616 Event?
item.dc:creator: Ayan Chattaraj et al.
item.description:
Chattaraj et al. systematically test whether coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering (CEνNS) can produce the 248 keV LZ recoil. Kinematics alone require E_ν≳118 MeV, killing solar and DSNB fluxes; only atmospheric neutrinos reach that energy, but their SM rate in the signal bin (225–271 keV) is R_I≃2×10⁻⁶ events. Introducing BSM scalar or vector mediators tuned to give one signal-region event overshoots the low-energy bins by 𝒪(10⁵⁾ events — six orders of magnitude above background — so the R_I=1 contour sits entirely inside the R_II-excluded region. Exotic monochromatic fluxes fare no better: DM annihilation (χχ→νν̅) requires ⟨σv⟩≳10⁻¹⁸ cm³/s and DM decay τ_χ≲10¹⁵ s, both far past existing bounds, while overpopulating low-recoil bins by hundreds of events. PBH evaporation is worst: the exponentially soft Hawking spectrum gives R_II/R_I∼10⁴–10²³ and demands f_PBH≳95, exceeding the total DM density.

Why it matters: the useful null of the day. The broad recoil spectrum inherent to elastic scattering is fundamentally incompatible with an isolated high-energy feature, reinforcing that the LZ event demands an inelastic/threshold mechanism (higgsino, exothermic DM). Caveat: the analysis is deliberately restricted to elastic channels — inelastic neutrino processes and atmospheric-neutrino upscattering (their ref. [29]) are outside scope.

item.title: From LUX-ZEPLIN to Colliders: Probing Higgsino Dark Matter
item.dc:creator: Kingman Cheung et al.
item.description:
Taking the 248 keV LZ recoil at face value as 1.1 TeV thermal Higgsino inelastic DM with neutral splitting δm_0≃350 keV, Cheung, Kang, and Kumar work out the necessary collider corollary: the charged Higgsino sits Δm_+∼(330–350) MeV above the neutral state (electroweak loops dominating over a ∼-9 MeV finite-gaugino tree contribution), giving proper lifetime τ≈0.025 ns, cτ≃(6–8) mm, and decays to a soft ∼300 MeV pion. This is a sub-centimeter disappearing tracklet. Current ATLAS disappearing-track (m_χ^±≲225 GeV) and CMS soft-track (≲185 GeV) limits sit far below the 1.1 TeV target because the survival probability through three pixel hits (R∼9 cm) is ∼3×10⁻⁶ at β_Tγ=1; the 0.57 fb production cross section compounds the problem. HL-LHC needs better short-track reconstruction, not luminosity; dedicated studies find 5σ reach at a 100 TeV collider (30 ab⁻¹) and a 10 TeV muon collider (10 ab⁻¹).

Why it matters: this is the digest’s cleanest LZ-to-collider bridge, converting a direct-detection splitting into a one-parameter trajectory in the (m_χ^±,cτ) plane — a genuinely falsifiable prediction rather than another fit. Caveats are stated honestly: the authors flag the unresolved high-energy S1c sideband tension (acceptance not public), note the charged splitting is not a precision pole-mass calculation, and stress the collider reaches are conditional projections tied to assumed detector geometry and beam-induced backgrounds.

item.title: For Whom the Xenon Recoils: Magnetic Inelastic Dark Baryons
item.dc:creator: Pouya Asadi et al.
item.description:
Asadi et al. build a strongly-coupled dark-baryon model where a transition magnetic dipole operator (g_M≃-2√(3), roughly twice the neutron moment) drives inelastic scattering while an accidental “ℋ-parity” forbids all diagonal one-photon moments, suppressing elastic scattering. In the benchmark N_c=N_f=3 theory with dark quarks in an SU(2)_L triplet, the neutral 3-plet/5-plet baryons carry opposite ℋ-parity; hyperfine and W-exchange contributions to their splitting produce δ∼𝒪(100) keV near dark-quark mass ∼800 GeV (m_χ∼2.4 TeV). Fitting the LZ event (spin-dependent nuclear response) gives best-fit (m_χ,δ)=(6.8 TeV,300 keV) for SHM and (14 TeV,280 keV) for a MW+LMC profile, with viable ranges 1–50 TeV and 100–500 keV.

The distinctive handle: the excited state de-excites via a photon of energy δ, with decay length ∼4.7 m — comparable to detector size — so a fraction of recoils carry a coincident 100–500 keV photon, offering directional information (the excited state travels with the heavy DM), a discriminant no other iDM reading provides. It also predicts weaker solar-capture constraints (spin-dependent capture on rare odd-mass isotopes; annihilation dominantly to dark mesons rather than neutrinos), evading the bounds killing the thermal Higgsino. Caveats: mass-splitting predictions carry 𝒪(10⁷⁾ dynamic-range uncertainty from the variational quark-model estimate (only lattice could sharpen them), the single-event fit neglects backgrounds, and halo-profile choice dominates the preferred region.

item.title: The Colors of Jet Quenching
item.dc:creator: Hannah Bossi et al.
item.description:
Bossi, Larose, and Mehtar-Tani perform a data-driven extraction of quark and gluon quenching factors by jointly fitting ATLAS inclusive-jet R_AA and CMS energy-energy correlators (EECs) for R=0.4 jets, restricted to the small-angle region (R_L<0.07) where hard-collinear dynamics dominate and soft medium response is subleading. The two observables have complementary flavor sensitivity — gluon EECs peak at R_L=0.025 versus 0.012 for quarks — breaking the identifiability problem that plagues R_AA-only extractions. Under the coherent-energy-loss null hypothesis they extract S_q≃0.8, S_g≃0.3, incompatible with Casimir scaling (S_g=S_q⁹/4≃0.54–0.58) at 8–11σ. Adding color decoherence via the antenna/dipole quenching factor S_dip(θ) — which interpolates from coherent (θ≪θ_c) to independent loss with a slow θ⁻²/3 power-law tail — improves the fit (χ²/dof 0.93→0.13) and restores Casimir scaling (S_q≃0.65, S_g≃0.40, within 1.5σ). The medium resolution angle is tightly constrained: θ_c=0.057±0.005 (fit)⁺⁰.014_-0.008 (syst), p_T-independent as expected.

Why it matters: this is direct evidence, drawn from data rather than tuned Monte Carlo, that the QGP partially resolves internal jet substructure down to θ_c≃0.05–0.07 — the color-decoherence transition made quantitative, paired with Mehtar-Tani’s companion generating-functional derivation. Caveats are stated plainly: absolute χ² values are not meaningful because published uncertainties are added in quadrature without correlations, so only relative fit quality is claimed; it is a proof-of-concept, not a global analysis, with vacuum reference and flavor fractions held fixed and higher-order/medium-response effects deferred.

item.title: Spin-dependent azimuthal asymmetry of coherent J/ψ photoproduction in hadronic PbPb collisions
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
What they did: CMS measured the azimuthal distribution of decay muons from coherently photoproduced J/ψ (reconstructed at p_T<0.2 GeV, 1.6<|y|<2.4) relative to the second-order event plane Ψ_2 in 50–80% central PbPb collisions at 5.36 TeV, using 1.26 nb⁻¹. The cos(2Δϕ) modulation amplitude is A_2=-0.194±0.022 (stat)±0.018 (syst) — negative, and different from zero by more than 5σ, the first such observation for spin-1/2 muons. A_2 shows no significant dependence on rapidity or centrality (7–18% dominant systematic from signal extraction; 3–9% hadronic/incoherent contamination subtracted via a high-p_T fit extrapolation).

Why it matters: Combined with the positive modulation previously seen for spin-0 pions from ρ⁰ decays, this establishes spin-state dependence of azimuthal asymmetries in coherently photoproduced vector-meson decays — direct confirmation that the J/ψ inherits the incident photon’s linear polarization. Crucially, using Ψ_2 rather than the meson-p_T interference proxy makes the polarization handle work across broad rapidity and different collision systems, opening a novel reaction-plane estimator that is less sensitive to nonflow and fluctuations, potentially valuable for small systems like pA. Caveat: the Wu et al. model describes the data well, but the saturation-based Shao et al. calculation overshoots the amplitude by roughly a factor of two, so the theory picture is not settled.

item.title: Exothermic and Endothermic Inelastic Dark Matter Interpretations at LZ
item.dc:creator: James B. Dent et al.
item.description:
What they did: Dent and Newstead reinterpret LZ’s single ~248 keV nuclear-recoil event (LZ230616, background 0.0106±0.0008) as exothermic inelastic DM, where the ambient heavier state χ^ down-scatters and dumps its splitting |δ| as recoil, producing a peak at E_0=μ_χN|δ|/m_N. An unbinned shape likelihood fixes the peak to the event energy with σ_p f_≃(0.5–3)×10⁻⁴⁵ cm². The empty high-energy sideband (350–680 keV, zero events) disfavors broad heavy-mass peaks — expected sideband yields per observed event are 0.02 (10 GeV), 19 (42 GeV), 73 (100 GeV) — bounding m_χ≲90 GeV at 95% CL. Excited-state stability then splits solutions into a ~40–90 GeV state with sub-MeV splitting and dark-photon mediator, or a sub-40 GeV state with ~1–10 MeV splitting requiring a leptophobic mediator (to close χ^*→χe⁺e⁻).

Why it matters: Exothermic scattering peaks above the elastic endpoint and is largely halo-tail-independent, sidestepping precisely the high-velocity-tail fragility that undermined the endothermic higgsino readings last week. It predicts ≃4.5 events in LZ’s projected 1000-day (~13 tonne-yr) run, and existing XENONnT/PandaX-4T exposures (1.1 and 0.5 expected events) could already test it in extended windows; the μ_χN/m_N peak scaling gives a distinct argon/germanium signature. Caveat: the sideband recast relies on unpublished efficiency/energy-scale extrapolations beyond calibration, and the Helm form factor gives an 𝒪(10⁻⁴⁾ suppression with large uncertainty at this q — the authors stress this is no substitute for a collaboration analysis.

item.title: Flavor Tomography of Long-Lived Neutrino-Mass Mediators
item.dc:creator: Renjie Wang
item.description:
What they did: Wang shows that if the long-lived charged particle producing displaced-lepton signals at the HL-LHC is also the mediator generating Majorana neutrino masses (the “shared-coupling condition”), the Casas–Ibarra parametrization fixes the displaced-lepton flavor ratio N_e/N_μ=∑_i|U_ei|² m_i/∑_i|U_μi|² m_i entirely in terms of PMNS data. At NuFit 6.1 best-fit with m_lightest=0: N_e/N_μ=0.140 (normal) vs 2.11 (inverted), a discrimination ratio ℛ=15.1. The prediction holds identically across Scotogenic, Type-III seesaw, inverse/linear seesaw, and lepton-portal DM models (given quasi-degenerate mediators and near-real R). Detector efficiencies cancel in the ratio; δ_CP dependence is <3%. An exact Poisson test gives 3σ ordering discrimination with 𝒪(25) timing-tagged (Δt>200 ps) displaced leptons; Scotogenic yields for M_LLP=300–600 GeV are N_disp≈64–2856.

Why it matters: This is a δ_CP-free collider handle on the mass ordering, structurally immune to the degeneracy that limits T2K/NOvA and complementary to JUNO — because the observable depends on |U_αi|², not U_αi. It sharpens exactly where prior two-HNL flavor-counting proposals (capped at ≲90% classification) are broad. It extends the week’s detector-repurposing theme, exploiting the CMS MTD / ATLAS HGTD timing layers already under construction. Caveats: requires the shared-coupling class (real R, degenerate mediators); complex-R and non-degenerate corrections reach 𝒪(10–30%); the worst-case 3σ scan gives ℛ=8.85, dropping to ℛ≥2.2 for larger m_lightest within the Planck-allowed range; and it presupposes a positive LLP discovery plus Majorana neutrinos.

item.title: Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with the High-Energy Sideband
item.dc:creator: Nicholas L. Rodd et al.
item.description: Abstract only. The empty region above the 248 keV event is the discriminant. A thermal 1.1 TeV higgsino tuned to the observed rate and spectrum — splitting δ ~ 370–490 keV depending on the halo model — would, Rodd et al. argue, generically populate a higher-energy sideband along LZ’s S1c axis with additional recoils. LZ reports zero events there, so the higgsino reading sits in mild tension with its own data. The caveat is explicit: the acceptance in that bin is not public, so the tension cannot be quantified without the collaboration’s input — precisely what the authors ask for. They note a non-thermal ~500 GeV higgsino can evade the sideband, and that heavier-target experiments could test the interpretation either way. This is the sideband complement to yesterday’s solar-capture bound: another empty region pushing the same direction, giving LZ a concrete internal cross-check rather than an external astrophysical one.

item.title: Seasonal dark matter from the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy event
item.dc:creator: Christopher McCabe
item.description: The high recoil energy forces the inelastic splitting against the kinematic ceiling set by the halo escape speed, and McCabe turns that into a sharp seasonal signature. A shape-only profile likelihood in the (m_χ, δ) plane confines δ to ~370–400 keV at 1σ for m_χ = 1 TeV, with small splittings disfavored because they place the spectrum below 248 keV. At δ = 350 keV the required v_min = 766 km/s sits just 44 km/s below the maximum lab-frame speed (810 km/s), so the entire signal comes from a thin sliver of the halo tail. The consequence: annual modulation amplitude A = 94% at (1 TeV, 350 keV), rising to 100% at 500 GeV — the rate literally vanishes for up to two-thirds of the year. The modulation is nearly pure timing information (97.2% of discriminating power is arrival-time, not energy correlation) and carries mass information even where spectra are degenerate. Reach: 11 events give 3σ on modulation, 31 give 5σ; XLZD at 200 t·yr reaches 7.5σ, and LZ’s own ~15 t·yr already hits 3σ for δ > 374 keV. A secondary handle is isotopic — ¹³⁶Xe supplies 47% of the rate at δ = 380 keV versus 8.9% natural abundance — though enrichment at scale is unrealistic. Honest caveat, stated twice: everything rests on the Standard Halo Model, precisely in the tail region where it is least trustworthy.

item.title: Inelastic Signatures of Electroweak Dark Matter
item.dc:creator: Juri Smirnov et al.
item.description: Smirnov, Griffith, and Beacom show that Higgs-coupled minimal dark matter — a Majorana plus adjacent Dirac multiplet at the custodial point — reproduces the LZ event through a mechanism that is universal across the whole 3_M2_D through 13_M12_D sequence. The neutral Higgs Clebsch is exactly 1/√2 independent of representation, so both the pseudo-Dirac splitting δ ≃ y²v²/4m_χ and the off-diagonal Z coupling (σ_n^inel ≃ 1.9×10⁻³⁹ cm²) are fixed by (m_χ, y) alone. Requiring one expected inelastic event in LZ’s 2.84 t·yr defines a rate-selected δ_LZ(m_χ) ~ 350–380 keV and a universal band in (m_χ, y); intersecting it with each multiplet’s thermal relic trajectory selects a benchmark, from 3_M2_D at 1.44 TeV to 13_M12_D at 131 TeV. The payoff is a correlated, representation-dependent loop-induced elastic signal — from 1.3×10⁻⁴⁷ cm² up to 5×10⁻⁴⁵ cm² — that must lie above the neutrino floor. Existing null elastic results already disfavor 11_M10_D and 13_M12_D, leaving 3_M2_D, 5_M4_D, 7_M6_D as the preferred survivors, all testable by next-generation searches. Caveats are candidly flagged: the rate estimate uses no full detector-response/likelihood reconstruction; the relic calculation is done in the unbroken phase while the signal depends on sub-MeV broken-phase splittings (argued negligible but unchecked); and it remains a single-event excess. The distinctive value is predictivity — inelastic rate, splitting, and elastic channel are locked together rather than fit independently.

item.title: Search for dark matter particle interactions in an extended nuclear recoil energy window with LZ
item.dc:creator: D. S. Akerib et al.
item.description:
The now-official source of the week’s theory storm: in a 2.84 tonne-year exposure (220 live days, 4.71 t fiducial), LZ extended its nuclear-recoil window to ~270 keV to probe NREFT and inelastic WIMP models whose spectra populate higher recoils. After selections and salt removal, one event survives in the NR band, consistent with a 248±23(stat)±23(sys) keV elastic recoil (S1_c=540.1 phd, S2_c=9268 phd), sitting 1.5σ below the NR median and 6.7σ below the ER median. A profile-likelihood scan over 293 distinguishable models finds a maximum local significance of 3.4σ (typically for masses >200 GeV/c²) and a global 2.6σ after look-elsewhere correction. The upper limits are world-leading on all models; the lower limits lift off zero because of the event. Compatible interpretations include inelastic 𝒪_1^s (Higgsino-like) with ~300–360 keV splitting and the magnetic-moment ℒ_10^s.

Why it matters: this fixes the kinematics the interpretation papers have been chasing — mass and splitting are tightly constrained, which is exactly why Pospelov et al.’s solar bound can bite. Honest caveats abound in the text: the salt (bias-mitigation) injection failed to cover the high-energy signal region, so this is explicitly a non-blind analysis above 55 keV; the dominant local backgrounds (accidentals, atmospheric-ν CEνNS, MSSI) each carry a 100% MSSI rate uncertainty and rely on absence of a larger low-energy population; and no background could be positively identified as the culprit. One event at 2.6σ remains one event.

item.title: Strong Constraints on Higgsino Dark Matter from Solar Capture
item.dc:creator: Maxim Pospelov et al.
item.description:
Pospelov and Ramani turn the Sun into an inelastic-DM accelerator. Infalling quasi-Dirac Higgsinos (m_χ≃1.08 TeV, the thermal-relic mass) reach ~1400 km/s in the solar core — far above the terrestrial ceiling — enabling endothermic Z-exchange up-scattering off heavy elements (iron through uranium) and capture. Captured DM annihilates to W⁺W⁻, and IceCube’s 10-year non-observation of solar neutrinos caps the annihilation rate at Γ_ann^lim=1.5×10¹⁹ s⁻¹. Tree-level Z exchange alone, with up-scattering stalling near 0.2R_⊙ on uranium, already excludes δ≲506 keV; including the robustly predicted loop-level spin-dependent elastic channel on hydrogen thermalizes the captured population and strengthens the bound to δ>566 keV, moving only ~60 keV across decades of loop cross-section.

Why it matters: the LZ event requires δ≃340–360 keV, where the annihilation rate would exceed the IceCube limit by O(10³⁾. This flatly excludes the endothermic-higgsino reading that yesterday’s cluster (Fan–Reece, Freese, Su et al.) converged on — the exact counter-pressure the digest flagged. The authors note a factor-4 correction to the tree-level cross-section that has propagated (wrongly, for a vector-like Higgsino) in the literature. Caveat: the escape hatch is explicit — dark-photon-mediated inelastic models with sub-GeV A’ produce no prompt solar neutrinos and evade the bound entirely, so the LZ event survives, just not as a Higgsino.

item.title: Stringent limits on CPT- and Lorentz-invariance violation from B_s⁰ decays
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
LHCb exploits the interference between B_s⁰–B̅s⁰ mixing and flavor-specific B_s⁰→D_s⁻π⁺ decay in the full Run 2 dataset (6 fb⁻¹, 13 TeV, 378,500 signal candidates, ~84% purity) to search for CPT violation. The large ΔΓ_s gives access to ℛe(z) — complementary to B⁰ systems, which are sensitive mainly to ℐm(z) — while the ~20× mean boost of B_s⁰ mesons in the forward acceptance amplifies any sidereal Lorentz-violating modulation. Results: ℛe(z)=0.018±0.016±0.003 and ℐm(z)=0.003±0.004±0.002, both consistent with CPT symmetry and the most precise in the B_s⁰ system. Within the SME, the Lorentz-violating four-vector reaches Δa∥=(+0.62±0.71±0.32)×10⁻¹⁴ GeV, with Δa_X,Δa_Y at the same 10⁻¹⁴ GeV level.

Why it matters: a quiet precision milestone superseding the earlier J/ψϕ (3 fb⁻¹) and D0 constraints, probing quark-content dependence of CPT/Lorentz coefficients through the bs̅ system. A binned sidereal-phase cross-check gives a 1.8σ preference for oscillation over the constant hypothesis — compatible with a statistical fluctuation, so no evidence for Lorentz violation. Systematics (dominated by fixed Γ_s, ΔΓ_s, and decay-time acceptance) are subdominant to the statistical uncertainties throughout.

item.title: Constraint on the Higgs boson width in the diphoton final state using signal-background interference in proton-proton collisions at √(s) = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS turns the interference between gg→H→γγ and the continuum gg→γγ amplitude into a width measurement, using 138 fb⁻¹ from 2016–2018. The interference distorts the m_γγ lineshape and shifts its peak by an amount that grows with Γ_H, so fitting that shift across categories binned in diphoton p_T and BDT output constrains the width without ever leaving the on-shell region. The result is Γ_H<92 MeV observed (138 expected) at 95% CL, against a SM prediction of 4.1 MeV and a previous best direct limit of 330 MeV.

Why it matters: the tightest existing number, Γ_H=3.0⁺².0_-1.5 MeV, comes from comparing on-shell and off-shell H→VV rates — which assumes the couplings governing the two regimes are the same, exactly the assumption new physics would break. On-shell rates alone cannot do better on their own, because a width inflated by a factor α through undetectable decays is degenerate with rescaling every Higgs coupling by 1/α¹/4. Interference breaks that flat direction using on-shell data only, so the weaker limit is doing more model-independent work than the raw number suggests. Caveats: sensitivity still sits more than an order of magnitude above the SM value, and the dominant experimental systematics are photon energy scale and resolution — which can mimic the very peak shift being measured.

item.title: Higgsino Above the Sea of Fog
item.dc:creator: JiJi Fan et al.
item.description:
Fan et al. read LZ’s single 248±23(stat)±23(sys) keV event as inelastic higgsino scattering. Ordinary spin-independent elastic scattering cannot produce it: an event at 250 keV would have been preceded by thousands at lower recoil energy. Scattering between two nearly degenerate neutral states changes the kinematics, and the required minimum velocity — v_min≈[350√(E_R/250 keV) (m_χ+m_N)/m_χ+ 425√(250 keV/E_R) (δ/350 keV)] km/s — puts the scatterer squarely in the high-speed tail of the local halo. A 1.1 TeV thermal higgsino with δ≈350 keV works: under the Standard Halo Model the recoil spectrum starts near 170 keV, peaks around 200 keV, and integrates to 0.3 events in the 215–270 keV signal window.

The theoretical payoff is that the splitting is not a free parameter — it is induced by higgsino–gaugino mixing, so δ≈350 keV pushes binos and winos to 10³–10⁴ TeV, and avoiding large logarithmic corrections to the higgsino mass drags the heavy Higgs doublet to the same scale: a heavy but unsplit spectrum, apart from the light higgsino. The caveats are the authors’ own and substantial. The high-velocity tail is highly uncertain; under an LMC-influenced halo with a fatter tail, δ must instead exceed 350 keV. They also note the annual modulation peaks near June 2 and the event landed on June 16, 2023 — suggestive, but this is one event.

item.title: Fermionic Dark Matter Absorption and the High-Energy Event in LUX-ZEPLIN
item.dc:creator: Yuanchao Lou et al.
item.description:
The same event by a different mechanism, and then a self-inflicted null. Lou et al. propose neutral-current absorption of a fermionic dark matter particle on a xenon nucleus: for m_χ≃247 MeV the coherent process deposits a monoenergetic 248 keV nuclear recoil, matching LZ with no appeal to the velocity tail. But the momentum transfer, q≃m_χ∼p_F^Xe≃262 MeV, resolves individual nucleons, so an incoherent single-nucleon knockout channel with a broad 200 keV–100.2 MeV spectrum comes along unavoidably. That correlated coherent–incoherent pair is the model’s distinctive signature, and the primary knockouts are argued to fail standard LZ selection cuts, keeping the low-energy spectrum clean. One effective coupling at Λ≃11.5 TeV, σ_χN^NC≃1.07×10⁻⁴⁶ cm², accounts for the single event.

Then they go looking where the incoherent channel would show. Recasting KamLAND’s neutron-emission channel χ+¹²C→ν+n+¹¹C^* at m_χ=247.5 MeV yields 90% CL bounds of Λ_90^V≃80 TeV and Λ_90^S≃73 TeV — both far above the 11.5 TeV the LZ interpretation requires, excluding the benchmark for vector and scalar operators alike. The authors call these bounds preliminary and valid “within the present signal and detector response treatment,” but the gap is wide. Worth reading precisely because it builds the case and then dismantles it, and because it shows large-volume scintillators now constrain xenon-anomaly interpretations.

item.title: First Measurement of Solar Neutrinos through Elastic Neutrino-Electron Scattering at the keV Scale
item.dc:creator: XENON Collaboration et al.
item.description:
XENONnT reports the first detection of low-energy solar neutrinos via elastic neutrino–electron scattering in a dark-matter TPC, using 2.46 t·y from the SR0 and SR1b science runs over a recoil-energy ROI of [1, 140] keV. An unbinned extended-likelihood fit rejects the background-only hypothesis at 5.0σ and yields a solar pp flux of (10.2±2.0)×10¹⁰ cm⁻²s⁻¹, with the 1 keV electron-recoil threshold translating to sensitivity down to 17 keV neutrino energy — the lowest neutrino detection threshold on record. Roughly 89% of the ROI signal is pp, ~10% ⁷Be, the rest sub-percent. Discovery power comes mainly from [1, 60] keV. The enabling advance is radon reduction: dedicated distillation cut ²²²Rn to ~0.9 µBq/kg, comparable to the neutrino rate, with the ²¹⁴Pb/²²²Rn activity ratio (0.66±0.03) fixed by a ²²²Rn calibration.

Why it matters: it cements liquid-xenon TPCs — built for WIMPs — as genuine keV-scale neutrino detectors, complementing the recent ⁸B CEνNS observations and pointing toward XLZD sub-percent pp measurements for electroweak and solar-metallicity tests. Caveats are honest and several: the flux sits 1.9σ above Borexino; the fit relies on the FEA-stepping signal model (the more complete RRPA is only available below 32 keV); an unexplained “tritium-like” excess overlaps the highest-S/B region below 20 keV and is left free; and adding ¹⁴C at its maximal conceivable level drops significance to 4.3σ (Borexino consistency to 1.2σ). Total uncertainty is 20%, split evenly between systematic and profile-likelihood.

item.title: Evidence for the dead-cone effect in bottom quark initiated jets in pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS finds evidence for the dead-cone effect — mass suppression of collinear gluon radiation within ΔR_dead=m_q/E_q — in b-jets from dileptonic tt̅ events, using 59.8 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV. The emission density ρ(ΔR) is measured via iterative Cambridge–Aachen declustering onto the Lund jet plane, in two jet-p_T bins (40–80, 80–200 GeV). Two novelties sharpen the measurement: a tag-and-probe selection of b-jets from tt̅ that avoids flavor-tagging substructure biases (91% b-quark purity, agreeing with generator-level selection to 2% versus 3–10% for direct DeepJet tagging), and a transformer encoder that partially reconstructs charged b-hadron decay products (95.6% signal efficiency) to restore the angle-ordered emission history. Compared to a HERWIG7 sample with the b-mass set to zero in the showering kernel, the data disfavor the massless model at 4.3σ (p=8×10⁻⁶) in the 40–80 GeV bin, while the nominal massive shower fits well (p=0.57).

Why it matters: this is a direct imprint of quark mass on the parton shower in b-jets — following ALICE’s D⁰-tagged first observation and CMS/LHCb charm and beauty measurements — and provides a clean benchmark for logarithmically-accurate shower development and analytic Lund b-plane calculations. It dovetails with the recent heavy-quark energy-correlator work. Caveats: significance is confined to the lower-p_T bin; at 80–200 GeV the narrower dead cone leaves no significant discrimination (nominal p=0.03, massless p=0.01). The massless-kernel comparison also shows hadronization plays a sizable role in the collinear suppression, so the effect is not purely perturbative.

item.title: The inclusive B̅ →X_sγ decay rate with higher precision
item.dc:creator: M. Misiak et al.
item.description:
Misiak et al. deliver an upgraded SM prediction ℬ_sγ^SM=(3.54±0.14)×10⁻⁴ for E_γ>1.6 GeV, a ~4% total uncertainty. The headline improvement is retiring the long-standing m_c-interpolation: the dominant 𝒪(α_s²⁾ interference terms Ĝ_17⁽²⁾, Ĝ_27⁽²⁾ are now computed with exact charm-mass dependence via four-loop cut diagrams (companion paper arXiv:2608.29864), enhancing ℬ_sγ by 4.2% relative to the interpolated value — exceeding the previously assigned ±3% interpolation error by 1.4×. The 𝒪(α_s) rate is also rendered formally complete by adding four- and five-body (s̅ b)(q̅ q) contributions (~−0.2%), and HQE matrix elements, m_b and |V_cb| are taken from the latest kinetic-scheme semileptonic fit including 𝒪(α_s³⁾. Including 𝒪(α_s²⁾ cuts the μ_b-scale variation to ±1.3% over [1.5, 10] GeV.

Why it matters: the prediction sits in perfect agreement with the experimental average (3.49±0.19)×10⁻⁴, and translates into an absolute (any-tanβ) 2HDM-II charged-Higgs bound M_H^±>670 GeV at 95% C.L. — stronger than comparable LHC direct searches. A convenient linear formula ℬ_sγ×10⁴⁼⁽³.54±0.14)-8.51 ΔC_7-2.16 ΔC_8 is provided for generic BSM fits. Against the persistent R(D^*) tension, the inclusive-radiative sector is now fully SM-consistent. Caveat, flagged by the authors: the exact-m_c Ĝ_17,27⁽²⁾ still omit the photon-energy cut (expected minor, given endpoint-peaked spectra), and PDG’s E_0 extrapolation factors from experimental cuts down to 1.6 GeV await updating, ideally via SIMBA.

item.title: Search for scalar leptoquarks produced via muon-quark scattering in pp collisions at √s = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
The first LHC search exploiting the proton’s charged-lepton content to produce a single TeV-scale scalar leptoquark resonantly through muon–quark fusion, using the full Run 2 dataset (138 fb⁻¹). The lepton comes from a photon fluctuation inside one proton (LUXlep PDFs), fusing with a quark from the other; the signature is a high-pₜ muon plus a light- or b-quark jet, with a soft second muon often lost down the beampipe. The observable is the μ-jet invariant mass, fit for a bump on a smooth background across eight categories (one/two muon × BDT tight/loose × b-tag). Data agree with background; 95% CL limits on σ·B exclude new territory in the (M_LQ, λ) plane: 1.5–3.6 TeV at couplings 0.2–0.6 for LQ(uμ), and M_LQ > 1.8 TeV at λ > 1 for LQ(bμ).

Why it matters: unlike pair production (QCD-driven, nearly λ-independent, giving a vertical exclusion) or nonresonant t-channel, this resonant mode scales as λ² and gains reach precisely where pair production dies from phase space — large λ and high mass. It’s a genuinely new handle motivated by the (now-fading) B-meson flavor anomalies, and complements existing modes rather than merely tightening them. Caveat: limits assume only lepton-induced production, neglecting gluon-induced single production; the authors flag this as conservative (weakening limits by ~10–15%) and verify via injection tests that the bias stays below half a standard deviation. The dominant systematic is the freely-floating background fit, i.e. statistics.

item.title: Observation of the Ξ_c⁰ → pK⁻ decay and measurement of its decay asymmetry
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
First observation of the singly Cabibbo-suppressed, purely W-exchange decay Ξ_c⁰ → pK⁻, reconstructed through the clean cascade Ξ_b⁻ → Ξ_c⁰(→pK⁻)π⁻ in 5.4 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV pp data. A signal yield of 134±14 is extracted from a simultaneous fit with the normalization channel Ξ_c⁰ → pK⁻K⁻π⁺ (6930±90 events), giving a relative rate R = (9.26±0.94±0.43)×10⁻³ and, using the known normalization branching fraction, B(Ξ_c⁰ → pK⁻) = (4.5±0.5±0.2±0.9)×10⁻⁵. Exploiting the cascade, an angular fit of the Ξ_c⁰ helicity angle (assuming α_{Ξ_b} = −1, validated by the analogous Λ_b measurement) yields the decay asymmetry α = 0.32±0.15±0.01, compatible with zero.

Why it matters: pure W-exchange charm-baryon decays are notoriously beyond reliable computation, and BESIII’s recent Λ_c⁺ → Ξ⁰K⁺ analysis already showed deviations from theory. This measurement supplies both a branching fraction and an asymmetry for a channel never before seen. The measured B sits significantly below most predictions (IRA/TDA ≈ 3.1×10⁻⁴, i.e. the observed value is far lower once the normalization uncertainty is accounted for), and the asymmetry sharply discriminates models — consistent with IRA/TDA/SU(3) predictions near zero but excluding current-algebra (α = 0.99) and one IRA (−0.81) result. The asymmetry consistent with zero indicates negligible S–P interference. Caveats: the dominant uncertainty is the 20% normalization branching fraction; the α measurement is statistics-limited and assumes unpolarized Ξ_b⁻ (a 5% polarization systematic is assigned). CP-violation sensitivity awaits the upgraded-LHCb dataset.

item.title: Imperfect axions with no domain wall problem
item.dc:creator: Marco Gorghetto et al.
item.description:
A new resolution of the domain-wall problem for post-inflationary axions with domain-wall number N > 1. The standard cure — a small PQ-violating operator that biases the N degenerate QCD minima — is tightly squeezed between the nEDM bound (θ_eff ≲ 10⁻¹⁰) and dark-matter overproduction from late wall decay. The authors point out that because the QCD axion mass is strongly temperature-suppressed (m_a²(T) ∝ T⁻⁸), a temperature-independent PQ-violating potential can dominate before the QCD potential switches on at T⋆. In that regime the PQ term (which has trivial wall number) forms unstable walls at H = m_PQ that destroy the string network before the stable N > 1 QCD walls ever form. Analytics plus N = 2 lattice simulations (3072³, “fat-string” system) confirm the network decays for m_PQ/m_a(T⋆) ≳ 0.32; accounting for the logarithmic string-tension enhancement extrapolated to the physical log ≈ 60 raises this critical value to ≈ 1.8.

Why it matters: this opens viable N > 1 post-inflationary parameter space (including DFSZ-motivated N = 6) requiring f_a ≲ (2/N)·5×10⁹ GeV, i.e. m_a ≳ (N/2) meV, in the 10⁻³–10⁻² eV window. Crucially, the needed PQ violation predicts an nEDM within two orders of magnitude of current limits — squarely in reach of the planned factor-100 improvement, tying the domain-wall solution to a testable signal. Caveats the authors stress: simulations reach only log ≈ 4.5–6 versus the physical ~60, forcing extrapolation of c_PQ; and the large relativistic-axion energy density radiated during scaling may obstruct wall formation entirely (App. C), which would shrink the early-decay region below the purple-dashed line. Dedicated simulations near the physical point are needed.

item.title: Deuterium Production in an Effective Field Theory Constructed from On-Shell Amplitudes
item.dc:creator: Tim M. P. Tait
item.description:
Tait computes n+p→dγ in a pionless EFT whose degrees of freedom are the nuclear states themselves: the amplitude is glued from on-shell three-point vertices (the d–n–p vertex normalized to the measured ANC A_S=0.8846 fm⁻¹/2), with S_0¹ rescattering resummed dispersively, leaving just two short-distance constants — an isovector magnetic (c_M1) and an electric dipole (c_E1) contact. A joint Bayesian fit to two thermal-capture measurements and the 22-point SLEGS photodisintegration set returns c_M1=+0.162±0.015 and c_E1=-0.88±0.21, both of natural size, with a comfortable fit (χ²⁼²⁰.3 for 22 dof). The thermonuclear rate is pinned to 0.22–0.24% across T_9=0.01–3, rising to 0.25–0.27% once truncation (bounded at 0.12%) is folded in. Propagated through PRyMordial, this shifts predicted primordial D/H by -0.06% and cuts this reaction’s D/H uncertainty contribution from 0.089% to 0.050% — effectively retiring np→dγ from the error budget, where the d+d burning reactions now dominate.

Why it matters: it delivers the sub-0.3% production anchor needed to keep pace with improving burning-rate data, and demonstrates the on-shell-amplitude program (previously applied to d(p,γ)³He) generalizes to a second capture, with the shared d–n–p vertex promising correlated control over all four primary reactions. Honest caveats: the fitted electric contact pulls 3.5σ against Rupak’s pre-2000 determination (L_E1=+14.9 vs -5.3 fm³), which Tait attributes to a genuine data–data tension between the near-threshold older set and SLEGS’s higher reach rather than a calculational disagreement. The two thermal measurements themselves differ by 1.9σ, requiring PDG error scaling. Notably, the paper states all analytic and numerical work was primarily derived using LLMs (Claude, GPT-5.6), human-validated.

item.title: Search for high-mass resonances in photon-jet final states using 140 fb⁻¹ at √s = 13 TeV with ATLAS
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
ATLAS scans the γ–jet invariant-mass spectrum over the full Run 2 dataset for localized excesses, finding none: BumpHunter yields no significant deviation across four regions (inclusive SR plus flavor-tagged SRL/SRC/SRB, the latter using the GN2 transformer tagger). The key advance over the 36.7 fb⁻¹ predecessor is heavy-flavor tagging of the leading jet, enabling separate excited-quark interpretations. For coupling f=1, masses are excluded up to 6.0 TeV (q_L^), 3.5 TeV (c^, via a simultaneous SRC+SRB+SRL fit), and 2.6 TeV (b^) — the c^ result being the first direct constraint in this channel at the LHC. Quantum-black-hole thresholds are excluded to 5.3 TeV (Randall-Sundrum, n=1) and 7.5 TeV (ADD, n=6). Model-independent Gaussian-resonance limits are provided for widths 2%/7%/15%.

Why it matters: it is today’s one full-dataset collaboration result, extending compositeness and extra-dimension reach and closing the c^* gap in γ–jet. Backgrounds are modeled analytically with smoothly-falling functions, validated via spurious-signal tests (bias required <50% of statistical uncertainty). Caveat: the ADD QBH exclusion (7.5 TeV) is actually slightly weaker than the previous 7.1 TeV in absolute terms only if misread — here it improves — but note downward data fluctuations at high mass, and minor ∼2σ local excesses near 1.8 and 2.6 TeV that stay within the expected-limit band. No theoretical uncertainties are assigned to the QBH benchmarks, following prior convention.

item.title: Efficient binned profile likelihood minimization for precision measurements with RABBIT
item.dc:creator: David Walter et al.
item.description:
Walter and Long present RABBIT, a TensorFlow-2 framework for binned profile-likelihood fits that uses automatic differentiation for exact gradients and Hessian-vector products, feeding a Krylov-subspace trust-region minimizer that solves the trust-region subproblem from HVPs rather than full Hessians. JIT compilation gives near-C++ speed with automatic CPU/GPU dispatch. The statistical model supports Poisson or χ² observation terms, log-normal or additive systematics, and Barlow–Beeston (full or lite) statistical uncertainties profiled analytically where possible; when all systematics are symmetrized and additive with a χ² model, the likelihood is purely quadratic and the MLE follows deterministically in one step. Physical observables (including unfolded cross sections) are obtained via differentiable “mappings” and “masked channels” with full post-fit uncertainty propagation.

Why it matters: this is the tooling-wave companion the digest flags — precision measurements already hit 3000+ bins and 4000+ nuisance parameters (CMS W-mass), and HL-LHC will push further. Benchmarks on synthetic models show decisive scaling advantages: at 1000 bins / 1024 systematics RABBIT finishes under 10 s where Combine and pyhf exceed the 10-minute limit, and at 100,000 bins only RABBIT succeeds. It was validated against Combine (NLL values and scans agree exactly up to constants) and already used in the CMS W-mass result. Honest caveats: GPU runs are memory-limited (largest fit had 2048 systematics on a V100); the tool complements rather than replaces established frameworks, and for simple models Combine remains fastest.

item.title: Measurement of tZq inclusive and differential cross-sections in pp collisions at √(s)=13 TeV with ATLAS
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
Abstract only. Working in the trilepton channel with the full 140 fb⁻¹ Run 2 dataset (three light leptons, 2–4 jets, 1–2 b-tags), ATLAS measures the pp→tℓ⁺ℓ⁻q cross-section for m_ℓℓ>30 GeV — including resonant and non-resonant dilepton production — as 95.2 ⁺⁸.5_-7.9(stat.) ⁺⁵.5_-5.3(syst.) fb, consistent with the most advanced SM predictions. Separate top-quark and top-antiquark cross-sections and their ratio are extracted, and absolute and normalised differential spectra are unfolded at both particle and parton level across many kinematic variables. The top-quark spin asymmetry, from the unfolded polarisation angle, is A=0.34±0.14(stat.)±0.06(syst.), again SM-consistent. The differential results are interpreted in SMEFT, setting limits on dimension-6 operators involving the top quark.

Why it matters: This is the day’s one full-dataset collaboration result and extends the “EFT-as-default” reading of top-sector data — every observable is SM-consistent, so the payoff is the constraint on anomalous top couplings via the spin asymmetry and differential shapes rather than any deviation. The caveat is inherent: with everything SM-compatible the sensitivity is entirely in the operator limits, and the polarisation measurement remains statistics-limited (statistical uncertainty on A more than double the systematic).

item.title: Impact of model-independent higher-order contributions to the Higgs-boson self-couplings
item.dc:creator: Johannes Braathen et al.
item.description:
Braathen, Naskar and Weiglein identify a closed, model-independent class of higher-order contributions to λ_hhh and λ_hhhh: SM-like diagrams containing only the observed Higgs h in the loop but with vertices dressed by loop-corrected coupling modifiers κ̅_λ, κ̅_4. Using an effective-potential setup inspired by leading-order HEFT, they compute these up to two loops in an on-shell tadpole/mass scheme (cross-checked against a FeynArts/FormCalc one-loop diagrammatic calculation), yielding analytic κ_λ(κ̅_λ,κ̅_4) and κ_4(κ̅_λ,κ̅_4). Confronting these with the current experimental κ_λ∈[-0.71,6.1], perturbative unitarity, and κ_4 bounds turns the one-dimensional interval into a non-trivial two-dimensional allowed region. For κ̅_4=1 the inferred upper bound tightens from the experimental 6.1 to κ̅_λ<4.9; blind directions open up at large positive κ̅_4 (reaching κ̅_λ≳8 before unitarity caps it near 7). A public code, check_kappas, implements the mapping.

Why it matters: This is a genuine correction to how self-coupling limits should be translated into BSM parameter space, continuing the 08-19 self-coupling thread. The effect is largest precisely where current bounds sit — far from the SM — and would shrink if future measurements land near κ_λ≃1. Honest caveats: the results carry residual MS renormalisation-scale dependence (bounds shift noticeably between Q=m_h and Q=v, especially at large |κ̅_4|), and the extracted κ̅’s are themselves scale-dependent quantities requiring careful matching to a UV model.

item.title: A High Performance Partial Wave Analysis Framework for Hadron Spectroscopy
item.dc:creator: Benhou Xiang et al.
item.description:
Xiang, Fang and Liu present CTPWA, a covariant-tensor PWA framework that exploits the factorisation of the amplitude: kinematic vertex tensors depend only on event four-momenta and decay topology, not fit parameters, so they are precomputed once and cached in GPU memory. The intensity becomes a per-event quadratic form I=θ_a^†𝐁θ_a, letting the negative log-likelihood, its analytic gradient, and full analytic Hessian be evaluated as batched dense linear algebra entirely on-device, with L-BFGS minimisation also on the GPU — eliminating graph re-tracing, host-device transfers, and per-iteration allocation. Benchmarks (10 channels, 3 polarisations) show per-iteration cost flat at 0.4–2.8 ms versus linear growth to ~400 ms for conventional pipelines; at 10⁶ events NLL+gradient takes ~2 ms (vs 23 ms GPU autograd, 2.3 s CPU autograd) and the analytic Hessian ~6 ms (vs 0.75 s and 75 s), while conventional pipelines exhaust device memory. A realistic J/ψ→K⁺K⁻η fit with 16 resonances, 33 couplings and 10⁶ events converges in ~7 s (fixed resonance parameters) or ~100 s (floating), after a one-time ~94 s precompute.

Why it matters: This is exactly the infrastructure high-statistics BESIII/LHCb analyses need, part of the day’s amplitude-analysis upgrade cycle alongside the neural ππ work. The analytic Hessian makes uncertainty estimation practical at high statistics. Caveat: gains depend on the likelihood being quadratic in couplings; floating resonance parameters break the phase-space pre-averaging and raise per-iteration cost roughly sevenfold, and memory reaches ~32 GB in that mode.

item.title: Direct lattice QCD calculation of the θ-induced CP-violating pion-nucleon coupling
item.dc:creator: Chuan-Yang Li et al.
item.description:
The χQCD collaboration reports the first direct lattice evaluation of the θ-induced CP-odd pion-nucleon coupling, extracting the forward proton matrix element of the isovector pseudoscalar density weighted by the topological charge to first order in θ̅. Working with overlap valence fermions on three RBC/UKQCD 2+1-flavor domain-wall ensembles at a single spacing (a=0.1105 fm), they use the index-theorem-consistent overlap definition of Q and cluster-decomposition error reduction (CDER) to tame the volume-enhanced noise, while explicitly including the θ̅-induced parity mixing of the external nucleon (the 2α_1 g_P term). A key simplification over their earlier nEDM work: the ratio at q²⁼⁰ directly isolates the full physical g̃_P with no zero-recoil extrapolation or separate α_1/g_P calculation, and Z_mZ_P=1 for overlap removes renormalization. An AIC-weighted average over 7 partially-quenched extrapolation forms yields g̃_πNN=0.0306(56)(124) θ̅; the full-volume cross-check gives 0.0305(87)(140) θ̅.

This supplies the hadronic-coupling rung above the nEDM, complementing yesterday’s Blum et al. extraction and testing the chiral matching relations that underpin EDM interpretations of light nuclei and diamagnetic atoms. The result is consistent with the indirect n–p mass-splitting estimate 0.0155(20)(16) θ̅, though the central value sits somewhat higher. The honest caveats are stark: the dominant second error is the extrapolation-form spread from heavy sea pions (no dedicated partially-quenched χPT expression exists), and the single lattice spacing means discretization effects are not quantified. Lighter-pion ensembles are underway.

item.title: Exclusive Determination of |V_cb| from Semileptonic Decays B→D⁽*)ℓν_ℓ
item.dc:creator: Xue-Wen Chen et al.
item.description:
Chen et al. perform a frequentist BGL global fit combining the latest Belle II B→Dℓν and B→D^ℓν spectra, updated lattice form factors (FNAL/MILC, HPQCD, JLQCD), and correlated large-recoil SCET/LCSR predictions with NLO and next-to-leading-power corrections, plus strong unitarity bounds from four heavy-to-heavy channels with HQET power corrections to 𝒪(ε_c²⁾. Three nested scenarios show LCSR constraints dramatically shrink high-order form-factor uncertainties. The full global fit yields |V_cb|=(39.18±0.47)×10⁻³, with the SM predictions R(D)=0.3069±0.0080 and R(D^)=0.2548±0.0043 from the lattice⊕LCSR theory fit. The correlated 68% theory ellipse in the (R(D),R(D^*)) plane shows “only modest overlap” with individual experimental measurements and a substantial deviation from the experimental average.

The takeaway for today’s flavor theme: even a state-of-the-art SM benchmark leaves the LFU tension intact, against a month where flavor has otherwise consolidated on nulls. The paper is candid about internal frictions — visible tension between the HPQCD B→D^ dataset and other lattice results, and mild lattice-vs-LCSR discord, though points overlap within errors. Their |V_cb| sits 1.7×10⁻³ below a recent Bayesian angular analysis, attributed to methodological choices (correlated LCSR inputs, dropping electron-mode data with known e/μ tension, frequentist vs. MCMC). Local angular deviations from Belle II exist but carry no significance. Whether the residual R(D⁽)) gap is theory systematics or new physics remains open pending better lattice/LCSR control and Belle II statistics.

item.title: S-matrix informed neural networks for amplitude analysis
item.dc:creator: Wyatt A. Smith et al.
item.description:
The Joint Physics Analysis Center introduces SINNs — neural representations of partial-wave amplitudes on the real axis that enforce S-matrix principles by construction. A shared trunk feeds channel-specific heads, with threshold barrier factors (q²ℓ+1) and the inelasticity map imposed algebraically in postprocessing (guaranteeing 0≤η≤1 and elastic unitarity below thresholds), while analyticity and crossing enter numerically through a twice-subtracted Roy-equation loss evaluated over 2m_π<√(s)<1.1 GeV. Training uses a six-phase curriculum with UPGrad multi-objective gradient handling to prevent the dispersive integrals from collapsing the fit to trivial solutions. Applied to ππ scattering, the framework recovers the expected σ/f_0(500), ρ(770), and f_0(980) features and yields scattering lengths a_0⁰⁼⁰.222⁺⁰.014_-0.014, a_0²⁼⁻⁰.041⁺⁰.005_-0.006 m_π⁻¹, consistent with Colangelo et al. and García-Martín et al. (with honestly larger bands, reflecting genuine amplitude-space sampling).

The methodological headline is “spectral response clustering”: each experiment is upweighted inside constrained ensembles, a symmetrized χ²-response matrix is spectrally embedded and Ward-clustered, and groups in tension are pruned automatically — replacing heuristic data selection. Two rounds cut the historically inconsistent ππ database to 18 experiments/621 points, dropping the deep-dip Protopopescu and several Grayer/Hyams solutions, lowering median loss from 7.2 to 3.1. Robustness is well-documented: a 100-architecture sweep shifts no central value by more than 0.42δx; closure tests recover a known CFD amplitude (|z|<0.4); and an ablation shows removing Roy constraints leaves data description untouched but degrades scattering lengths outside the universal band. Caveats acknowledged: the selected dataset implicitly depends on the selection architecture, unknown experimental systematics likely dominate, and the KK̅ cusp in the S_0 phase is deliberately not imposed. The workflow is presented as transferable to πK, πN, and beyond.

item.title: Search for the lepton-flavor-violating decay τ→μγ at Belle II
item.dc:creator: Belle II Collaboration et al.
item.description:
