Belle II sets ℬ(τ^±→μ^±γ)<9.5 (12.2)×10⁻⁸ at 90% (95%) CL on 428 fb⁻¹ (393×10⁶ ττ pairs), from an unbinned 2D extended maximum-likelihood fit in M_bc and ΔE/√(s) after a GBDT selection (final signal efficiency 5.97%, τ⁺τ⁻ rejection 99.8%). Eight events are observed in the signal region against a sideband-extrapolated background of 5.7±1.2; the fitted branching fraction (2.8⁺⁴.4_-2.6)×10⁻⁸ is consistent with zero. The observed limit is slightly weaker than the expected 7.6 (9.2)×10⁻⁸, attributed to a statistical upward fluctuation. Systematics are dominated by the 5.7% GBDT data/MC efficiency uncertainty (total 6.0% on the efficiency×luminosity×cross-section product); the dominant physical background is τ→μνν̅ plus an ISR/beam photon.

Why it matters: this is the flagship charged-LFV channel, where SM rates are ∼10⁻⁵⁴ and many BSM scenarios (SUSY, seesaw, Littlest Higgs) predict 10⁻¹⁰–10⁻⁸. The result does not yet beat Belle’s 4.2×10⁻⁸ (988 fb⁻¹) or BaBar’s 4.4×10⁻⁸, but on less than half the luminosity it achieves 41% higher signal efficiency and 81% lower background than the Belle analysis, and introduces a unified likelihood with profiled nuisance parameters — establishing the machinery for the far larger datasets to come. The honest caveat is scale: 428 fb⁻¹ is a fraction of Belle II’s design target, so this is a foundation-laying benchmark rather than a world-best number.

item.title: Calculation of neutron electric dipole moment from Lattice QCD
item.dc:creator: Thomas Blum et al.
item.description:
Blum et al. extract the θ̅-induced nEDM via a new Feynman–Hellmann route: rather than the noisy forward limit of the F_3 form factor, they compute the matrix element of the local (single-time-slice) topological charge density between nucleon ground states spatially polarized by a uniform background electric field. Because the dipole interaction is anti-Hermitian, these states have mixed parity and are constructed variationally through a non-Hermitian GEVP over a four-operator basis. On three 2+1-flavor domain-wall ensembles (a≈0.11 fm, m_π=340,420,576 MeV, electro-quenched), they obtain a statistically significant signal and extrapolate to d_n=-0.0050(4)(8) θ̅ e·fm. Comparison with the experimental bound gives |θ̅|≲10⁻¹¹, confirming the strong-CP problem.

Why it matters: previous F_3-based calculations at the physical point (Alexandrou et al., Bhattacharya et al.) yield no significant signal because the global topological-charge summation is too noisy; truncated-sum methods (Dragos et al., Liang et al.) introduce their own systematics. Sampling the topological charge locally sidesteps both global summation and the Q²→0 extrapolation, and the authors show the conventional positive-parity projection suffers large excited-state contamination that the GEVP removes — plausibly explaining a real discrepancy with the lighter-mass points of Liang et al. The method extends directly to Weinberg three-gluon and four-quark CP-odd operators. Caveats are explicit: single lattice spacing, electro-quenched approximation, and a physical-point extrapolation anchored at m_π=340 MeV — finite-volume and discretization effects remain to be quantified.

item.title: Electroweak and Single Top-Quark Conspiracy in Current LHC Data
item.dc:creator: Christoph Englert et al.
item.description:
Englert, Kogler, and Spannowsky ask whether recent above-SM central values in tWZ (μ=1.77±0.32) and tqγ (1.34⁺⁰.19_-0.17), plus a large ATLAS tHq (7.2⁺⁴.6_-4.0) alongside below-SM tt̅H (0.59⁺⁰.22_-0.20), form a coherent SMEFT pattern while VBS/triboson channels stay SM-like. A linearized (𝒪(Λ⁻²⁾) five-coefficient Warsaw-basis fit to eight LHC rates plus five Z-pole observables gives χ²_min=11.2 (8 d.o.f., p=0.19), improving on the SM by Δχ²⁼¹³.4 (local ∼2.1σ). The largest pulls are a triple-gauge C_W (∼1.9σ) and the weak top dipole C_tW (∼1.7σ), with positive C_Hq⁽³⁾; C_HW is poorly constrained. Fixing C_W=0 still fits (χ²⁼¹⁴.9, 9 d.o.f.). Notably, the fit absorbs the A_FB⁰,b anomaly — but only by shifting A_e ~4σ below LEP/SLD, a subset artifact flagged by the authors.

Why it matters: this is the EFT-as-diagnostic thread — using SMEFT not for limits but to test UV consistency. Under weakly-coupled renormalizable matching, no single scalar, vector, or vector-like-quark multiplet reproduces the pattern: currents need a charge-2/3 singlet, the dipole’s opposite chirality needs a hypercharge-1/6 doublet, and positive C_Hq⁽³⁾ demands triplet custodial partners protecting Zb_Lb̅_L. A benchmark multi-threshold VLQ sector (1.6–2.0 TeV) reproduces the current alignment with κ_t≃0.91, but the fit-preferred dipole must come from unspecified loop dynamics. Caveats: linearized truncation with no EFT uncertainty, no experimental covariances, and a preselected measurement set — the “2σ” is explicitly local and not a global SM improvement.

item.title: First Search for Ultraheavy Dark Matter Using a Magnetically Levitated Particle
item.dc:creator: Dennis G. Uitenbroek et al.
item.description:
(abstract only) POLONAISE uses a milligram-scale ferromagnet levitated in a superconducting trap as an impulse sensor, reaching a force sensitivity of 0.07 fN Hz⁻¹ᐟ² and resolving momentum kicks as small as 1 TeV/c. Treating every candidate impulse as a possible DM scatter, the collaboration sets optimum-interval upper limits on the neutron coupling for DM interacting via a light mediator: for masses 10⁶–10¹⁵ GeV/c² and mediators below 30 meV/c², they exclude couplings down to α_n = 3.2×10⁻⁹ at 95% CL, giving leading constraints on the DM–neutron cross section for composite DM.

The headline is the apparatus, not a signal. Magnetic levitation extends the mass reach of levitated-sensor DM searches seven orders of magnitude beyond optical levitation, opening the ultraheavy frontier where composite/dark-nugget candidates deposit resolvable single-scatter impulses. This is the mechanical-sensor counterpart to the day’s other hidden-sector hardware routes (qubit sensing, the HFIR mirror-neutron beam). With only the abstract available, the exposure, background model, and impulse-candidate treatment can’t be assessed here — but the quoted sensitivity and mass span are the concrete takeaways.

item.title: Angular analysis of the decay Λ_b⁰ → Λ(1520)μ⁺μ⁻
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
First angular analysis of this baryonic b→sℓℓ mode, using LHCb’s full Run 1+2 9 fb⁻¹ sample. The leptonic forward-backward asymmetry A^ℓ_FB,3/2 and the CP-averaged S_1cc are extracted in four narrow q² bins (0.1–12.5 GeV²/c⁴) plus the wide [1.1,6.0] bin, with the Λ(1520) reconstructed in pK⁻ and spin-1/2 Λ* contributions plus their interferences modelled explicitly. All measured values agree with SM predictions built on lattice-QCD and dispersive form factors — e.g. A^ℓ_FB,3/2 = 0.16±0.15±0.06 and S_1cc = 0.19±0.30±0.18 in [1.1,6.0]. The single mild outlier is S_1cc = 1.35±0.54±0.17 in [6.0,8.0], but statistics dominate throughout.

This is the baryonic complement to the mesonic b→sℓℓ program, probing the same FCNC transition with different hadronic structure and spin content — a useful cross-check as the mesonic picture has consolidated rather than sharpened since the mid-month C₉ discussion. Caveats are candid: the measurement is statistics-limited, the fit sits near physical boundaries (biases up to ~18% of the statistical error, corrected via pseudoexperiments), and systematics are dominated by combinatorial and Λ_c⁺-feeddown backgrounds. Discriminating among form-factor predictions awaits larger samples.

item.title: New Limits on n→n′ Transformation from HFIR Cold Neutron Beam
item.dc:creator: James M. Rogers et al.
item.description:
A neutron-regeneration search at HFIR’s CG-2/GP-SANS cold beam pushes the mirror-neutron transformation limit an order of magnitude below the prior SNS results. A 3.5 mm cadmium wafer at the center of a 6.6 T split-pair magnet absorbs all beam neutrons (to <10⁻²⁰); any n→n′ conversion in the first magnet half lets sterile n′ pass the cadmium and regenerate to detectable neutrons in the second half, caught by the low-background ³He detector 20 m downstream. No signal appears above background: 95% CL regeneration-probability limits reach ~1.25×10⁻¹¹ per neutron (B=0) up to a few×10⁻¹¹ at nonzero field, translating to an order-of-magnitude improvement in 2θ₀² across Δm = 0.1–1000 neV.

The gains come from HFIR’s ~400× higher average intensity, colder/wider spectrum, and the facility ³He detector. This is the same mirror-neutron channel flagged on 08-13, and one of four hidden-sector hardware routes in the day’s digest. Honest caveats: the 2021 run (~40 h) suffered detector activation of ⁵⁵Mn→⁵⁶Mn, raising and time-varying the background, so it carries reduced weight; the 2024 run (~90 h) is cleaner but background still crept up ~8% over the run. Beam-intensity normalization carries ~4–6% systematics reconciled across multiple monitors. Further reach demands higher intensity, longer beam time, and hard background reduction.

item.title: Observation of an excess at the top quark pair production threshold in the single-lepton channel
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
(Abstract only available.) CMS reports a 6.1σ excess near the tt̅ production threshold in single-lepton (e/μ + jets) final states using the full Run 2 dataset (138 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV). The analysis exploits the relative top–antitop velocity plus two angular observables sensitive to the parity and spin of the tt̅ system, comparing to an NNLO QCD baseline. The excess maps onto an observed total cross section of 5.1±0.9 pb and is consistent with a simplified NRQCD-motivated color-singlet pseudoscalar toponium state.

The significance here matters as much as the central value: the single-lepton channel is statistically independent of the dilepton measurement that first flagged the threshold enhancement, so this constitutes a genuine confirmation rather than a re-analysis of the same events. With two channels now converging on the same ∼5 pb, pseudoscalar-consistent signal, the “toponium” reading moves from a single anomaly toward a coherent picture — and sets up the competing elementary-scalar interpretation (Matsuoka’s top-philic 2HDM CP-odd Higgs) as the live alternative to test. The caveat is intrinsic to the modeling: the “toponium” is extracted against a fixed NNLO tt̅ prediction and fit to a simplified single-state NRQCD template, so the inferred cross section and its pseudoscalar identification are only as robust as that threshold-region theory baseline.

item.title: Search for top quark FCNC in multilepton final states using an EFT approach
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS performs the first global top-FCNC search in which all 24 relevant dimension-six SMEFT Wilson coefficients (12 for tu, 12 for tc) are constrained simultaneously in one likelihood, using 138 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data in same-sign dilepton and trilepton final states. Signal is probed in both single-top production and tt̅ decay via Higgs-, Z-, photon-, gluon-, and directly lepton-pair-mediated FCNC vertices; BDT discriminants (binary for 2ℓss, multiclass jigsaw-reconstructed for 3ℓ) feed a maximum-likelihood fit where signal yields are quadratic polynomials in the WCs. No excess is seen; 68% and 95% intervals are set on all 24 coefficients and translated to branching-fraction limits.

The headline is methodological and archival: this is the first simultaneous treatment of the complete FCNC operator set — including the first-ever direct constraints on two-quark–two-lepton FCNC operators — rather than the usual single-mediator-at-a-time approach that ignores interference. The resulting ℬ(t→Hq) and ℬ(t→Zq) bounds are quoted as similar to or more restrictive than prior anomalous-coupling results, and the framework is explicitly pitched as the reference for future LHC combinations. This fits the digest’s EFT-as-default-language theme. Caveats are candid: chiral partners are assumed equal-strength and lepton flavors share common WCs to keep the fit tractable; gluon (c_tG) and photon (c_tA) operators are included only “for completeness” given the multilepton channel’s weak sensitivity; and a 50% uncertainty on tt̅W reflects a known modeling tension.

item.title: Tracing Vacuum Hadronization with Conserved Currents
item.dc:creator: Weiyao Ke et al.
item.description:
Ke, Li, Li, Liu, and Shao argue that color triality — the requirement that an anti-fundamental Wilson-line endpoint be screened by matter of conjugate triality — forces the net electric-charge, baryon-number, and strangeness flows into a jet (or celestial region) to satisfy a jet-level Gell-Mann–Nishijima relation, ⟨Q_flow⟩_f ≃I_3,f + 12(⟨S_flow⟩_f + ⟨B_flow⟩_f). Because these are moments of conserved currents, they are IR-safe and renormalization-scale independent at leading power: any shift from the initiating parton’s charge is purely nonperturbative “defect-charge” screening. The net jet baryon number directly reads out the diquark-to-quark vacuum ratio, ⟨B_flow⟩_f ≃r_qq/(1+r_qq), and the strangeness flow encodes the strange-to-light ratio r_s.

Pythia 8.3 (Lund string) and Herwig 7.3 (cluster) validate the relations in e⁺e⁻ dijets across E_CM=50–1000 GeV: parton-level flows recover Q_f; hadron-level flows shift but obey the Gell-Mann–Nishijima diagonal in both generators. Scanning probStoUD recovers r_s≈ the input value across three independent slope projections; scanning probQQtoQ gives ⟨B_flow⟩ largely independent of the strange parameter, as predicted. This is the conserved-current-observable program (cf. the DELPHI one-point charge correlator) applied to hadronization microphysics, offering a flavor-resolved probe complementary to inclusive yield fits. Honest caveats: the extraction rests on a minimal one-quark/anti-diquark screening truncation (validated only to ∼9% by the event-level r_topology check), assumes light-flavor symmetry and independent flavor sampling, and the extracted r_qq deliberately does not equal probQQtoQ because of the state-dependent fragmentation history. Everything so far is generator-level; experimental tests are left to future work.

item.title: Observation of enhanced baryon production using strange hadrons in oxygen-oxygen collisions
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS measured p_T-differential K⁰_S and Λ cross sections in OO and pp collisions at √(s_NN)=5.36 TeV (6.8 nb⁻¹ and 1.06 pb⁻¹), reconstructing the neutral strange hadrons via displaced two-track vertices. The nuclear modification factor R_OO for K⁰_S tracks that of inclusive charged hadrons, but Λ baryons are enhanced over both in the intermediate range 2<p_T<8 GeV; above 10 GeV all three converge and sit well below unity, consistent with nPDF effects plus parton energy loss. The headline is the Λ/K⁰_S cross-section ratio, which shows a pronounced enhancement in OO versus pp for 2.3<p_T<5.2 GeV, with a significance of 5.0–6.3σ across bins after accounting for correlated systematics. The ratio’s peak also shifts from p_T≈2.3 GeV in pp to ≈2.8 GeV in OO.

This is the first observation of a baryon-to-meson enhancement in OO — the quark-coalescence/radial-flow signature of a deconfined medium — in a genuinely small system, without the event-activity selections that complicate high-multiplicity pp/pPb interpretations. It caps the season’s OO program (CMS charged-hadron suppression, ALICE/ATLAS flow, Υ suppression) with a clean coalescence handle. The qualitative trends mirror PbPb and AuAu, though “less pronounced in the smaller OO system.” Caveats are honest: the Λ feed-down correction (∼18% at 5 GeV) relies on scaling ALICE Ξ/Ω ratios to the OO multiplicity, and the pp comparison inherits pileup and secondary-track corrections.

item.title: Search for anomalous couplings in WW and WZ production with single-lepton final states at √s = 13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
Using the full Run 2 dataset (138 fb⁻¹), CMS searched for dimension-six EFT effects in boosted WV (WW/WZ) production where one W decays leptonically and the hadronic boson merges into a single large-R jet, tagged with mass-decorrelated ParticleNet (43% V-tag efficiency, ∼1% mistag). The m_WV spectrum (950–4550 GeV) is fit simultaneously with W+jets and tt̅ control regions, with the SM WV cross section floated (constrained to 0.32±0.1 times the NLO prediction — a notable tension the authors attribute to large LO-to-NLO K-factors and flag for dedicated measurement). Data are SM-consistent, and the analysis is statistics-limited.

The payoff is the strongest constraints to date on aTGC operators: in the HISZ basis the observed 95% intervals are c_WWW/Λ²∈[-0.93,0.93], c_W̃ WW∈[-0.37,0.49] TeV⁻², improving 30–70% over the previous 36 fb⁻¹ result. In SMEFT, c_W and c_W̃ reach [-0.08,0.08] TeV⁻² — the tightest triple-gauge bounds available — while the light-quark operators are competitive with, but not surpassing, inclusive-jet limits. This entrenches EFT with merged-jet substructure as the default diboson language, matching the digest’s theme. The main limitation is statistical, plus the approximate treatment of SMEFT operators potentially affecting background shapes (exact only in the HISZ triple-gauge case), and strong c_qq⁽³,1)–c_qq⁽³,8) degeneracy from insensitivity to color flow.

item.title: Axion-like particle at the 10 GeV scale: Higgs decays to wide jets and photons
item.dc:creator: Bogdan A. Dobrescu et al.
item.description:
Dobrescu and Roy build a renormalizable model where an ALP A_h couples to the SM only through the Higgs portal (-μ_Hϕ2v_ϕH^†H A_h A_h), with TeV-scale charge-2/3 colored scalars generating loop-induced A_h→gg (BR ∼99%) and A_h→γγ (BR ∼0.15%, fixed by 8α²/9α_s²). An effective portal coupling μ_Hϕ/v_ϕ≈10⁻² yields B(h⁰→A_hA_h)≈10%, below current undetected-width limits (<12% from ATLAS under |κ_V|≤1). The key claim: h⁰→A_hA_h→(gg)(γγ) produces an automatically boosted diphoton at M_A≈13.6 GeV that satisfies existing low-mass diphoton selections. Delphes-level cutflows give acceptance×efficiency of 12.7% (CMS) and 11.9% (ATLAS), and the model’s 1σ bands overlap both the CMS 3.5σ excess and the milder ATLAS ∼1.8σ at the same mass — reconciling the two, which under a singly-produced-ALP hypothesis appeared inconsistent.

If it holds, the CMS excess is not a lone diphoton resonance but a Higgs cascade with distinctive hadronic activity: the second A_h yields a wide jet J_gg with 2-prong substructure, and combining it with the diphoton reconstructs a 125-GeV peak (broad, from their simulation) — a background-suppression handle CMS/ATLAS could exploit. The companion h⁰→A_hA_h→4g mode (two wide jets, or (2+2)-prong when boosted) is unsearched. Caveats: the fit relies on order-of-magnitude kinematic estimates and simplified isolation proxies (large PTRatioMax to bypass rejection), not a full experimental reproduction, and the ALP mass formula requires tuned but “natural” cutoffs.

item.title: Quadruple-Higgs boson production at the high-luminosity LHC
item.dc:creator: Andreas Papaefstathiou et al.
item.description:
First phenomenological study of gg→hhhh as a probe of the Higgs self-couplings, targeting the eight-b-jet final state at √(s)=14 TeV, 3000 fb⁻¹. The SM LO rate is tiny — σ(gg→hhhh)≃1.24×10⁻⁴ fb, a factor ∼350 below triple-Higgs — but the four-Higgs amplitude carries more quartic-coupling structure. An XGBoost classifier trained on 52 reconstructed observables, combined with a five-bin Poisson likelihood over the (c_3,d_4) plane (where c_3=κ_3-1, d_4=κ_4-1), yields simultaneous 95% bounds -10.3<c_3<11.2 and -222<d_4<234. The signal hypothesis actually combines hhhh, hhh+bb̅, and hh+4b; at the SM point it expects only 0.39 signal vs 21.9 background events. They also show hhhh→8b events with ≥6 tags feed the ATLAS hhh→6b region — with ∼89.5% tag probability the four-Higgs contribution can reach 10–100% of the hhh rate in parts of the plane.

Why it matters: the quartic coupling κ_4 is essentially unconstrained by phenomenology; this opens a channel and argues for jointly treating hhh and hhhh in inclusive multi-b analyses, complementing the ATLAS Higgs-combination push into loose corners. Caveats are heavy and honest: statistics-only limits, no detector/PDF/scale systematics, the hh+4b piece computed in m_t→∞ with only c_3 dependence, forced-splitting approximations, and sub-unit expected counts making asymptotic contours approximate. On a like-for-like basis the reach is comparable to ATLAS hhh in c_3 but weaker in d_4.

item.title: Entanglement of back-to-back gluon pair
item.dc:creator: Lei Yang et al.
item.description:
Full polarization density matrices for back-to-back gluon pairs in unpolarized pp collisions, computed at tree level for the qq̅→gg and gg→gg channels. For qq̅→gg, chirality conservation plus the MHV structure restrict the state to the |Ψ^±⟩ Bell sector; at perpendicular emission (θ=π/2) the pair becomes the pure Bell state |Ψ⁻⟩ — maximally entangled, concurrence 𝒞=-c_q(θ) reaching unity and S_max>2 (CHSH-violating) across 0<θ<π. In contrast, gg→gg is separable at all angles (𝒞=0, S_max≤10√(2)/9<2) but retains an appreciable linear-polarization correlation, c_g(π/2)=1/9≈11%. The observable link is the four-point energy correlator (E4C): contracting the pair density matrix with collinear splitting kernels maps the correlation onto a cos2ΔΦ azimuthal modulation between the two branching planes, with asymmetry 𝒜^κ=12(C_xx’+C_yy’)a^κ(n).

Why it matters: it extends the collider quantum-information program into the gluon sector, showing entanglement is generated purely by QCD helicity structure rather than a color-singlet vertex as in H→gg. The distinction between an entangled qq̅-initiated state and a merely correlated gg-initiated one is physically sharp. Caveat: the inclusive E4C signal suffers strong cancellations among qq̅ qq̅, qq̅ gg, gggg splitting channels; heavy-flavor tagging in both jets is needed to isolate QQ̅ QQ̅ and recover sensitivity. Extraction relies on the one-step collinear-splitting approximation, and the tagged sample is expected to be gg→gg-dominated with qq̅→gg as irreducible Born contamination.

item.title: Astrophysical Graviton Squeezing Can Be Hidden in the Far-Field
item.dc:creator: Cheng-Jun Fang et al.
item.description:
Using spatial quantum-optics methods extended to gravity, the authors compute the second-order coherence g⁽²⁾ accessible to a single far-field detector for gravitons emitted in a macroscopically squeezed state from a localized astrophysical source. An EFT description of squeezed-graviton generation yields Bogoliubov coefficients that inherit the source’s momentum envelope; the far-field projection (retarded pole extraction, angular stationary phase) shows a local observer effectively measures the asymptotic out-state along a single line of sight. The key result is a “same-cone” kinematic conflict: for a non-relativistic source the squeezing matrix peaks on the anti-diagonal (𝐩+𝐪≈0, back-to-back pairs), so the anomalous coherence M_D requires one internal momentum simultaneously near 𝐩 and -𝐩’ — incompatible for same-direction detection. The result is g⁽²⁾⁻²∼𝒪[exp(-2d ℰ/k_*)]+𝒪(L_D/r), so a globally squeezed state appears classically thermal (g⁽²⁾⁼²) locally.

Why it matters: this is the third graviton-quantumness no-go the memory has tracked (after Bao et al. and Miyauchi et al.), attacking macroscopic squeezing from the far-field-observability angle rather than production. Global squeezing does not guarantee local detectability. The authors frame it as a conditional no-go requiring three conditions: non-relativistic source, single localized detector, near-flat propagation. Each suggests an escape: relativistic/collinear sources (BH binaries, jets) could restore ℰ/k_*∼1; multi-detector networks probing both partner cones recover cross-correlations (feasible for a nearby solar axion halo); and strong-curvature lensing near compact objects can redirect back-to-back pairs into one cone. A concurrent independent preprint (ref. 51) reached consistent conclusions via a different framework.

item.title: First measurement of the one-point charge correlator in e⁺e⁻ collisions at √(s)=91.2 GeV with DELPHI Open Data
item.dc:creator: Jingyu Zhang et al.
item.description:
Zhang et al. deliver the first-ever measurement of the one-point charge correlator — the net electric-charge flux 𝒬(θ) into the detector as a function of polar angle relative to the e⁻ beam — from 61 pb⁻¹ of archival DELPHI Open Data (46 pb⁻¹ in 1994, 15 pb⁻¹ in 1995). This is a jet-free, hemisphere-free, IRC-safe reformulation of the hadronic forward-backward asymmetry: the parity-odd cosθ coupling structure shows up directly as a sin(2θ) modulation in the charge-weighted track density (tracks with p_T>2 GeV, 20°≤θ≤160°). Detector effects are handled in two stages — a PYTHIA 8.3-based correction for track-finding, fakes and charge misID, then a data-driven tag-and-probe measurement of the residual data–MC charge-misreconstruction bias in Z→τ⁺τ⁻ events, where charge conservation fixes the probe’s true sign. The fully corrected result exhibits the expected sin(2θ) shape, negative in the forward hemisphere, crossing zero at 90°, and agrees with PYTHIA 8.3 within uncertainties.

Why it matters: this establishes experimental viability of a genuinely new precision-EW handle, one whose relation to the Z couplings is not mediated by jet-charge model dependence — the very ambiguity blamed for the persistent A_FB^b tension. The construction extends to heavy-flavor currents where tensions are largest, and prefigures Tera-Z programs at FCC-ee/CEPC. The honest caveat is prominent: this is a proof-of-principle, not a competitive extraction. Systematics (27.6%/35.6% at θ=55°/125°) dominate over statistics and are set by the τ control-sample size; the parity-odd bias component is bounded, not measured to vanish. Sagitta and photon-conversion calibrations are the named next steps.

item.title: Evidence for parity violation in gravitational fields
item.dc:creator: V. Gharibyan et al.
item.description:
Gharibyan et al. analyze 314,896 Compton spectra from the HERA transverse polarimeter (2004–2007), tagged by 514.5 nm laser helicity, and report a laser-helicity-dependent asymmetry in the Compton-edge energy (ω_max=13.9 GeV) of A=(4.89±0.52)×10⁻⁵, claimed at 9σ. Within a phenomenological framework where the gravitational coupling acquires a helicity-dependent term G_s=G+(𝐬·𝐏/P)ΔG_𝒫, the modified energy-momentum relation shifts ω_max oppositely for the two helicities, and the γ² amplification factor sets the sensitivity. They translate the asymmetry into a helicity-dependent gravitational-potential difference ΔU_𝒫=(1.71±0.036±0.187)×10⁻¹⁴, i.e. ΔG_𝒫/G=(5.7±0.6)×10⁻¹⁰ using summed local potentials (dominated by the Virgo Supercluster). The signal is isotropic in right ascension (constant fit checked against 64 bins), which they argue excludes Lorentz-violating vector theories, and they estimate instrumental false asymmetries from transverse/longitudinal beam polarization and linear-light contamination to be sub-dominant.

Why it matters: if real, this would be the first high-energy test of a discrete symmetry in gravity showing violation, with speculative implications for galactic rotation curves via a chiral-gravity shift of the 21 cm line — potentially bearing on dark matter. But this is an extraordinary claim resting on a 5×10⁻⁵ edge shift in a polarimeter never built to measure absolute energy asymmetries. The authors themselves flag “hidden systematic factors”: helicity-dependent detector gain (estimated opposite-sign from bremsstrahlung fits, but uncorrected due to unknown beam offsets on an inhomogeneous calorimeter) and helicity-correlated laser spatial jitter convolved with the lepton phase space. The digest’s “read skeptically” is well-earned.

item.title: Truncation of the Radial Ladder in Heavy Quarkonia
item.dc:creator: Wen-Xuan Zhang et al.
item.description:
Zhang, Luo and Liu ask whether the radial excitation ladder of quarkonia terminates, solving a screened relativized Godfrey–Isgur Hamiltonian for cc̅ and bb̅ via the Gaussian expansion method (N_max=20, r_max=30 fm) up to n=14. Screened confinement replaces the linear term’s unbounded rise with a plateau M_∞=m_1+m_2+b/μ+c, giving limiting masses of 4.74 GeV (cc̅) and 11.67 GeV (bb̅). Crucially, while masses saturate — adjacent gaps dropping below 10 MeV — RMS radii keep diverging to ∼10–50 fm, an order of magnitude past the confinement scale. This “mass–radius decoupling” defines a breakdown of the qq̅ picture. A threshold criterion (min gap <10 MeV with radius increments >3/2 fm), corroborated by CUSUM/two-segment changepoint analysis of log(ΔR/ΔM) and a resolvability index χ_n=ΔM_n R_n collapsing below unity, locates operational upper limits at n≈8–10 for charmonium (D-waves first, then P, then S) and n≈12–13 for bottomonium. Staged χ² fits give RMS mass residuals of 34/24 MeV (10/4 MeV for low-lying states), with the charmonium screening length μ⁻¹≈1.4 fm inside the lattice string-breaking range.

Why it matters: this is the first quantitative answer to a long-standing spectroscopy question, and it is directly testable — no new charmonia should appear above ∼4.7 GeV, and BESIII/Belle II/LHCb can probe this. Caveats are candidly stated: high-n bottomonium shows round-off artifacts; the thresholds are empirical; and the truncation value is model-input-dependent (alternative fits give 4.61–4.83 GeV). Formal parameter errors are not quoted. The manuscript was substantially AI-drafted (Grok, GPT-5.4), per the authors’ declaration.

item.title: Beyond Δm²: Absolute Mass Sensitivity in Neutrino Oscillations
item.dc:creator: Gustavo F. S. Alves et al.
item.description:
The headline is conceptual: the oscillation phase, expanded beyond leading order in mᵢ/E, contains a term ∝ (mᵢ⁴−mⱼ⁴)L/E₀³ = Δmᵢⱼ²(mᵢ²+mⱼ²)L/E₀³, so oscillations do carry absolute-mass information through the mass-squared sum. The authors show this cannot be recovered from naive plane-wave prescriptions — equal-energy, equal-momentum, and various t↔L replacements disagree at NLO — and derive it properly with a wave-packet treatment that fixes each eigenstate’s mean energy/momentum from beta-decay kinematics (an effective two-body decay N_A→(N_B e)+ν̄). The production-dependent correction enters only at the per-mille level (E₀/m_A ≲ 10⁻⁴). Applied to JUNO’s 52.5 km reactor baseline, a χ² fit to ~9.5×10⁴ IBD events over six years yields sensitivity m₁ < 305 keV (1σ), 434 keV (2σ) with oscillation parameters profiled; the solar channel dominates because its broad dip lands in JUNO’s high-statistics band and survives energy smearing intact.

Why it matters: this overturns the textbook statement that oscillations measure only Δm². It is a genuinely new, mechanism-independent absolute-mass probe, sensitive to a different combination than beta decay (m_νe), 0νββ (m_ββ), or cosmology (Σmᵢ). The honest caveat is scale: at few-hundred-keV, this is ~10⁴× weaker than KATRIN (0.45 eV) and ~10⁷× weaker than cosmology (0.053 eV), and the sensitivity is limited by a degeneracy in which the NLO shift mimics a rescaling Δm₂₁²→Δm₂₁²(1+m₁²/2E₀²), broken only by the 1/E₀² energy dependence.

item.title: Enhanced Three-Particle Contribution to Electroweak Penguin B-Meson Decays
item.dc:creator: Yong-Kang Huang et al.
item.description:
Using SCET with two-step QCD→SCET_I→SCET_II matching, the authors compute for the first time the subleading-twist correction to B→{K,π}ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ from the three-particle twist-three B-meson distribution amplitude at NLO, plus new NNLO corrections to the spectator-scattering (C-type) and weak-annihilation topologies and the O(α_s) D-type spectator term. This is billed as the last missing ingredient for a complete leading-power factorization proof of the b→{s,d}ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ matrix element. The three-particle convolution integrals over the two soft momenta are shown to converge, and the new jet function J_C^(3P) is validated by a second, method-of-regions calculation. Numerically, the newly included leading-power effects shift both real and imaginary parts of the top-sector amplitude T_π⁰ by O(30%) in q²∈[1.5, 4.0] GeV², driven by cancellation among A- and B-type pieces; the largest phenomenological impact is on the direct-CP-asymmetry differences ΔA_CP(B→Pℓℓ), shifted 15–20% at large recoil, where the nontrivial strong phase of J_C^(3P) dominates.

Why it matters: this is the theory-side counterpart to the week’s C₉ story — tightening the leading-power factorization control that any short-distance NP interpretation of b→sℓℓ requires. The honest caveat is that it does not resolve the anomaly: branching fractions for B⁰→K⁰ℓℓ and B⁺→K⁺ℓℓ “remain in sharp tension” with Belle/CDF/LHCb/CMS at large recoil, and the new B⁺→π⁺ℓℓ predictions actually favor old LHCb data over the latest full-Run-1+2 result (1.1–2.5σ).

item.title: Improved measurement of CP violation in B⁰ₛ→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ decays
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
LHCb performs a time-dependent, flavour-tagged amplitude analysis of ~94,000 B⁰ₛ→J/ψπ⁺π⁻ signal decays from the full Run 2 6 fb⁻¹ sample (38 fs decay-time resolution, 4.5% tagging power), extracting φₛ = −0.077 ± 0.034 ± 0.007 rad, |λ| = 0.993 ± 0.026 ± 0.007, and Γ_H = 0.610 ± 0.002 ± 0.004 ps⁻¹. The π⁺π⁻ spectrum is modelled with six resonances plus a nonresonant term — adding an f₂(1565) contribution to a small ~1.6 GeV peak relative to earlier work — with the CP-odd f₀(980) carrying 72.5% fit fraction. Combining with Run 1 gives φₛ = −0.046 ± 0.031 rad; folding in all other LHCb channels yields φₛ = −0.041 ± 0.017 rad (χ²/ndf = 35/30), consistent with the J/ψφ average and improving precision by ~15%.

Why it matters: against a week where the flavour front ran on anomalies, this is a clean null. The result sits squarely on the SM prediction φₛ^SM = −0.0376₋₀.₀₀₀₅⁺⁰·⁰⁰⁰⁶ rad, and no direct CP violation is seen (|λ| compatible with 1). The main caveat is explicit in the text: subleading penguin contributions are neglected throughout — externally constrained to a Δφₛ = 5.0 ± 4.6 mrad shift from B⁰→J/ψρ⁰ — and the production asymmetry A_P is fixed to zero (a ±2% variation is taken as systematic). Systematics remain subdominant to the 34 mrad statistical uncertainty on φₛ.

item.title: Observation of several sources of CP violation in B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
Working the full 3 fb⁻¹ Run 1 sample (115,102 candidates, 88.7% purity), LHCb performs an amplitude analysis of B⁺→K⁺π⁺π⁻ with three independent treatments of the troublesome Kπ and ππ S-waves (isobar/GLASS, K-matrix, and a first-of-its-kind quasi-model-independent binning of two crossing partial waves). All three agree, and six CP-violation phenomena clear observation-level significance at once. The headline first observations: quasi-two-body CPV in B⁺→ρ(770)⁰K⁺, 𝒜_CP=+0.280±0.022±0.029 (minimum 5.9σ across S-wave models); and in B⁺→f_2(1270)K⁺, rejected at 8.2–9.1σ at amplitude level. First evidence appears for CPV in the elastic ππ-ππ rescattering S-wave below the 4π threshold (𝒜^S_CP=+0.665±0.032±0.053), in S–P interference with ρ(770) (5.4σ), in S–D interference near the f_2(1270) (≥4.4σ), and — a genuine first — in a spin-3 state, ρ_3(1690)⁰ (≥3.3σ).

Notably, no CPV is seen in ρ⁰–ω mixing, contrary to several predictions; this dilution explains why the fitted ρ(770) asymmetry exceeds the model-independent P-wave value (0.150±0.022). A large positive asymmetry immediately above ππ threshold resists all three models, hinting at sizeable cc̅-loop or isospin-2 contributions. Systematics are comparable to statistical uncertainties throughout — good model control, but a signal that Run 1 statistics can no longer fully exploit. This is the measurement-side counterpart to the season’s flavor anomalies, sharpening reference points for γ extraction and B→Kπ-type isospin sum rules.

item.title: Probing CP-violating top-quark dipole moments with tomographic observables
item.dc:creator: Maxim Perelstein et al.
item.description:
Perelstein, Shaik and Youn recast tt̅ spin tomography as a CP-violation search. Symmetry fixes which Fano coefficients a CP-odd (chromo-)electric dipole can populate: the normal polarization difference ΔB_n and the antisymmetric normal-plane correlations A_rn, A_kn, all exactly zero in the SM (three-loop suppressed). They compute the production density matrix in closed form for e⁺e⁻, qq̅ and gg, build the statistically optimal CP-odd observable O_opt=f_1/f_0 (proven to saturate the Cramér–Rao bound), and carry the analysis to Delphes detector level. Projected 95% CL reach on inverse couplings: 10–15 TeV for the electroweak electric dipoles d_γ,d_Z at FCC-ee (365 GeV, 3 ab⁻¹), and 40 (200) TeV for the top chromo-EDM at LHC Run 2 (HL-LHC) — exceeding the conventional triple/quadruple-product observables (e.g. the CMS O_1 search) used today. d_γ projects mainly onto A_rn, d_Z onto ΔB_n; the optimal weight combines them for ~40 TeV parton-level FCC-ee reach.

A sharp negative result accompanies this: they prove a no-go theorem that the top–antitop discord asymmetry Δ𝒟 (and geometric discord, steering asymmetry) vanishes identically for the dipoles, contradicting a recent claim that advertised it as a CP probe — the reported nonzero values are CP-even absorptive artifacts. Caveats: reach at FCC-ee threshold is diluted by poor top-direction reconstruction (∼40^∘, dilution factors 0.24–0.40); systematics are assumed subdominant, and the EFT-consistent linear-order truncation neglects dimension-eight-degenerate terms.

item.title: High-precision measurement of the space-like η' transition form factor
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
BESIII measures the single-virtual space-like η’ TFF via single-tag two-photon fusion e⁺e⁻→e⁺e⁻η’ on 20.3 fb⁻¹ at 3.773 GeV, reconstructing η’→π⁺π⁻γ and π⁺π⁻η. The result spans Q²∈[0.1,6.0] GeV² in 18 fine bins, reaches better than 3% precision below 1.5 GeV², and provides the first direct determination at Q²<0.3 GeV² — filling the gap between BaBar (>4 GeV²) and L3 (<0.15 GeV², which inferred Q² indirectly from the η’ transverse momentum). Tight control of the untagged-photon virtuality (Q²_miss∈[0,0.08] GeV², with a +1.0% correction to Q²_miss=0) is the key improvement; total systematics run 2.5–4.7% on the cross section, halved on the TFF.

The extracted values are the most precise to date and lie systematically above earlier data — attributed to the larger, less-controlled Q²_miss of prior measurements. Crucially, the data agree with lattice QCD (BMW) and holographic (LMR) predictions while sitting above data-driven dispersive models. Since LQCD and holographic approaches also predict a larger a_μ^η’ than the data-driven evaluation, this input feeds directly into the hadronic light-by-light contribution to muon g-2 — where LQCD HLbL now runs ~50% above the 2020 white-paper number — and the authors flag that existing data-driven analyses may warrant re-evaluation. The result also constrains the η’ gluonic component and η’ production models.

item.title: Model-independent measurement of the transversity amplitudes of the B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ decay
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
LHCb reconstructs the full set of B⁰→K^*0μ⁺μ⁻ transversity amplitudes unbinned in q² over 1.1<q²<8.0 GeV²/c⁴, expanding each P-wave amplitude in four Legendre polynomials (32 parameters, S-wave as nuisance) fitted to 8.4 fb⁻¹. The orthogonality of the Legendre basis reduces amplitude correlations relative to earlier empirical parametrisations, and CP-averaged observables (S_5, A_FB, etc.) are then built as continuous functions of q². Systematics run 0.09–0.35 of the statistical error, dominated by kinematic/trigger corrections. Profiling in flavio with the Ref. [14] baseline binning gives Re(C_9^NP)=-1.17⁺⁰.21_-0.20, a 4.3σ pull; quartering the bins tightens to -1.17⁺⁰.19_-0.18 and 4.8σ.

The key point is methodological: because hadronic (long-distance) contributions and a genuine NP C_9 shift have distinct q² dependences, the unbinned amplitude reconstruction lets global fits choose their own binning and, in principle, disentangle the two. The C_9 deviation surviving this more flexible treatment — and growing with finer q² resolution — is exactly what one expects from a real short-distance effect rather than a mismodelled charm-loop contamination. Results agree with the latest binned angular analysis [14]. Caveat: the interpretation still fixes all other Wilson coefficients to SM values and imports SM hadronic nuisance parameters through flavio’s covariance; the significance is a one-parameter statement, and the amplitude fit assumes no scalar/timelike contributions and a uniform-in-q² S-wave. The disentangling of hadronic versus NP awaits improved theory predictions to compare against the measured amplitudes.

item.title: Anomalies in Hadronic B Decays
item.dc:creator: Marianne Bouchard et al.
item.description:
This BEACH 2026 proceedings summarises SU(3)_F global fits to B→PP (P∈{π,K,η,η’}) in the topological-diagram basis, using EWP-tree relations to reduce 10 complex amplitudes to seven effective diagrams (13 real parameters). Individually the ΔS=0 (χ²/dof=1.1/2, p=58%) and ΔS=1 (1.6/2, p=45%) fits are excellent, but the combined SU(3)_F-symmetric fit collapses to χ²/dof=43/17, a 3.6σ SM discrepancy. The cause: best-fit diagram magnitudes differ across sectors by ~10×, e.g. |T̃’/T̃|=13.1±2.1, |C̃’/C̃|=8.9±1.3 — nominally 1000% SU(3)_F breaking versus the ~20–30% (f_K/f_π-1) expected. Adding η,η’ (25 parameters) worsens the fit to 4.1σ; the B→VV extension exceeds 7σ.

Imposing theory-motivated constraints makes things worse, not better: forcing |C̃/T̃|=0.2 (QCD-factorisation colour-counting) against the fitted 0.85±0.12 pushes to 4.9σ, and setting the annihilation diagram Ã=0 (expected ∼f_B/m_B-suppressed, yet fitted ∼|T̃|) gives 5.2σ. The claim to near-rigour rests on the EWP-tree relations being modified only ~10% by neglected c_7,8. This is the day’s second, independent B-anomaly hint, from the non-leptonic sector. Caveat: it is a proceedings, results drawn from Refs. [6–9]; the central assumption is exact SU(3)_F with a fixed θ_η=19.5°, and the authors themselves flag that whether a genuine ~30% breaking could accommodate the data “has to be checked” — work in progress.

item.title: Measurement of the ν̅_μ–Hydrogen CCQE cross section using the NOvA Near Detector
item.dc:creator: The NOvA Collaboration
item.description:
NOvA isolates ν̅_μH→μ⁺ⁿ from the 10.8%-hydrogen scintillator/PVC near detector (1.2×10²¹ POT), exploiting the nuclear-effect-free kinematics of a free-proton target: two BDT discriminants (topological HitID, kinematic KineID) plus data-driven control regions yield 35,509 background-subtracted signal events — the highest-statistics (anti)neutrino–hydrogen sample ever. The result, σ=0.538±0.009(stat)±0.010(syst)±0.055(flux)×10⁻³⁸ cm² at ⟨E⟩=1.9 GeV, is the most precise total QEH cross section to date, superseding the 13±6-event BNL bubble-chamber measurement. The decisive feature: the combined stat+non-flux systematic (2.5%) is more than four times below the 10.2% flux uncertainty, so the measurement can invert the usual logic and constrain the absolute ν̅_μ flux.

This lands squarely on the digest’s theme: the same cross-section systematics that were shifting DUNE sensitivities 25–30% (Puhan et al.) are precisely what a nuclear-effect-free reference process pins down. The data-correction scheme is validated by 10,000 fake-data throws showing background predictions stable against ~60% MC variations, with k_cut factors anticorrelated with the model shifts. Caveats are candidly stated: QEH purities are only ~41%/36% and signal efficiencies 3.6%/4.8%, so the analysis leans heavily on control-region-driven background subtraction; FSI weights are derived solely from neutrino-mode inclusive CC data and applied unchanged to antineutrino mode. The flux uncertainty still dominates the cross section itself — the payoff is prospective, once this becomes a flux standard candle.

item.title: An improved direct limit on the muon electric dipole moment
item.dc:creator: 2 Collaboration et al.
item.description:
The Fermilab Muon g−2 collaboration sets d_μ⁺⁼⁽⁻⁰.35±0.19_stat±0.34_sys)×10⁻¹⁹ ecm from its 2019–20 straw-tracker data (2.34×10⁹ positrons across Run-2, Run-3a, Run-3b), yielding |d_μ|<1.10×10⁻¹⁹ ecm at 95% CL — a factor 1.5 improvement on the BNL E821 limit. The measurement uses the traceback method: a muon EDM tilts the spin-precession plane, producing an oscillation in the average vertical decay angle ⟨θ_y⟩ that is π/2 out of phase with the anomalous precession. Data are fit in 8 momentum bins × 2 stations × 3 runs (48 measurements, average reduced χ²⁼¹.08), combined via BLUE. Combining with BNL tightens the bound to |d_μ|<0.98(0.86)×10⁻¹⁹ ecm at 95(90)% CL.

Why it matters: the result stays ~19 orders of magnitude above the SM prediction (∼10⁻³⁸ ecm), so it functions as a clean BSM null test on a CP-violating source independent of the anomalous-moment program, complementing the model-dependent indirect bound (1.9×10⁻²⁰).

Caveat, honestly flagged: this is systematics-limited, dominated (by far) by the vertical-alignment false-signal correction (3.12×10⁻²⁰, vs. 1.87 statistical). Notably, the analysis failed the initial soft-unblinding 3σ check, triggering the internal review that uncovered the vertical-misalignment and longitudinal-field systematics; a data-driven correction was then developed while still blinded. The alignment uncertainty is itself statistics-limited and should shrink with Runs 4–6 (2.5× the present dataset).

item.title: TauPolaris: reconstructing tau lepton polarimetric vectors with conditional normalizing flows
item.dc:creator: Daniel Winterbottom et al.
item.description:
TauPolaris estimates the undetected neutrino momenta in τ decays with a conditional normalizing flow (nine spline-coupling blocks, transformer conditioning network), modeling the full joint density p(ν|𝐜) rather than a point regression. This preserves the correlations between momentum components — crucially reconstructing the τ mass at the physical 1.78 GeV, where an MSE-trained transformer biases low and pushes the neutrino collinear with the visible τ. A gradient-ascent MAP estimate in the flow’s latent space gives per-event neutrino configurations with ~40% better angular resolution than the transformer and ~20% better than sampling. On simulated LHC pp collisions with Delphes+CMS-HPS detector modeling, three applications are demonstrated: distinguishing quantum entanglement from a classically-correlated null in H→ττ at >4.3σ (and Bell witness m_12 at 4.0σ) with 3 ab⁻¹; improving CP-violation sensitivity via ϕ_CP by 18% overall (up to 88% in 3π^±0π⁰–3π^±0π⁰, and enabling 3π^±1π⁰ reconstruction for the first time); and new polarimetric variables to suppress Z→ττ.

Why it matters: this moves the collider-QI program from top-quark tomography toward a deployable analysis tool, extending the optimal polarimetric-vector method to every τ decay topology (previously restricted to 3-prong modes with secondary vertices).

Caveats: entirely simulation-based, with hand-added track smearing to patch Delphes; the entanglement 4.3σ is an upper limit set by finite pseudoexperiments, and yields are extrapolated from a single BDT window assuming preserved S/B. The 𝒞/m_12 estimators are biased on finite data, requiring pseudoexperiment calibration.

item.title: Electroweak precision observables at NLL order in the SMEFT
item.dc:creator: Ulrich A. Haisch et al.
item.description:
Haisch and Stefanek upgrade SMEFT predictions for electroweak precision observables to next-to-leading-logarithmic accuracy by combining one-loop EW matching with two- and one-loop RG evolution from Λ to m_Z, leveraging the newly available two-loop SMEFT beta functions. A key methodological point, proven via the T-parameter contribution of the right-handed four-top operator Q_uu³³³³: two-loop matching is not needed for NLL — higher-order matching cannot generate ln(Λ/m_Z) logarithms, so one-loop matching plus NLL running suffices. The headline deliverable is numerical NLL expressions encoding the full dependence on all 210 independent Wilson coefficients (excluding only Q_H, which enters at NNLL), released as ancillary files, with explicit results tabulated for five benchmark operators.

Why it matters: whereas tree-level matching reaches only 23 operators, NLL running opens EWPO sensitivity to the entire operator set — including operators contributing only at two-loop order (Q_G, Q_HG, Q_uH³³), which have no one-loop EWPO effect at all. For the top chromomagnetic dipole Q_uG³³, the genuine two-loop L (green) terms actually dominate the L²/L (red) terms, driven by a large y_t³ beta function mixing into Q_HD. This is positioned as the reference basis for FCC-ee/CEPC global fits at sub-permille precision, continuing the SMEFT-precision thread.

Caveats: the framework is illustrated on current LEP/SLC fits and projections rather than delivering a full global result here; couplings are fixed at m_Z (differences are NNLL). The authors note complementary concurrent work (Mantani et al.; Born et al.), and stress that a complete analysis must retain both oblique and non-oblique observables.

item.title: Neutrinoless Double-Beta Decays from Operator Mixing
item.dc:creator: J. de Vries et al.
item.description:
(abstract only) A complete one-loop SMEFT renormalization-group analysis shows that dimension-seven operators which do not contribute to 0νββ at tree level nonetheless generate sizable contributions via operator mixing under RG running. Accounting for the full one-loop evolution, the resulting 0νββ constraints become the most stringent bounds to date on numerous dim-7 operators — improving on limits from meson decays. The authors stress that effects beyond the first leading logarithm can dominate for specific operators and flavor combinations.

Why it matters: this is the day’s most experiment-adjacent rigor, converting the extreme sensitivity of 0νββ into a systematic constraint on the broader lepton-number-violating operator basis rather than a single-parameter mass bound. Caveat: only the abstract is available, so the numerical bounds and the flavor/operator specifics cannot be verified here.

item.title: The π/12 model: trimaximal first-column lepton mixing with charged-lepton μ–τ breaking
item.dc:creator: Vernon Barger
item.description:
Barger decomposes the first PMNS column into two independent conditions — the trimaximal norm |U_e1|²⁼²/3 (ε_1) and the μ–τ balance |U_μ1|=|U_τ1| (ε_2) — and shows that including the first JUNO result the data treat them asymmetrically: ε_1=+0.014±0.010 (consistent with zero at 1.4σ) while ε_2=+0.29⁺⁰.07_-0.13, large in central value but disfavoring zero only at 1.5σ because the profile likelihood in δ is shallow. A TM_1 neutrino sector with the electron-row condition |U_e2|/|U_e3|=2+√(3) fixes sin²θ_13=(2-√(3))/12=0.02233 and sin²θ_12=0.31811; a single charged-lepton 2–3 rotation (angle θ_e≃-1.9^∘, phase forced to α=0 by flavon alignment in an S_4×C_4×C_3×C_2 realization) generates ε_2=sin2θ_ecosα and pins δ=272^∘±2^∘, with ε_2=-0.066 — opposite in sign to the measured central value.

Why it matters: the framework is unusually falsifiable. The predicted δ sits 1.7σ from the current central value on the present profile likelihood, and Hyper-Kamiokande’s 20^∘ design precision resolves it at 3σ; a confirmed second octant (δ≈177^∘) would exclude it at >4σ. Caveat: the rigid mass sum Σm_ν=65.6 meV sits at/just beyond the DESI ΛCDM bound (64.2 meV), requiring dynamical dark energy if cosmology tightens; m_ββ=5.4 meV is below current 0νββ reach.

item.title: The Challenge of Detecting Quantum Nature of Gravitational Waves
item.dc:creator: Yu Miyauchi et al.
item.description:
Working with Gaussian states and a linear single-mode detector coupling, Miyauchi et al. use a squeezing witness W=|M|-N (W>0 certifies sub-vacuum quadrature variance impossible for any coherent-state mixture) to track whether source squeezing survives projection onto the detector-accessible wave-packet mode. Three source scenarios all fail: inflationary two-mode squeezing reduces to a thermal marginal (W_A=-N_A<0); a single-mode-squeezed stochastic background has random phases across coherence patches, washing out |M_A|; an isolated source is suppressed geometrically by W_A≤ΔΩ(ℓ_eff+1)²/8π, giving ΔΩ∼(3 km/100 Mpc)²∼10⁻⁴² for ground detectors unless emission is collimated to ℓ_eff≳10²¹.

They then show source squeezing is inessential: a pre-squeezed detector state acquires a positive witness W⁽Q)_b̃<sin²ϵ/2 from a quantized wave even when the incident mode is unexcited, whereas a classical c-number field only displaces the detector (W⁽C)_b̃=0). But the witness is throttled by the graviton–detector coupling ϵ̅=h_QG/h_th, which their strain-sensitivity table gives as ∼10⁻¹⁷–10⁻³³ across nHz–THz; detection needs ϵ≳N_trial⁻¹/4, and coherent integration (ϵ∝√(ωT)) reaches only ∼10⁻⁸.5 for a THz signal over a year.

Why it matters: this is the second no-go in two weeks, explicitly extending the Bao et al. (2607.27313) coarse-graining/weak-transfer argument to gravitational waves. The detector-squeezing loophole is real but doesn’t defeat the coupling suppression — the program’s wall is confirmed from another direction. Caveat: results are restricted to Gaussian states and linear single-mode coupling, which the authors argue is the optimistic case.

item.title: Combination of Higgs boson measurements at √s = 13 TeV and their interpretations by the ATLAS experiment
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
(Abstract only available.) ATLAS combines its full Run 2 (up to 140 fb⁻¹) Higgs measurements into a single reference, reporting an inclusive signal strength of 0.990⁺⁰.053_-0.051 — split as ±0.027 (stat.), ±0.024 (exp.), ⁺⁰.037_-0.035 (sig. theo.), ⁺⁰.016_-0.015 (bkg. theo.). The signal-theory term, dominated by missing higher-order QCD and parton-shower modelling, is now the leading uncertainty, so precision is theory-limited rather than statistics-limited. Sensitivities improve up to 35% over the previous combination. Combining single-Higgs and HH rates gives κ_λ=1.3⁺³.1_-1.6 ([-1.5,6.5] at 95% CL); the on-/off-shell rates yield Γ_H=3.6⁺².1_-1.6 MeV; and the H→bb̅ partial width delivers a first ATLAS running b-mass at the Higgs scale, m_b(m_H)=2.73⁺⁰.27_-0.25 GeV (MSbar). Kinematics are probed via STXS in 44 regions and interpreted in SMEFT.

Why it matters: this is the document every future coupling, self-coupling, and width comparison will cite, closing out the incremental HH/tH updates the memory has tracked. The signal strength sitting on unity at percent-level with theory now dominant sharpens where the community must invest — better fixed-order and shower predictions rather than more luminosity. The b-mass extraction demonstrates the Higgs as a running-mass probe. Caveats are structural: κ_λ and Γ_H remain broad, and the width relies on the on-/off-shell interpretation with its model assumptions.

item.title: Cosmic birefringence from a joint analysis of ACT and Planck
item.dc:creator: Johannes R. Eskilt
item.description:
Eskilt performs the first joint isotropic-birefringence fit to ACT DR6 and Planck DR4 polarization, exploiting cross-power spectra between the two experiments — which break the α+β miscalibration degeneracy in independent ways (Planck via Galactic foreground EB, ACT via optics-model priors on α, probing only ℓ>600). Sampling 17 miscalibration angles, three dust-EB amplitudes, and one β, the baseline gives β=0.277^∘±0.057^∘, excluding zero at 4.8σ. Crucially, positive EB appears in all three blocks separately: ACT×ACT (0.207^∘±0.073^∘), ACT×Planck (0.178^∘±0.078^∘, 2.3σ), and Planck×Planck (0.387^∘±0.094^∘). A conservative dust-mitigation test — masking Planck to 30% Galactic cut, keeping only ℓ>600, dropping foreground-dominated bands — still yields 0.236^∘±0.067^∘ at 3.5σ, so recovering β=0 requires both the α priors and the dust-EB model to fail simultaneously.

Why it matters: a frequency-independent β≠0 is the signature of an axion-like field coupled to electromagnetism via a Chern-Simons term — parity violation beyond ΛCDM, a direct window on the dark sector. Two independent hints now cross-correlate into the strongest signal yet. Caveats are candidly stated: the ACT×ACT block fits poorly (PTE 0.1%, an unexplained PA5 f090/f150 angle discrepancy the ACT team flagged), there is 1.5σ Planck–ACT tension in preferred β, the HFI priors are pre-flight, and the author’s pipeline underestimates ACT EB errors by ~7%. Unresolved systematics preclude a firm cosmological conclusion.

item.title: Laboratory-frame T-matrix and heavy quark drag in the quark-gluon plasma
item.dc:creator: Anurag Tiwari et al.
item.description:
Tiwari and He solve the in-medium two-body T-matrix directly in the medium rest (laboratory) frame rather than the pair center-of-mass frame, where the standard partial-wave reduction assumes the total pair-momentum P⃗ dependence is negligible. Since a thermal medium breaks Lorentz invariance and defines a preferred frame, physical observables must be built from lab-frame amplitudes. Exploiting the residual azimuthal symmetry about the P⃗-axis, they decompose the five-dimensional scattering equation into uncoupled integral equations for azimuthal components T_m, making it numerically tractable. For charm–light-quark scattering (m_Q=1.3 GeV, m_q=0.4 GeV, T=190 MeV, screened Cornell potential), the lab- and CM-frame amplitudes coincide at P=0 but diverge sharply as P grows: in non-forward regions |T_CM|² overshoots by 40–150% at P=1–1.5 GeV, and the relativistic normalization R_E further distorts the forward peaks. Folded into the drag coefficient, the lab-frame result exceeds the CM baseline by 25–30% at T=190 MeV (low p_Q) and 30–40% at T=258 MeV across most momenta.

Why it matters: heavy-quark drag is the key transport parameter extracted from charm-hadron flow to characterize the near-ideal QGP. A previously unquantified 25–40% frame-mismatch bias directly reduces the theory uncertainty in inferring QGP transport properties — a concrete tightening. Caveats: the calculation uses constant quark widths (Γ=100–200 MeV, itself a 20–30% spread) rather than a self-consistent spectral function, treats only heavy–light-quark (not quark–gluon) scattering, and has not yet been propagated through Langevin transport to observables.

item.title: Baryogenesis via the CKM Matrix with Minimal Flavor Violation
item.dc:creator: Innes Bigaran et al.
item.description:
Bigaran, Krnjaic, Langhoff and Xiao construct an explicit counterexample to the folklore that SM CP violation is too small for baryogenesis. The model adds a scalar leptoquark 𝒮∼(3̅,1)_1/3×3_d̅ whose baryon- and lepton-violating couplings are built entirely from Yukawa spurions under MFV, so the only CP phase is the Jarlskog invariant J. Flavor breaking splits the three 𝒮_i masses (m_i²⁼M²⁽¹⁺γy_d_i²⁾), which lets tree–propagator interference in 𝒮_i decays generate a CP asymmetry per decay that peaks near resonance at ϵ_1^max≈0.15 — vastly above the naive Y_B∼10⁻²⁰ estimate. Crucially, no time-varying parameters are needed, distinguishing it from Mesogenesis. Two cosmologies are offered: low reheat (T_RH<130 GeV) with non-thermal 𝒮 production, requiring m_𝒮≲10¹¹ GeV; or high reheat with right-handed-neutrino ΔL=2 washout converting B+L into surviving B-L, viable for ϵ_i≳10⁻⁷.

Why it matters: it directly challenges the “SM CP violation is insufficient” verdict that motivates much BSM baryogenesis, and anchors the digest’s flavor/CP top-down thread. The honest caveats are prominent: the vertex-correction contribution vanishes and the entire asymmetry rides on the propagator term, which dies at mass degeneracy; the B-L-preserving decays require an extra ingredient (a late-decaying scalar or RH neutrinos) to escape sphaleron washout; and proton decay forces M≳10¹⁴ GeV for electron couplings (relaxed to ∼6×10⁹ GeV for τ). The authors explicitly frame it as a proof of principle, not a classified model.

item.title: Photon-nucleon entanglement in Compton scattering at low and high energies
item.dc:creator: Yoshitaka Hatta et al.
item.description:
Hatta and Martínez-Fernández extend the collider quantum-information program to elastic Compton scattering, treating the final photon helicity and nucleon spin as two qubits. Their central analytic result is a no-go theorem: in unpolarized scattering off any spin-12 target with real amplitudes, the partially-transposed density matrix cannot have a negative eigenvalue, so no entanglement is possible — proven generally, extending an earlier numerical electron-only observation. To generate entanglement they turn to polarized initial states. Below the pion threshold (ω<140 MeV) all six helicity amplitudes are real, yet with polarized beams they find a rich pattern of maximally entangled Bell states (and unitary equivalents, including a cyclic-anticorrelation Ψ^↻) distributed across the (θ,ω) plane, with proton and neutron showing distinct structure. They also compute the high-energy wide-angle regime at NLO in pQCD via GPD-based soft form factors, where an 𝒪(α_s) imaginary part gives entanglement everywhere but never maximal (λ_min≈-0.36 at best).

The striking physics point is diagnostic: for the neutron, where the Thomson term is absent, the electric and magnetic polarizabilities α_Eⁿ,β_Mⁿ control not just the pattern but the very existence of entanglement — setting α_Eⁿ⁼β_Mⁿ⁼⁰ makes the (x̂,x̂) configuration separable. This positions entanglement as a probe of nucleon EM structure, measurable at MAMI, JLab and a future EIC. Caveat: measuring final-state spin correlations is acknowledged as experimentally challenging, and the free-neutron extraction relies on deuteron subtraction, left to future work.

item.title: Three-baryon femtoscopy as an effective 3→3 scattering experiment
item.dc:creator: ALICE Collaboration
item.description:
ALICE measures the three-proton correlation function in 13.6 TeV pp collisions (Run 3, 53.1 pb⁻¹, with dedicated software triggers selecting triplets at Q_3<1.4 GeV/c, found once per 30000 minimum-bias events). A data-driven decomposition isolates the genuine p–p–p signal (79% of triplets) from Λ/Σ⁺ feed-down and misidentification backgrounds, with the source size ρ_0=(2.54±0.04) fm fixed by the companion two-proton measurement (r_0=1.27 fm). Comparison to hyperspherical-adiabatic three-body continuum calculations (AV18 + Coulomb, three-body force negligible by Pauli blocking) reproduces the data at n_σ=2.5. The headline sensitivity result: removing the NN p-wave interaction produces a 22.2σ disagreement, proving the correlation function resolves the partial-wave structure of the nuclear force. Two novel continuum signatures emerge — the nuclear interaction stays relevant up to grand-angular momentum K≤7 (far slower convergence than the two-body case, since large K still admits pairs in l_x=0), and the correlation stays above unity as it approaches the uncorrelated limit, the first experimental signature of an effective long-range attraction (∝ζ/ρ³, with ζ tied to the two-body scattering length).

This establishes femtoscopy as a genuine 3→3 scattering experiment and gives the first direct access to the isospin-3/2 three-body continuum, previously reachable only in isospin-1/2 via nucleon–deuteron scattering. Caveats acknowledged by the collaboration: the three-body Coulomb problem is treated approximately (no exact solution), feed-down modeling could be sharpened, and the 2.5σ agreement leaves room for theory improvement. The clear payoff is extension to p–p–Λ, p–p–Σ, p–p–Ξ for the strangeness sector.

item.title: A Bayesian approach to the long-baseline neutrino oscillation sensitivity of DUNE
item.dc:creator: DUNE Collaboration et al.
item.description:
DUNE recasts its established sensitivity inputs (the same flux, GENIE-based cross-section, and detector models as the 2020 TDR) into a Bayesian MCMC framework using MaCh3, with Adaptive Metropolis proposal tuning (~50× fewer steps than manual tuning, further reduced ~15× by 5% downsampling). This is explicitly not an updated sensitivity but a demonstration of what the Bayesian treatment adds. Two payoffs stand out. First, four-dimensional posteriors expose the strong sin²θ₂₃–sin²θ₁₃ correlation, producing two well-separated octant lobes; applying a reactor short-baseline θ₁₃ constraint post hoc via prior reweighting yields “a significant increase” in θ₂₃-octant sensitivity — the reactor prior breaks the appearance-channel degeneracy that otherwise smears the octant. Second, and the headline, this is the first study of DUNE’s sensitivity to the Jarlskog invariant J, a parametrization-independent CP measure derived trivially as a posterior of the sampled parameters. Studies span NuFIT 6.0 (NO, lower octant) and T2K-NOvA (IO, upper octant) Asimov points, δ_CP = 0, −π/4, −π/2, at 200 and 1000 kt-MW-yr.

Why it matters: it establishes the machinery for parametrization-independent CP inference and flexible constraint incorporation as DUNE moves toward real data, where robust systematic propagation and derived-quantity posteriors become essential. Caveats are honestly flagged: results are Asimov-based, mass-ordering sensitivity is not evaluated (assumed >5σ), θ₁₂ and Δm²₂₁ are fixed by Gaussian priors (no solar samples yet), and the ND is found to be systematics-limited with the current CC-inclusive binning.

item.title: Moving a Detector to Probe New Neutrino Interactions: IWCD at Hyper-Kamiokande
item.dc:creator: Thomas Schwemberger et al.
item.description:
Schwemberger and Takhistov reframe the movable IWCD not as a systematics-control tool but as an interaction spectrometer: sliding the same 300-ton water Cherenkov detector through the J-PARC off-axis beam (1°, 2.5°, 4°, peaking at ~1.0, 0.6, 0.4 GeV) exposes one target/apparatus to distinct incident spectra while keeping detector and interaction uncertainties correlated. Using the NCQE/CCQE event-rate ratio R^θ — in which common normalization largely cancels — they show that combining positions breaks vector-axial and normalization degeneracies that a single spectrum cannot, because the vector-axial interference term B carries a distinct energy dependence. Combining three positions with a 5% correlated normalization benchmark, they project 95% CL NSI sensitivities of −0.07 ≲ ε^{uA}{μμ} ≲ 0.06, −0.10 ≲ ε^{uV}{μμ} ≲ 0.12, and −0.05 ≲ ε^{udL}_{μμ} ≲ 0.05. Axial NC NSI, which do not contribute to the coherent matter potential, are the key complementary target to oscillation and high-energy scattering probes; the left-handed CC coefficient, which merely rescales CCQE, benefits little from multiple positions.

Why it matters: it gives movable/multi-position detectors a genuinely new physics use — spectroscopy of interaction structure — extensible to single-pion channels and other beams. Caveats are substantial and acknowledged: the analysis retains only the dominant ν_μ component, treats oxygen as an incoherent free-nucleon sum with a hard Pauli-blocking cutoff (yielding NCQE rates above NEUT), adopts an 80% flat NCQE efficiency and a schematic 5–10% systematic, and for light mediators the low-Q² cutoff removes most position-dependent discriminating power.

item.title: The QCD Axion and Neutrino Masses
item.dc:creator: Hridoy Debnath et al.
item.description:
Debnath, Fileviez Pérez, and Miller perform a unified analysis identifying the PQ-breaking scale with the neutrino-mass-generation scale (M_seesaw ~ v_S ~ f_a) across both DFSZ and KSVZ, for six mechanisms: Type-I/II/III seesaw, the Zee model, and colored seesaw I/II. For each they compute the E/N anomaly ratio and hence g_aγγ. Within DFSZ, Type-I, Type-II and Zee leave E/N unchanged from the minimal model (new fields are singlets or scalars), whereas Type-III’s fermionic electroweak triplets shift E/N (8/3→11/3 for DFSZ-I, 2/3→5/3 for DFSZ-II) — a measurable g_aγγ signature. In KSVZ, colored seesaw I and II predict E/N = 0 and 16/9, giving g_aγγ^I/g_aγγ^II ~ 14. A robust generic prediction across all frameworks is a derivative axion-neutrino coupling ∝ m_ν/f_a. If the axion is dark matter, a→νν decays produce a monochromatic flux peaked at E_ν = m_a/2 lying above both the CNB and solar thermal fluxes, with branching ratios and lifetimes sensitive to the neutrino mass ordering.

Why it matters: it ties the strong-CP solution, neutrino mass, and dark matter to one scale and yields correlated, testable handles — future haloscopes (ADMX, JWST bounds already excise parameter space), a distinguishing g_aγγ per mechanism, and a PTOLEMY-adjacent neutrino signal. Caveats: the axion-neutrino couplings are enormously f_a-suppressed, the neutrino-flux detectability is “very challenging,” and the seesaw–PQ identification is an assumed upper bound on f_a rather than a forced relation.

item.title: The Forward Neutrino Flux and its Secondaries at a 10 TeV Muon Collider
item.dc:creator: Ju-Yeol Choi et al.
item.description:
Using a purpose-built Monte Carlo (MINT) that propagates and decays muons through a realistic IMCC hybrid lattice (v0.9 straight section + v0.6 arcs), Choi et al. characterize the forward ν flux from the ±180 m straight sections around the IP. The headline: ∼7×10¹⁸ ν+ν̅/year through a benchmark 3.2-tonne, 43 g/cm² fiducial volume at 5 km, giving 𝒪(10⁹⁾ neutrino-nucleus interactions/year plus ∼5×10⁵ ν-e scattering events. Crucially, the beam divergence (𝒪(0.1–1) mrad) dominates over the intrinsic 1/γ∼0.02 mrad opening angle, washing out the “prism” energy-angle correlation claimed in preliminary studies — a concrete correction to earlier flux modeling. Secondary muons from CC interactions in upstream rock give ∼2 penetrating, >99.9%-polarized muons (⟨E_μ⟩≃1.2 TeV) per bunch crossing per detector — a background overlapping the neutrino signal in time, but also a potential wide-band polarized TeV muon source. Secondary ν_τ (charm, ITD, tridents, D_s^*) yield only ∼0.2 CC events/year: unobservable.

Why it matters: this is the concrete simulation behind today’s neutrino-factory framing, quantifying both the physics opportunity (electroweak precision, HNL searches reaching |U_μN|²≃2×10⁻¹¹ near 15 GeV, dipole couplings to ∼4×10⁻¹⁰ GeV⁻¹) and the radiation/background reality. Caveats are stated plainly: the lattice is optimized for luminosity, not neutrinos; the BSM reach curves are event-yield targets before backgrounds and efficiencies; and recovering the prism effect would need a ~100× larger β-function. Results are declared compatible and complementary to the independent Burk et al. study.

item.title: Collider Spin Tomography with Missing Neutrinos
item.dc:creator: Tengyu Ai et al.
item.description:
Ai et al. recast spin tomography under invisible particles as a coarse-grained POVM on the production density matrix, proving that information loss is governed by the kernel of the visible-data map, not by the number of kinematic solutions. Applied analytically to e⁺e⁻→τ⁺τ⁻→π⁺π⁻νν̅, the twofold ambiguity leaves exactly one unidentifiable direction: the antisymmetric transverse correlation C_nr-C_rn. The differential rate, both polarization vectors, and the remaining fourteen spin coefficients are all recoverable from the pion distribution alone. They build a template-free, self-consistent fixed-point unfolding where fold weights are set by the data-reconstructed density matrix rather than a flat 50/50 average. Closure tests on 10⁸ events (∼9.3 ab⁻¹) show the flat average is visibly biased even in the production-angle distribution, while iterations converge to truth on the identifiable subspace — confirmed in both SM and a deliberately large anomalous tau-dipole benchmark (a_τ=0.01-0.02i), proving it is not an SM template fit. Power-iteration/Arnoldi analysis pins the sole marginal (λ≃1) mode to C_nr⁻, with the next eigenvalue ≃0.96 (contracting).

Why it matters: this extends the collider-quantum-information program (following the tt̅ tomography flagged two days ago) to final states with missing energy — tau pairs, but also, they note, fully leptonic WW and dileptonic tt̅. Entanglement/CHSH claims survive: concurrence and CHSH are reported as positivity-constrained intervals over the null direction, still yielding truth-consistent sensitivity. Caveat: the clean one-dimensional kernel is specific to the πν channel; multi-hadron modes require numerical POVMs, and results are closure tests, not full sensitivity projections with detector effects.

item.title: Measurement of forward jet suppression in Pb+Pb collisions at √(s_NN)=5.02 TeV with ATLAS
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
(Abstract only.) ATLAS reports the first inclusive jet R_AA at forward rapidity in heavy-ion collisions, for anti-k_t R=0.4 jets with p_T>74 GeV in 2.8<|y|<3.2 and 3.2<|y|<3.6, using 1.72 nb⁻¹ Pb+Pb and 255 pb⁻¹ pp at 5.02 TeV. Jets are significantly suppressed; suppression increases monotonically from peripheral to central collisions with only mild p_T dependence. The key comparison: suppression is stronger in 2.8<|y|<3.2 than in the previously measured central region |y|<2.8. In the most forward bin (3.2<|y|<3.6) the precision is insufficient for a conclusive statement.

Why it matters: forward jets probe more asymmetric parton kinematics — different flavor mix (more quark-initiated, higher-x), different path geometry, and different local medium density — so the stronger-than-central suppression is a genuinely new lever on parton energy loss, complementing today’s small-system QGP thread (ALICE OO strangeness, weekend Υ/charm-v_2 results). Caveat visible in the abstract: the most-forward bin’s limited statistics leaves the extrapolation of the trend to |y|∼3.4 open, so the flavor/geometry interpretation rests mainly on the 2.8<|y|<3.2 interval.

item.title: Measurement of the Hubble constant with high-energy neutrinos
item.dc:creator: Gonzalo Herrera et al.
item.description:
The first-ever H_0 determination from astrophysical neutrinos: Herrera, Kamp and Argüelles build a distance ladder from 12 X-ray–selected Seyferts with IceCube per-source excesses, exploiting the disk-corona relation L_ν=κL_X^β. NGC 1068 (Cepheid+TRGB, 10.93±0.74 Mpc) anchors the absolute scale; the 11 Hubble-flow sources supply H_0 through the d_L²⁽β-1) lever arm that only exists when β≠1. Re-extracting signal counts from the 14-year public point-source data with SkyLLH and profiling κ analytically, they find H_0=49⁺⁴⁰_-30 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ and β=0.67⁺⁰.16_-0.25, with the calorimetric β=1 disfavored at ∼2σ — the first population-level slope measurement, pointing to subcalorimetric coronae (Bethe-Heitler or synchrotron suppression).

Why it matters: this is a genuinely new distance rung immune to dust, absorption, scattering and radiative-transfer systematics — the entire error budget lives in source physics. As the digest frames it, it proposes a new rung rather than kicking away an old one. Caveats are candid and severe: the H_0 uncertainty is enormous and consistent with both Planck and SH0ES at 1σ; the value swings dramatically with the NGC 1068 intrinsic luminosity choice (H_0=109⁺²⁹_-37 if the high value is adopted) and with adding NGC 4151 as a second anchor (to H_0≈109, a ∼15% residual tension the authors attribute to intrinsic L_ν–L_X scatter). Selection on neutrino significance can also imprint a spurious correlation. IceCube-Gen2 could reach σ(H_0)≈16–20.

item.title: Combination of vector boson scattering measurements in leptonic final states at √(s)=13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS delivers its most comprehensive VBS combination: seven analyses over the full 138 fb⁻¹ Run 2 dataset, spanning same-sign and opposite-sign WW, WZ, ZZ, plus semileptonic WV/ZV channels, fit simultaneously across 48 phase-space regions and 1525 bins. A 4-POI model returns signal strengths all consistent with unity — μ_SSWW=1.05⁺⁰.15_-0.14, μ_OSWW=1.11±0.20 (6.4σ), μ_WZ=1.21⁺⁰.28_-0.25 (7.0σ), μ_ZZ=1.15⁺⁰.44_-0.37 (4.0σ) — with the combination sharpening OSWW and WZ uncertainties by up to 15% over the best individual inputs. A charge-separated 6-POI model probes the expected production charge asymmetry from the proton’s valence content, finding μ_W⁺W⁺⁼¹.13⁺⁰.17_-0.16 versus μ_W⁻W⁻⁼⁰.84⁺⁰.28_-0.24.

Why it matters: this is the consolidated stress-test of the electroweak-scattering program, coherently accounting for cross-channel correlations that single measurements cannot — the reference point against which unitarity-violating BSM effects in longitudinal boson scattering would appear as event excesses. Everything is SM-consistent, so it functions as a benchmark and a clean baseline for the EFT/anomalous-coupling recasts that follow. No tension is flagged; the correlations among signal strengths are mild.

item.title: Modification of Υ production in pO and OO collisions at LHCb
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
Abstract only. LHCb measures Υ(2S) and Υ(3S) yields relative to Υ(1S) in pp, pO, and OO collisions. The pp ratios match earlier LHCb results; pO shows only slight relative suppression of the excited states, but OO suppresses the Υ(2S) by a factor of ∼2, with evidence for Υ(3S) suppression. The jump from a small pO effect to significant OO suppression is read as the onset of additional mechanisms — color screening in a deconfined medium — with QGP-formation models successfully describing the OO data.

Why it matters: alongside ALICE’s charm-sector v_2 splitting, this pushes the “how small can QGP be” question onto real Run 3 oxygen data, with sequential melting appearing in a system this small. The caveat, visible even from the abstract, is disentangling cold-nuclear-matter effects from genuine deconfinement screening — the pO reference is precisely what makes the OO excess interpretable, but the model dependence of the QGP interpretation remains.

item.title: Observation of a Charged Charmoniumlike Structure in e⁺e⁻→D⁰D⁻π⁺⁺c.c.
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration
item.description:
BESIII performs a partial-wave analysis of e⁺e⁻→D⁰D⁻π⁺ on 1667 pb⁻¹ collected at √(s)=4682 MeV, using combined single- and double-tag reconstruction. A near-threshold enhancement in the D⁰D⁻ system, modeled with a Flatté lineshape, requires J^P=1⁻ and yields mass (3794.7±6.0±8.7) MeV/c² and D⁰D⁻ coupling (1.6±0.2±0.2) GeV. The raw fit significance is 7.7σ; after 320 pseudo-experiments account for the look-elsewhere effect and systematics are folded in, it settles at 5.3σ — enough to claim observation of this new charged charmoniumlike state, X(3790)⁻. Cross-checks (alternative J^P<4, added PHSP or non-resonant amplitudes) leave the signal at ≥8σ when nuisance components are included. The analysis simultaneously updates the excited charmed mesons, with new D_2^(2460), D_1^(2600) and D_1^*(2760) parameters.

Why it matters: this is the first isovector state seen coupling to a (DD̅)^± pair — a channel previously argued unlikely, since spin-parity conservation forbids the DD̅π vertex under pure pion-exchange binding, yet phenomenology and lattice predict a scalar DD̅ bound state. A charged 1⁻ structure right at threshold extends the Z_c/X(3872) molecular narrative into a new final state and constrains heavy-quark-symmetry partner counting.
