Caveats: the fit fraction is small (1.3±0.3%), systematics on mass are large (±8.7 MeV), and the Flatté parameterization plus fixed D_3^(2750) and D̅^0-width inputs carry model dependence; the state’s nature (molecule vs. threshold cusp) is not resolved here.

item.title: Gravity Probe-DM: The Gravitational Laboratory for Dark Matter
item.dc:creator: Yu-Dai Tsai et al.
item.description:
Tsai and Foote propose a purely gravitational Solar-System dark-matter search exploiting the irreducible downstream wake the Sun’s gravity carves into any incident unbound DM flow. Two precision-ranged spacecraft act as a heliocentric gradiometer: a uniform acceleration cancels, but the wake tidal tensor projected along the baseline does not. For a LISA-like 2.5×10⁶ km baseline crossing a 0.1 AU coherent width at 30 km/s, a one-percent density excess gives a raw uniform-core range response of only 0.63 pm over the 5.77 d crossing. Because the free response grows as T² while the projected tide stays coherent, an axial “wake-skimming” arc lifts this to 2.5 nm over one year; an optimistic low-lag dark-disk benchmark (20% of local density, 30% focused contrast) reaches ~15 nm. REBOUND/REBOUNDx integrations validate the linear-in-density scaling and the ω̇∝M_od precession law.

Why it matters: existing planetary/asteroid-ephemeris bounds only limit smooth, near-spherical DM around the Sun; this concept instead targets an anisotropic, directional structure tied to the Galactic flow, giving a distinctive turn-on/turn-off tidal waveform and, for wave DM, de Broglie-scale interference. A detection would be the first Solar-System gravitational DM map and would calibrate the local phase-space model underlying direct detection. Caveats are substantial and stated plainly: nanometre signals sit beneath solar/planetary/asteroid tides, radiation pressure and thermal recoil; the T² enhancement requires a passive one-year dwell that is unavailable near 1 AU without going to several AU; and every number is a pre-fit response scale, not a demonstrated sensitivity. LISA Pathfinder archival data is proposed only as a methodological null test.

item.title: Quantum Tomography of Top Quarks as a Probe of Charge-Parity Violation
item.dc:creator: Eren Erdogan et al.
item.description:
Erdogan et al. compute the first fully renormalized one-loop Higgs-induced correction to the tt̅ production spin density matrix from a CP-mixed top-Yukawa coupling ℒ=-(m_t/v)h t̅(a_t+ib_tγ_5)t, predicting its imprint on all fifteen Fano coefficients. The couplings enter at 𝒪(y_t²/16π²⁾; CP-odd effects are linear in a_tb_t and populate specifically the antisymmetric correlation C_nr⁻ (dispersive) and the polarization difference P_k-P̅_k (absorptive), none of which shift the cross section. On-shell renormalization forces imaginary top field-renormalization constants ∝a_tb_t — the first complete renormalized CP-odd density matrix. Confronting CMS’s full 15-parameter tomography with its covariance, they find at a_t=1 the bound -1.40<b_t<1.23 (95% CL, inclusive Fano fit), tightening to -1.01<b_t<1.26 when spin and m_tt̅-shape information are combined — comparable to ATLAS’s |b_t|≈1.1 from tree-level tt̅H/tH.

Why it matters: this converts the collider quantum-information program from demonstrating entanglement/magic to a genuine precision measurement, using the reconstructed quantum state itself as the observable. The method is model-agnostic — any operator shifting the density matrix can be confronted with the same tomography without regenerating events. Caveats: the SM sits within 68% CL, so this is a constraint not a hint; the bound assumes all other new physics decouples from the loop; and the existing binning was optimized for quantum-property studies, so finer m_tt̅ bins near threshold — where Higgs corrections peak — would sharpen sensitivity. Two mirror minima under (a_t,b_t)→(-a_t,-b_t) remain unresolved.

item.title: A measurement of the Higgs boson mass in the diphoton decay channel in proton-proton collisions at √(s)=13 TeV
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS pins down m_H=125.13±0.15 GeV (±0.10 stat±0.12 syst) using the full 138 fb⁻¹ Run 2 diphoton sample — a near factor-of-two systematic reduction over their 2020 result. The key advance is the photon energy scale: rather than extrapolating electron scales from Z→ee via simulation (previously the dominant uncertainty), they now measure residual electron-photon differences directly from Z→μμγ FSR photons, and apply fine-grained E_T-dependent resolution corrections that bridge the gap between Z-electron energies (≈45 GeV) and H→γγ photons (≈60 GeV). The leading systematics are now the Z→μμγ sample statistics (74 MeV), muon momentum scale (55 MeV), and high-E_T non-linearity (54 MeV). The signal strength μ=0.95±0.06±0.07 is SM-consistent.

Why it matters: this is the most precise single-channel m_H to date, a direct input to EW global fits and vacuum-stability arguments. Combined with CMS 7+8 TeV diphoton data it gives 125.06±0.14 GeV. One visible caveat: the 13 TeV value sits 1.2σ above the earlier CMS 7+8 TeV combination, and the result remains systematics-limited, with further gains tied to the statistically starved Z→μμγ calibration sample.

item.title: The Very Nearly Right Theory of Flavor
item.dc:creator: Nima Arkani-Hamed et al.
item.description:
(Abstract only.) Arkani-Hamed et al. parametrize the ten-dimensional space of quark flavor data using “nine-link textures” — full-rank Y_u,d matrices with nine total nonzero entries and a single CP phase. Fitting all such textures, they find the CP phases cluster tightly around multiples of π/8, driven by a “Yukawa triangle” defined by the matrix entries that coincides with the unitarity triangle at leading order in small flavor parameters. The empirical observation being explained is that (α,β,γ)≈(π/2,π/8,3π/8). Crucially, the two triangles differ beyond leading order, yielding calculable deviations from these values that the next generation of unitarity-triangle-angle measurements can decisively confirm or exclude.

Why it matters: this turns a striking numerical coincidence into a falsifiable framework, and lands one day after Lin’s geometric CKM reparameterization — two independent attacks on the same pattern. A bonus: the textures are sparse with naturally real determinants, which combined with spontaneous CP violation offers a route to solving strong CP. Caveat: as abstract-only, the robustness of the “clustering” claim and the size of the predicted deviations relative to projected experimental precision cannot be assessed here.

item.title: Suppressed Quantum Effects of Weakly Coupled Waves
item.dc:creator: Yunjia Bao et al.
item.description:
Bao et al. prove two general obstructions to detecting nonclassicality in weakly coupled waves (axion DM, gravitational radiation), using the cavity haloscope as worked example. First, detectors couple not to fundamental plane-wave modes but to a coarse-grained “effective mode”; if DM occupies many independent modes, the quantum central limit theorem drives the effective-mode P-function to a nonnegative thermal Gaussian, erasing negativity regardless of occupancy. They show convergence is rapid — the purity of 𝒩 coarse-grained Fock states approaches the Gaussian value 1/(1+2n) as ∼n(n+1)/[𝒩(2n+1)²], fast even for n∼1. Second, even granting a maximally nonclassical effective mode, all nonclassicality signatures carry extra powers of the tiny conversion efficiency η=sin²⁽gt_m)∼10⁻²¹: Mandel Q_c=ηQ_a≥-η, squeezing S_c=ηS_a. Distinguishing a Fock from a coherent axion via number statistics needs N_shot∼1/η², i.e. t_int≳10¹⁷ yr — utterly impractical and unenhanced by large N_eff.

Why it matters: this is a general no-go closing off the recent high-profile “quantize gravity from GW observations” program, and the cold-water counterpart to yesterday’s Blas–Oller GW→γγ claim. Distinguishing classical states (coherent vs. Gaussian) remains feasible, needing only N_shot∼1/⟨n_c⟩². Caveat honestly flagged: the CLT can be evaded — few contributing modes (fuzzy DM, condensates), surviving inter-mode correlations, or highly monochromatic late-time sources with TΔω≲1 — though even then the η-suppression persists unless quantum resources scale as 1/η.

item.title: Anomalies in Hadronic B→VV Decays
item.dc:creator: Bhubanjyoti Bhattacharya et al.
item.description:
Bhattacharya et al. extend last year’s charmless B→PP SU(3)_F puzzle to the vector-vector modes, fitting HFLAV/PDG data with reduced matrix elements (equivalently topological diagrams) in the exact SU(3)_F limit, the only theoretical simplification being neglect of the small Wilson coefficients c_7,c_8 (a ~10% effect). Three fits are staged. The isospin-only B→ρK^ fit is acceptable (χ²/d.o.f.=3.6/3, p=0.31) — but forces |P_uc/P_tc|∼200, some 300× above the expected ≲0.5; imposing the physical constraint ≤1 collapses it to 4.4σ. The combined SU(3)_F fit over V∈{ρ,K^} gives 39.2/5, a 5.2σ discrepancy; adding ϕ,ω pushes it to 130/20, p<10⁻¹⁵, i.e. >7σ. The jump is driven partly by ℬ(B⁰→ϕK^0) and ℬ(B⁰→ωK^0) (each contributing >20 to χ²) and by the failure of f_L≫f_T in the new modes sharpening tension with ΔS=1 polarization data.

If it holds, this is a hadronic-amplitude anomaly distinct from the b→sℓℓ/νν̅ FCNC anomalies — a breakdown of the SM’s flavor-symmetry structure in tree/penguin dominated decays. The result’s strength is its minimal theory input; its acknowledged vulnerability is that only exact SU(3)_F was tested. The authors concede that whether realistic ~30% SU(3)_F-breaking can absorb a 7σ gap “must be checked,” though they judge it unlikely. Robustness was verified with three independent codes and tens of thousands of seeds.

item.title: First Search for Quirks at the LHC with FASER
item.dc:creator: FASER Collaboration
item.description:
FASER delivers the first LHC quirk search, using 186 fb⁻¹ of 13.6 TeV pp data (2022–2024). Quirks — pairs charged under a QCD-like infracolor SU(N_IC=2) with right-handed-lepton SM charges — are Drell-Yan produced forward, remain bound by an unbreakable IC string, and arrive at FASER (480 m downstream) slow and out-of-time. The signature is a pair depositing ~2 MIPs of charge in all eight scintillators with reconstructed speed 0.6<β<1 and arrival time t_0 offset from the nominal bunch. Backgrounds (through-going muons via an ABCD estimate, muon-induced “kinked” showers) total well below one event; the signal region contains zero observed events. Using a CL_s fit, masses up to 179 GeV are excluded at Λ=10 keV, and for the first time weak-scale quirk masses are excluded across the broad range 300 eV<Λ<100 keV.

This opens a genuinely new frontier: non-Abelian hidden sectors (motivated by neutral naturalness and IC-glueball dark matter) had no prior dedicated LHC search, only the DØ Tevatron limit. FASER’s forward, low-background geometry turns the quirks’ slowness into a clean discriminant. Caveats are honest and intrinsic: only ~0.03–0.04% of produced quirks reach the fiducial region, with reconstruction/selection efficiency ~1% (10%) at m_𝒬=50 (175) GeV, and the signal normalization carries a ~25% ISR/FSR modeling uncertainty (up to 28% simulation-statistics uncertainty at small Λ). This is half of Run 3, so reach will grow.

item.title: Improved HH→bb̅τ⁺τ⁻ Analysis with 196 fb⁻¹
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
(Abstract only.) ATLAS updates its non-resonant di-Higgs search in bb̅ττ, combining 140 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV with 56 fb⁻¹ at 13.6 TeV plus reconstruction and analysis improvements. The signal strength is μ_HH=2.6⁺¹.4_-1.0, an observed (expected) significance of 2.6 (1.2)σ over background-only, and 1.65σ above the SM prediction — a mild upward pull consistent with the SM. The self-coupling modifier is constrained to κ_λ∈[-3.4,1.6]∪[5.5,10.1] observed ([-1.7,8.5] expected) at 95% CL. As validation, ZH and ZZ in the same final state are measured at 3.5 (2.4)σ and 1.8 (2.7)σ respectively.

The result advances the HH program incrementally: the tightened κ_λ interval sharpens the constraint on the Higgs potential, while the ~2.5× SM central value continues a pattern of slight excesses in this channel worth tracking as Run 3 statistics accumulate. The excess is modest — the SM lies comfortably within 1.65σ — so no anomaly is claimed. The validation channels demonstrate the method’s control, though the observed ZH pull sits above expectation and ZZ below, indicating the measurements remain statistics-limited.

item.title: High-energy neutrino emission from the Milky Way
item.dc:creator: R. Abbasi et al.
item.description:
Abstract only. Combining all three neutrino-flavor event morphologies with updated ice modelling, calibration and reconstruction over 12 years of IceCube data, a predefined global analysis establishes high-energy neutrino emission from the Galactic plane at 5.7σ. A follow-up study identifies the inner Galaxy as a prominent source: 217 shower events above 5 TeV visible energy against an expected background of 154.4 ± 4.1. The multi-flavor approach is what pushes this over the discovery threshold — earlier IceCube plane hints leaned on cascades alone.

Why it matters: this is the constructive counterpart to the week’s UHE-neutrino tension thread. The diffuse Galactic component is precisely the background assumed in the ANITA/KM3NeT-vs-IceCube joint fits, so having it in hand at >5σ tightens those interpretations while opening Galactic multi-messenger astronomy — cosmic-ray propagation and neutrino properties probed over kiloparsec baselines. As an abstract-only entry, the systematic treatment of the diffuse-emission modelling (which sets whether the inner-Galaxy excess is source-like or propagation-driven) can’t be assessed here.

item.title: Observation of electroweak γγjj production at 13 TeV in 140 fb⁻¹ with ATLAS
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
Abstract only. ATLAS observes the electroweak production of two isolated photons plus two jets at 6.2σ, with a fiducial cross section of 13.8⁺³.0_-2.6 fb, sitting below but consistent with the SM prediction of 17.1 ±2.4 fb. Fiducial and differential cross sections are measured for both the EW-only and combined QCD+EW γγjj processes, and the data are interpreted in EFT, setting limits on several dimension-8 Wilson coefficients parameterising anomalous quartic gauge couplings.

Why it matters: this extends the ATLAS electroweak-boson program — following recent WZjj polarization and ZZ work — into a new VBS-adjacent channel, using the same dim-8 aQGC language that is now the default for these searches (and the framework Yilmaz et al. project forward to FCC-hh). The measured central value ~20% below SM is within the ~2 fb uncertainties, so no tension, but the modest downward pull is the kind of thing differential distributions and more data will need to pin down.

item.title: Gravitational waves decay in vacuum: a low-energy effect of quantized gravitation
item.dc:creator: Diego Blas et al.
item.description:
Blas and Oller argue that GWs, treated as coherent graviton states rather than classical fields, decay into photon pairs via graviton fusion (gg→γγ, Skobelev amplitude) — a process forbidden classically and semiclassically, vanishing as ħ→0, and enhanced by the graviton number squared N². The key technical point (Supplement SA): the coherent-state mode cannot propagate in the internal graviton line because momentum conservation forces it on-shell at s=0, where the derivative coupling vanishes. The radiated power scales as W_γ∝G² E_rel²ω_s²σ_ω², giving a compact form W_γ=350π(r_m/ℓ)²ħω². They derive first constraints on recurrent GW populations from CMB μ/y distortions (COBE/FIRAS: |μ|<9×10⁻⁵, |y|<1.5×10⁻⁵), UV/X-ray and γ-ray backgrounds, and D/⁴He photofission, all cast as bounds on √(Γ) ϵE_rel/M_⊙ vs ω_s.

Why it matters: a genuinely new, purely quantum-gravitational handle on GW sources, whose detection would evidence quantized gravity. The honest caveat is front and center: for astrophysical binaries the photon luminosity is minuscule (comparable to Hawking radiation of the equivalent mass, number luminosity ∼10⁶ s⁻¹ at merger), and SGWB depletion is negligible (∼10⁻¹¹⁰ m⁻³s⁻¹; |Φ|≈10⁻²⁵ Hz⁻¹ to the GUT scale). Only in ultralight-dark-matter scenarios, where huge occupation numbers boost gg↔ϕϕ, do rates reach ∼10⁵⁴ s⁻¹ — and that requires the exotic light-scalar sector to exist.

item.title: Precision measurements of D⁰→π⁻ℓ⁺ν_ℓ and D⁺→π⁰ℓ⁺ν_ℓ (ℓ=e,μ)
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
Using 20.3 fb⁻¹ at √(s)=3.773 GeV and the double-tag technique, BESIII measures all four D→πℓν modes to record precision. The branching fractions land at (2.950±0.017±0.017)×10⁻³, (2.817±0.037±0.019)×10⁻³, (3.622±0.034±0.018)×10⁻³, and (3.507±0.043±0.026)×10⁻³ for the π⁻e, π⁻μ, π⁰e, π⁰μ channels respectively — a factor 2–3 improvement over the previous BESIII results, which are superseded. A simultaneous fit of partial rates in ten q² bins yields f_+^D→π(0)|V_cd|=0.1425±0.0005±0.0003 (sub-percent), giving |V_cd|=0.2262±0.0008±0.0005±0.0018_LQCD or f_+^D→π(0)=0.6339±0.0024±0.0014 depending on which external input is assumed. First forward-backward asymmetries are extracted, and a first scalar-current search gives Re(C_S^μ)=0.022±0.023±0.003, consistent with zero.

Why it matters: this tightens one rung of the CKM ladder (c→d) on the same day the digest highlights kaon-to-B propagation, and the null scalar current directly constrains the two-Higgs-doublet/leptoquark scenarios invoked for the b→c LFU anomalies — here in a clean, SM-consistent charm transition. LFU is tested via μ/e rate ratios across q². Caveat: the |V_cd| extraction is now dominated by the lattice form-factor uncertainty (±0.0018_LQCD versus ±0.0008 statistical), so further gains require theory, not more data.

item.title: Off-shell Higgs boson measurements: Yukawa couplings, self-coupling, compositeness, and width
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
(Abstract only.) CMS analyzes off-shell Higgs production in the four-lepton channel with 138 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV, combining H→ZZ and H→WW to extract Γ_H=5.1⁺².0_-1.8 MeV and exclude the no-off-shell hypothesis at >5σ. The analysis delivers several firsts: a direct test of composite-Higgs models with Λ_H>870 GeV at 95% CL, the first off-shell constraint on the Higgs self-coupling, and — combined with on-shell data — the tightest light-quark Yukawa limits to date while relaxing the usual bound on the HVV coupling for more model-independent width results.

Why it matters: the off-shell region breaks the coupling-vs-width degeneracy that plagues on-shell rate measurements, and folding in BSM loop content and modified vector couplings makes the Γ_H determination more robust than earlier off-shell extractions. The compositeness and self-coupling handles are novel uses of the same dataset. Caveat: no methodological detail is available beyond the abstract, so assumptions behind the model-independence claims cannot be assessed here.

item.title: Implications of K→πνν̅ for new physics in B decays
item.dc:creator: Lukas Allwicher et al.
item.description:
Allwicher and Bordone propagate the new NA62 ℬ(K⁺→π⁺νν̅)=9.6⁺¹.9_-1.8×10⁻¹¹ (sub-20% precision) into two BSM frameworks. In the modified-Z-coupling scenario, under Minimal Flavor Violation B_s→μμ dominates the constraints, while under Partial Compositeness the kaon mode becomes the sharpest handle on right-handed couplings δg_R — even resolving a two-fold solution that B→Kνν̅ then breaks. Both give effective NP scales Λ^Z_eff≳8 TeV, tree-level accessible at HL-LHC. In the alternative U(2)⁵ semileptonic fit with third-generation dominance (Λ_eff≳1.8 TeV), the more precise NA62 value now admits an ϵ∼0 / C_ℓq⁻∼0 SM-like solution at 68%, though in mild tension with R_D⁽) and B→K⁽)νν̅; the preferred large-BSM branch predicts ℬ(K_L→π⁰νν̅)/ℬ(K⁺→π⁺νν̅)∼1.5 (normalized to SM), within the Grossman–Nir bound.

Why it matters: this is exactly the cross-mode phenomenology the digest has tracked since the NA62 result — one kaon branching ratio now feeds correlated predictions for B→K⁽*)νν̅, B_s→μμ, and future K_L→π⁰νν̅ (KOTO II). The framework makes K_L a genuine prediction, testable by combining projected NA62 (15%), KOTO-II (25%), and Belle II (8%) precision. Caveat: the persistent B⁺→K⁺νν̅ central value sits above all predictions, and the two green fit lobes remain equally allowed at current precision — conclusions hinge on which branch nature picks.

item.title: First Lattice QCD Determination of Lepton-Flavor-Universality Ratios in Light-Meson Leptonic Decays
item.dc:creator: Peter Boyle et al.
item.description:
(abstract only) Boyle et al. deliver the first lattice QCD+QED calculation of the structure-dependent (SD) radiative correction to R_e/μ — the electron-to-muon leptonic-width ratio — for both π and K, working at the physical pion mass and in the continuum limit. Using the infinite-volume reconstruction method with Coulomb-gauge photons to suppress statistical noise and finite-volume effects, they obtain SM predictions R_e/μ^π= 1.23501(10)×10⁻⁴ and R_e/μ^K = 2.47653(34)×10⁻⁵ — sub-permille precision on the previously dominant hadronic uncertainty.

Why it matters: R_e/μ is a benchmark LFU test, and the O(0.1%) SD correction was the limiting theory input as PIONEER and NA62 push toward matching precision. This calculation supplies exactly that ingredient from first principles, replacing model-dependent estimates. It is the SM number those experiments will now quote against. As an abstract-only entry, the systematic budget of the continuum/QED extrapolations isn’t visible here, but the quoted errors already sit well below current experimental sensitivity.

item.title: Boosted H→ττ cross-section measurements with ATLAS
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
(abstract only) ATLAS reports evidence for Higgs production at p_T^H > 300 GeV in the di-hadronic-τ final state, combining full Run 2 (140 fb⁻¹, 13 TeV) with a partial Run 3 sample (162 fb⁻¹, 13.6 TeV). Standard hadronic-τ reconstruction loses efficiency when the two τs collapse into a single large-radius jet, so the analysis deploys dedicated boosted di-τ reconstruction and identification plus multivariate discriminants. The inclusive boosted measurement reaches observed (expected) significance of 3.8 (3.3)σ — evidence-level.

Why it matters: this extends H→ττ sensitivity into a high-p_T regime that probes the Higgs coupling structure and is sensitive to BSM contributions that grow with momentum transfer. Results are cast in the simplified-template-cross-section framework, with differential p_T^H measurements for gluon fusion and an inclusive VBF cross section — directly usable for EFT interpretation. The observed significance modestly exceeds expectation, consistent with SM within the still-limited boosted statistics.

item.title: Scattering Amplitudes as Programs: Self-Evolving Search for Theory and Event Generation
item.dc:creator: Yi Gu et al.
item.description:
Gu and Krippendorf treat amplitude evaluation as a program-search problem: a repository-scale coding agent (OpenAI Codex) acts as mutation operator inside an external generate–evaluate–select loop with frozen correctness gates and objectives, evolving executable amplitude programs. Three benchmarks. (1) Scaling: from a BCFW seed, search rediscovers Berends–Giele currents, then CSW, then a fixed-k split-helicity transfer dynamic program with O(n) source work, hitting an 805× geometric-mean speed-up over 34 timing cells. (2) Structural: NMHV rational forms are reorganised into R-invariant-style cells and glued supercells, lifting a cancellation-conditioning score from 0.376 to 0.605 and collapsing 8–13 terms to 2–3. (3) Tree complexity: across twenty QCD/EW processes, exact arithmetic falls 47.7× (geometric mean 11.68×), with a 5.9× post-hoc Python runtime gain. In matched pure-gluon tests (n=4→6), the evolved engine’s lead over a Sherpa-Comix exact-sum call grows 10×→277×, while its gap to -O3-compiled MadGraph Fortran narrows 77.7×→13.7×. Total cost: 115 candidates, ~$112, 8.15 agent-hours.

Why it matters: with HL-LHC projections assigning ~20% of ATLAS CPU to event generation, matrix-element kernels are a real bottleneck, and this shows agent-driven search can traverse genuine changes of representation — not just tuning — with fully archived, inspectable lineages. This is the digest’s “agents orchestrating” thread made concrete. Caveats are stated plainly: these are tree-level, single-stack, isolated-kernel benchmarks; the Comix comparison targets exact colour/helicity sums (Comix can sample), no symbolic divisibility proof accompanies the gluing, and native generator integration plus end-to-end throughput remain untested.

item.title: A converged architecture for processing 32 Tbps of physics data in real-time at the LHCb experiment
item.dc:creator: Roel Aaij et al.
item.description:
The upgraded LHCb now reads out its entire detector — roughly 30 MHz of non-empty pp collisions, 32 Tbps — with no hardware low-level trigger, a factor-40 increase in data rate over the previous system. The engineering result: the full stream is filtered in real time on just 164 nodes (2× AMD EPYC 7502, 2× NVIDIA RTX A5000 each), applying a 30:1 reduction in HLT1 entirely on GPU. The design rests on three moves: commercial-off-the-shelf networking (an InfiniBand HDR fat-tree treating event-building as an all-to-all personalized exchange), second-scale host-memory buffering that eliminates incast without deep-buffer switches, and a “converged” node hosting readout, event-building, and GPU filtering together via zero-copy/RDMA. Algorithmically, a multi-event GPU scheduler batches ~600–800 events per sequence, with mixed-precision reconstruction (single precision for a truncated-region Kalman filter; half precision for VELO storage and SciFi seeding). They report 41 MHz peak combined throughput, 36% headroom over the 30 MHz requirement, and demonstrate a full EB+HLT1 integration test sustaining 160 GB/s memory and 115 GB/s PCIe per node with no performance drops.

Why it matters: this is the production endpoint of the month’s real-time-reconstruction wave (the July 17 GPU-Kalman work), and the comparison table makes the claim concrete — the highest software-processed data rate of any experiment, exceeding ATLAS/CMS (1.6 Tbps into software after a 300× L1 cut) and ALICE (7.2 Tbps). Removing the low-level trigger reduces selection bias by considering the whole event. It’s an engineering demonstration paper rather than a physics measurement; the throughput figures are commissioning-phase benchmarks.

item.title: What could an emerging Big Bang Nucleosynthesis discrepancy be hinting at?
item.dc:creator: Vivian Poulin et al.
item.description:
Using PRIMAT (rewritten in Python) with the Cooke et al. deuterium measurement (10⁵D/H = 2.527±0.030), the BBN-inferred baryon density ω_b ≃ 0.0219 sits ~2.1σ below the ΛCDM CMB value and ~3.1σ below the higher ω_b = 0.02272±0.00014 preferred in EDE fits — early-dark-energy solutions to H₀ generically raise ω_b and thus worsen the deuterium problem. The authors test three expansion histories against the EDE ω_b target: ΛCDM, a ΔN_eff extension, and a transient “very early dark energy” (vEDE) component peaking during deuterium burning. Constant extra radiation fails (Q_DMAP = 3.1σ, ΔAIC ≃ +1.2): it raises Y_p too efficiently at weak freeze-out. vEDE succeeds, because a boost localized at T_D ≃ 0.03 MeV shortens the residual deuterium-burning window (raising D/H at large ω_b) while barely touching ⁴He synthesis. The combined fit gives ΔH/H(T_D) = 0.087⁺⁰·⁰³⁶₋₀.₀₃₇, no residual tension (Q_DMAP = 0.7σ, ΔAIC ≃ −5.3).

Why it matters: this is the natural referee’s-follow-up to the H₀ World Cup — the very models that win on H₀ lose on primordial deuterium, and the resolution demands yet another light scalar, framed as an axiverse window at the BBN epoch. Caveats are candidly stated: the CMB is compressed to a single Gaussian ω_b likelihood (not a joint fit); nuclear-rate uncertainties enter only through tabulated MC errors; the discrepancy is partly rate-driven (PArthENoPE agrees better with the data), and the updated D/H = 2.508 softens the ΛCDM tension to 2.7σ.

item.title: Hubble tension: the shape wall
item.dc:creator: Miguel A. Sabogal et al.
item.description:
The standard no-go against late-time H₀ solutions is a normalization wall (BAO fixes r_d·H₀). This paper erects an independent shape wall: at fixed acoustic scale θ_s and sound horizon, δH₀/H₀ ≃ δI/I, where I ≡ ∫dz/E(z). Using Gaussian-process reconstructions of the dimensionless expansion rate E(z) from unanchored SNeIa (PantheonPlus, DESY5Dvk, Union3) and DESI DR2 BAO — marginalizing over the r_d·h amplitude to retain only shape information — they find E(z) can deviate at most ≈5–7% from fiducial ΛCDM. The directly-constrained low-redshift integral I_< (z ≲ 2.3) is pinned to the percent level: δI_</I_< ≲ 0.5% (68%), ≲1.5% (95%) across SNeIa+BAO combinations, mapping to (δH₀/H₀)_< ≲ 0.8% at 95%. Adding a model-guided estimate of the unconstrained high-z tail I_> (from ΛCDM/wCDM fits) yields a total δH₀/H₀ ≲ 2% (conservative) to ≲3.7% (maximally permissive) — versus the ≈9.3% needed to close the tension, leaving ≳4.3σ residual.

Why it matters: alongside Poulin et al., this is the day’s second wall against tension-solvers, and it is statistically stronger than the normalization wall since it survives redshift-independent BAO recalibration. The key methodological point — pointwise E(z) envelopes overstate freedom because integrating I preserves cross-redshift correlations — is well argued. Honest caveats: I_> bounds are model-dependent (not nonparametric); flat FLRW, smoothness, and the distance-duality relation are assumed. The explicit surviving loophole is new physics at z ≪ 0.01, below SNeIa reach.

item.title: Evidence for longitudinally polarised Z bosons in electroweak W^±Zjj production
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description:
Abstract only. ATLAS reports 4.0σ evidence for a longitudinally polarised Z in electroweak W^±Zjj production, combining 140 fb⁻¹ at 13 TeV and 164 fb⁻¹ at 13.6 TeV in the fully leptonic (e/μ) channel. The integrated fiducial fraction is f_X0=0.32±0.09, consistent with the NLO-EW Standard Model prediction. Upper limits at 95% CL of 0.19 and 0.12 are set on longitudinally polarised W and on doubly-longitudinal WZ events, respectively. The 13.6 TeV fiducial cross-section is measured as 0.374±0.077 (stat)±0.053 (syst)±0.009 (lumi) fb per lepton flavour.

Why it matters: This is the direct sequel to last week’s doubly-longitudinal ZZ observation, extending the electroweak-symmetry-breaking polarization program into the VBS-adjacent WZjj sector — the channel most sensitive to longitudinal-boson scattering that probes unitarization by the Higgs. That the single-longitudinal Z fraction sits squarely on the SM prediction, while the doubly-longitudinal component remains only bounded (<0.12), reflects the statistical reach of current datasets rather than any tension. The caveat is intrinsic: a 4.0σ result on f_X0 with ±0.09 precision and the merged two-energy dataset means the harder doubly-longitudinal target awaits Run 3 luminosity.

item.title: First Measurement of the Relative Phase between Proton Psionic Form Factors
item.dc:creator: BESIII Collaboration et al.
item.description:
What they did: Using 10.09×10⁹ J/ψ events, BESIII measured the normal polarization 𝒫_y of protons from e⁺e⁻→J/ψ→pp̅ by exploiting secondary pp elastic scattering off hydrogen in the beam-pipe mineral-oil layer and MDC inner wall — turning the spectrometer itself into a polarimeter. Requiring a third track (the knocked-out target proton), vetoing quasi-free nuclear collisions via |p_target|<50 MeV/c, they isolate 2556 elastic events (15.2% efficiency) and extract, via the SAID analyzing powers, sinΔΦ=-0.20±0.34_stat±0.11_syst — the first determination of the relative phase between the proton’s psionic (complex G_E^ψ, G_M^ψ) form factors.

Why it matters: The relative TL-region phase had been unreachable for nucleons, which lack self-analyzing decays; hyperons (Λ, Σ, Ξ) had been mapped but the proton and neutron remained blank. Placing the proton near Σ⁺/0 and below Λ, Ξ⁻/0 gives a first SU(3)-symmetry test point. The method — validated by a pseudo-experiment recovering an injected sinΔΦ=-0.84 as -0.82±0.02 — is reusable at any large-acceptance spectrometer, with Σ⁻ and (with better neutron detection) the neutron as obvious next targets. Caveats: the result is statistics-limited and consistent with zero; two ΔΦ solutions remain degenerate, resolvable only with a polarized beam (𝒫_x) or antiproton polarization, e.g. at STCF.

item.title: Four, One, and None: Quantifying the UHE Neutrino Anomaly Across ANITA-IV, KM3NeT, and IceCube
item.dc:creator: Dibya S. Chattopadhyay et al.
item.description:
What they did: Chattopadhyay, Argüelles, and Brdar perform the first joint statistical fit of the four near-horizon ANITA-IV events, the single KM3-230213A event, and IceCube’s null result, using semi-analytic energy-, direction-, and time-dependent effective areas for all three detectors with realistic exposures (26.6 d for ANITA-IV, 287 d for ARCA-21, 5400 d for IceCube). For a common diffuse power-law flux, no normalization/spectral-index choice reproduces the observed (4,0,1) counts: the best fit predicts ~5 events at IceCube and 𝒪(10⁻³⁾/𝒪(10⁻¹⁾ at ANITA-IV/KM3NeT, a 7.5σ tension (7.9σ for fixed E⁻²). Modeling rare all-sky transients, with the probability of four favorable ANITA-IV overlaps fixed to ∼10⁻⁴ and scanning 10⁵ MC realizations, the least-anomalous benchmark (185 sources, 10-day duration) still leaves 5.9σ.

Why it matters: This converts the qualitative ANITA/KM3NeT-vs-IceCube “puzzle” into a hard number, sharpening the KM3-230213A thread. Crucially, the tension is driven by ANITA-IV, not KM3NeT: the ANITA-IV–IceCube-only fit gives 5.8–7.8σ, while KM3-230213A alone is a mild 1.8–2.5σ. The authors conclude neither diffuse flux nor rare identical transients works within the SM, pointing to structured source populations, detector/classification effects, or new physics. Caveats: the effective areas are semi-analytic, reproducing collaboration values only within a factor ~2 near the horizon; the trigger-efficiency parametrization and spherical detector approximation (especially for the anisotropic ARCA-21) carry acknowledged modeling uncertainty.

item.title: Dark matter searches with a 13 meV threshold superconducting sensor array
item.dc:creator: Christopher Albert et al.
item.description:
QUALIPHIDE-FIR ran a 41-pixel array of aluminum microwave kinetic inductance detectors (MKIDs) — FIR astronomy photon-counters, peak-tuned at 25 µm/50 meV — as a dual-mode dark matter search with a 13 meV threshold, the lowest yet in a direct-detection experiment. The array couples to a gold-plated spherical dish (5163 mm²) that converts hidden-photon DM into real photons collected at the focus; four on-focus pixels see any signal while 37 off-focus pixels build a data-driven background model, giving genuine discovery potential rather than upper limits only. A blind analysis of 22 hours found no excess (peak local significance 1.33σ at 82 meV), setting the strongest hidden-photon kinetic-mixing limits over 13–90 meV, reaching χ = 1.5×10⁻¹² at 50 meV and improving on prior terrestrial bounds above 90 meV by >20×. The same Al inductors serve as scattering targets: with 1.33 ng·day exposure and the optimal-interval method, the search reaches DM masses of 5 MeV (nuclear) and 20 keV (electronic), roughly an order of magnitude below QROCODILE’s 0.11 eV threshold, carving out new sub-overburden parameter space.

Why it matters: this is the diversifying-detection theme with real limits, opening the meV “THz gap” where cavity and TPC methods fail. The 13 meV threshold also probes the low-energy-excess background at single-phonon energies (below Al’s ~41 meV maximum) for the first time. Caveats are honest: the dominant efficiency systematic η₀ = 0.46±0.06 lumps uncharacterized losses; resolution above 70 meV is uncalibrated (treated as a single counting bin); and the projected scattering sensitivity assumes an aggressive 1000× background reduction, versus the ~10× already demonstrated.

item.title: Prospects for K_L→π⁰νν̅, K_S→μ⁺μ⁻, K_L→π⁰ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ and ε'/ε after the new K⁺→π⁺νν̅ result from NA62
item.dc:creator: Monika Blanke et al.
item.description:
Abstract only. Blanke et al. take yesterday’s NA62 result — a K⁺→π⁺νν̅ branching ratio (2016–2024 data) fully consistent with the precise SM prediction — and ask what room remains for its neutral counterpart. The answer: with suitably large new complex phases and a small right-handed s̅d coupling added to the left-handed structure, K_L→π⁰νν̅ can still be enhanced by an order of magnitude relative to the SM while keeping both K⁺→π⁺νν̅ and ε_K SM-like. In the same scenario K_S→μ⁺μ⁻ (LHCb) and K_L→π⁰ℓ⁺ℓ⁻ (KOTO II) are strongly enhanced and the Dual-QCD ε’/ε anomaly is removed, illustrated with a specific Z’ model.

Why it matters: this is the direct phenomenology sequel to the NA62 golden-mode measurement, showing that an SM-like charged channel does not close the door on KOTO II’s discovery target — the golden K_L mode retains up to tenfold enhancement. The construction is explicitly a proof-of-existence within a chosen Z’ framework, and hinges on tuning new phases plus right-handed currents; the authors note the final NA62 result (2016–2026) could still shift.

item.title: Astrophysical Neutrino Sources as Colliders
item.dc:creator: Carlos A. Arg\"uelles et al.
item.description:
Argüelles et al. present a recipe to extract two-sided bounds on the inelastic pp and pγ cross sections from neutrino point sources by independently pinning every astrophysical input — cosmic-ray luminosity (bounded above by Eddington/relativistic-beaming limits, below by the power needed to sustain observed neutrino and X-ray fluxes) and target column density (from X-ray spectroscopy, Thomson depth, or variability) — leaving σ as the only free parameter. Applied to IceCube’s TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, the Galactic plane, the stacked 11-source Seyfert population, and KM3NeT’s 220-PeV KM3-230213A, the bounds span √(s)∼1 GeV to ∼10⁵ GeV. Concrete bands: TXS 10-year data gives σ_pp≃0.5–70 mb at √(s)≃0.9–2.8 TeV; the Seyfert stack gives σ_pp∈[2.3,70] mb and σ_pγ∈[0.08,9] mb with the smallest astrophysical uncertainties. Dedicated Pythia 8 simulations revise the per-flavor neutrino energy fraction upward to ξ_ν^pp≃0.086–0.099, ~1.8× the canonical leading-pion estimate, relaxing lower bounds by nearly 2×. Several bounds are more stringent than the Froissart–Martin unitarity limit, and pγ constraints reach beyond HERA’s √(s)≃209 GeV.

Why it matters: it reframes neutrino telescopes as flux-based hadronic colliders scanning continuously in √(s), complementary to the shape-based (flux-independent) Auger air-shower method and to collider fixed points. The SM cross section sits inside every band — a nontrivial consistency check. Caveats are prominent: band widths (factors of ~30) are set by astrophysical systematics, not neutrino statistics; TXS relies on an upper-bound-only column density and requires super-Eddington CR power even after beaming correction; and KM3/UHE bounds are projections under a “standard-candle” idealization awaiting source association.

item.title: Measurement of the branching ratio of the K⁺→π⁺νν̅ decay
item.dc:creator: NA62 Collaboration
item.description:
NA62 reports ℬ_2023-2024(K⁺→π⁺νν̅)=(7.2⁺².3_-2.1)×10⁻¹¹ from 33 candidates against 22.9±1.1 SM signal and 12.0⁺².9_-2.2 background events, then combines with 2016–2022 to obtain (9.6⁺¹.9_-1.8)×10⁻¹¹ — 20% precision and consistent with SM predictions near 8×10⁻¹¹. Across 2016–2024, 84 observed events against 30⁺⁴_-3 background give background-only rejection exceeding 6σ, and the SM-observation significance passes 5σ for the first time. The 2023–2024 data were taken at lower intensity (440 MHz vs. the 580 MHz design max), sitting on a broad signal-per-spill maximum around 450 MHz where DAQ dead time and accidental vetoes are balanced; this improved the random-veto efficiency by 1.14 and roughly halved several relative backgrounds. New deep-learning tools — a transformer-based 4D GTK tracker (false-track rate 13%→4%, purity 87%→97%) and a ResNet-based calorimetric π/μ classifier (~2% higher pion ID, 40% lower μ→π misID) — sharpen the selection. A KTAG upgrade to H_2 radiator cut material budget from 3.9% to 0.7% X_0.

Why it matters: this is now the world’s most precise handle on the theoretically cleanest FCNC kaon mode (SM intrinsic uncertainty ~3%, dominated by long-distance charm), and it lands squarely on the SM. The dominant background remains upstream (accidental K⁺/π matching), estimated fully data-driven with ~30% uncertainty. NA62 expects a further ~50% more signal events after 2025–2026 running.

item.title: First Observation of an Exotic Reggeon (G. D. Alexeev (for JPAC Collaboration) et al.)
item.description:
(Abstract only.) COMPASS presents high-statistics measurements of peripheral ηπ⁻ and η’π⁻ production in π⁻ p→η⁽’)π⁻ p, performing for the first time an unbinned analysis of the high-mass region to disentangle the exchange mechanisms governing production. They report the first observation in high-energy scattering of an exotic Reggeon, at significance exceeding 5σ in both channels, most likely related to the spin-exotic π_1(1600).

Why it matters: this establishes a production-side foothold for the π_1 spin-exotic program, complementing the decades of resonance-spectrum work. Where earlier analyses focused on identifying the exotic state in the produced system, disentangling the exchange mechanism gives independent evidence that exotic quantum numbers propagate in the t-channel — a genuinely new handle on QCD’s exotic sector. As only the abstract is available, the details of the exchange decomposition and systematic treatment cannot be assessed here.

item.title: Theoretical uncertainties in reconstructing model parameters with gravitational waves from supercooled phase transitions
item.dc:creator: Maciej Kierkla et al.
item.description:
Taking the classically conformal U(1)_X model as representative of strongly supercooled transitions, the authors scan {g_X,M_X} over 𝒪(10⁴⁾ points and compute GW spectra with two nucleation-rate schemes: a 4D daisy-resummed potential with dimensionally-estimated prefactor, and a full NLO calculation (two-loop 3D-EFT matching plus exact scalar and vector fluctuation determinants, “NLOdet”). Injecting the resulting signals into LISA and running a Fisher-matrix reconstruction of the fundamental parameters, they find the daisy scheme strongly disfavored: the two methods disagree by 𝒪(10%) in the reconstructed gauge coupling g_X, an order of magnitude larger than the daisy RG-scale ambiguity (𝒪(1%)) and more than an order of magnitude above the sub-percent Fisher reconstruction uncertainty. The hierarchy is δ_g^exp∼δ_g^μ̅,NLOdet≪δ_g^μ̅,daisy≪δ_g^meth∼𝒪(10%). Crucially, no reasonable RG-scale choice reconciles daisy with NLOdet — contradicting a recent claim that scale-shifting suffices — because the discrepancy stems from genuinely missing higher-order physics (the scale-shifting gauge modes require exact determinants, not a derivative expansion). M_X is essentially unaffected, since it just sets the low-T Hubble scale.

Why it matters: this extends the digest’s recurring message — GW “signals” from first-order transitions hinge on poorly controlled non-equilibrium/thermal inputs. For high-SNR LISA targets, theoretical diligence, not detector sensitivity, limits the inverse problem. Caveats: dynamical prefactor uses the no-damping approximation (neglecting back-reaction), and the hierarchy inverts in the lower-SNR PTA band.

item.title: Track fitting at the full LHC collision rate
item.dc:creator: Pierre Billoir et al.
item.description:
(Abstract only.) LHCb deployed a fast parameterised Kalman filter in the first trigger stage from the 2025 run, fitting charged-particle trajectories at the full 30 MHz collision rate on ~500 GPUs. The trick is to replace magnetic-field-map lookups and numerical integration with analytical parameterisations while keeping the Kalman mathematical framework intact. Against the previous partial fitter it delivers a factor-of-two improvement in D⁰ and J/ψ invariant-mass resolution (from improved momentum resolution), greater robustness to misalignment, and more than doubled rejection of accidental tracks at no loss of genuine-track efficiency — for only a 2% processing-time increase.

Why it matters: this is real-time reconstruction crossing from R&D into production in an all-software trigger, the hardware counterpart to the month’s ML-trigger work. Sharper online mass resolution and background rejection directly widen what LHCb’s first stage can select and store, a template for HL-LHC-era triggering. As an abstract, the numbers are headline-level; the underlying validation (efficiency turn-ons, systematics of the parameterisation across the field volume) isn’t visible here.

item.title: A Precise Determination of the Shape of the Proton's Gluon Cloud from HERA data
item.dc:creator: Tobias Toll et al.
item.description:
(Abstract only.) An analytic leading-twist calculation of coherent and incoherent exclusive J/ψ photoproduction cross sections in the hotspot model is fit to all H1 and ZEUS diffractive data, yielding χ²/ndf=0.77. The extracted gluon-cloud profile has a perturbative Gaussian core of 0.105(1) fm sitting inside a non-perturbative exponential halo of 0.220(2) fm — a two-scale structure the authors report as independent of x_Pom or hotspot number, with a stable energy dependence α’_eff=0.046(19).

Why it matters: a clean, tightly-fit picture of the proton’s small-x gluonic transverse structure, resolving core from halo, is exactly the input the EIC structure program needs, and the excellent fit lends the hotspot framework credibility as an interpretive tool. As an abstract, the key caveats — leading-twist/leading-order treatment and the model-dependence of the incoherent-to-fluctuation mapping — can’t be assessed from the text provided.

item.title: Searching for the N-naturalness tower of neutrinos
item.dc:creator: Sofia Lonardi et al.
item.description:
First experimental test of the N-naturalness neutrino tower, via a global fit of public data (Daya Bay, GERDA, LEGEND-200) plus projections (JUNO+TAO, LEGEND-1000) in the Newtrinos.jl framework. The model solves the hierarchy problem with N dark sectors of varying Higgs mass, encoding residual fine-tuning in a parameter r (r=1 = no tuning); implemented via the many-mixing-partners mechanism, it generates suppressed neutrino masses and a tower of extra light states that distort oscillations and shift m_ββ. Numerically diagonalising the full N-sector mass matrix (avoiding the perturbative breakdown at small N), they set 90% CL contours. For Majorana neutrinos, current GERDA+Daya Bay data already exclude non-fine-tuned scenarios (r=1) up to N=10⁴ for both orderings — killing the tidy N=10⁴ GUT-unification benchmark that let the framework address the hierarchy problem without ad-hoc tuning. JUNO+TAO projections push lower bounds to N≳500 and require r≲0.1 in 500≤N≤10⁴.

Why it matters: it converts a “no-fine-tuning” selling point into a falsified benchmark using existing neutrino data, exactly the constraining mood of today’s DM-and-naturalness cluster. Caveats are honestly flagged: the Dirac case is far weaker (no 0νββ handle, excluded only to N∼50); results assume m_0=0.01 eV and η=1+1/N; and m_ββ rests on a single benchmark set of nuclear matrix elements (varied only for robustness checks).

item.title: The H_0 World Cup II: A comprehensive competition between proposed Hubble tension solutions
item.dc:creator: Nils Sch\"oneberg et al.
item.description:
(Abstract only.) An updated systematic bake-off — the sequel to the “H_0 Olympics” — subjecting fourteen representative alternatives to ΛCDM to a common analysis of current CMB (ACT/SPT), BAO (DESI) and Type Ia SN data, now with the Hubble tension quoted above 7σ. The contenders span four mechanisms: late-time expansion modifications, modified recombination, extra pre-recombination radiation, and early non-radiative energy injection. Every model is scored with both Bayesian and frequentist tension/performance metrics, with the neutrino mass sum left free, and tested for whether adding curvature or CPL dark energy improves the fit. Leading contenders face a robustness gauntlet: alternative CMB likelihoods and multipole cuts, different SN samples, LSS information, and BBN constraints.

Per the digest, the verdict favors early dark energy and early modified gravity (shifting H_0 toward 70 and cutting the SH0ES residual to ∼2.5–3.6σ), places varying-electron-mass models intermediate, and finds enhanced-radiation and late-time scenarios failing to beat ΛCDM. Why it matters: it converts a scattered literature of individual tension “solutions” into a refereed, common-framework ranking — the reference tournament model-builders will cite, with Paper II’s robustness tests being the operative part. The honest caveat is intrinsic to any such contest: conclusions depend on the chosen dataset combination and priors, which is precisely why the robustness suite is included; results not visible here beyond the digest summary.

item.title: Dark Energy and Neutrino Flavor from the Weak Axion
item.dc:creator: Pedro Bittar et al.
item.description:
Bittar and Wagner identify dark energy with a “weak axion” — the phase of a complex scalar carrying the SM’s anomalous U(1)B+L charge — and show its potential can be radiatively stable at the meV scale. Electroweak-instanton contributions come out ∼10 orders of magnitude too small (Λ_inst⁴≃(6×10⁻⁶ eV)⁴|c_BL|³), so the dominant potential arises from two inequivalent Weinberg operators generating an axion-dependent Majorana mass. A spontaneously-broken S_3 lepton permutation symmetry enforces the orthogonality condition Tr[M_Φ^†M⋆]=0, which simultaneously kills the quadratic divergence and the leading T_ν² m_ν² thermal force, pushing the first axion-dependent Coleman-Weinberg term to quartic order in neutrino masses. The amplitude vanishes in the exact tribimaximal limit, so the observed departure sets the scale: Λ_ν≃2.3 meV√(|cosδ_CP/0.52+sin(θ_23-π/4)/0.055|), landing in the 1–4 meV range for current oscillation data.

Why it matters: this is a rare falsifiable quintessence model — the dark-energy scale becomes a prediction from PMNS parameters, with δ_CP accounting for ∼80% of the variance, so Hyper-K/DUNE directly test it. It also predicts m_ββ≃1.5–3.7 meV (below next-gen reach) and behaves as instability-free thawing quintessence for f∼M_pl. Caveats, stated frankly: it does not address the cosmological-constant problem (vacuum energy assumed zero), faces a “severe axion-quality problem” requiring |ΔV_UV|≲ρ_DE, and needs near-Planckian f — treated as low-energy assumptions rather than derived. NuFit and long-baseline (T2K/NOvA) best-fits currently map to different Λ_ν.

item.title: Evidence for sequential Υ(nS) suppression in light ion collisions
item.dc:creator: CMS Collaboration
item.description:
CMS reports the first measurements of Υ(1S,2S,3S) in oxygen-oxygen and Υ(1S,2S) in neon-neon collisions at √(s_NN)=5.36 TeV, with a pp reference at the same energy (integrated luminosities 8.4 nb⁻¹, 0.81 nb⁻¹, 456 pb⁻¹). Double ratios of excited-to-ground-state yields relative to pp come out below unity in OO: D_21=0.664±0.055±0.007, D_31=0.392±0.077±0.023, D_32=0.59±0.12±0.04 — the last below unity by 3.2σ, the headline “evidence” for sequential suppression in a light-ion system. In NeNe, D_21=0.27±0.12±0.01, lower than OO by 3.0σ. The OO Υ(3S)/Υ(2S) ratio is compatible with PbPb across p_T and integrated, supporting a common QGP-medium interpretation.

Why it matters: it extends state-dependent bottomonium suppression to ⟨N_part⟩≈10, a system size an order of magnitude below PbPb, reinforcing that QGP-like final-state effects need not require large volumes — bearing on the long-running debate over deconfinement in small systems. Caveats the paper flags: the D_32 significance is modest (3.2σ); event-activity trends “should be carefully interpreted” since multiplicity alone does not fix suppression (head-on OO can rival PbPb particle production per participant); and the shinchon transport model “significantly underestimates” the measured suppression, hinting at missing medium dynamics.

item.title: Observation of pair production of longitudinally polarized Z bosons in four-lepton final state with the ATLAS detector
item.dc:creator: ATLAS Collaboration
item.description: (abstract only) ATLAS measures ZZ production in the 4ℓ channel (ee/μμ pairs) using 164 fb⁻¹ at √(s)=13.6 TeV, extracting polarization fractions inclusively and in two m_4ℓ regions — all consistent with the SM. The headline comes from combining with the earlier 13 TeV measurement: the first observation of two simultaneously longitudinally polarized Z bosons, at 6.5σ observed (5.6σ expected). This pushes the electroweak-symmetry-breaking program — long anchored in single-boson W_L/Z_L fractions and W_LW_L scattering — into the doubly-longitudinal diboson sector, directly probing the Goldstone-mode content of two gauge bosons at once. The caveat is structural: a genuine observation is only reached after statistical combination across two center-of-mass energies, so the 13.6 TeV dataset alone is not yet decisive, and the analysis reports agreement with the SM rather than any deviation.

item.title: Bounds on axion-like particles from fully merged photons at the LHC
item.dc:creator: Simon Knapen
item.description:
Knapen recasts the ATLAS 139 fb⁻¹ high-mass diphoton resonance search (2102.13405) into an ALP-photon bound by exploiting that for 0.1–6 GeV ALPs the two decay photons from qq̅→aγ merge into a single reconstructed photon. Because the aFF̃ operator is dimension-five, the parton cross section is energy-independent while the γγ background falls as 1/m_γγ², so the signal-to-background ratio grows as (m_γγg_aγγ)²; a profile-likelihood fit to bins with m_γγ>1.5 TeV yields g_aγγ≈4×10⁻⁴ GeV⁻¹, the strongest current bound over most of 0.1–6 GeV. PDF systematics are shown subdominant (~10% of the statistical uncertainty). This is a clean, reinterpretation-style result that plants an LHC flag in a mass window otherwise covered by beam dumps, FASER and e⁺e⁻ machines — squarely today’s “axions fanning out” theme.

Honest caveats are flagged by the author himself: the limit weakens below 0.2 GeV (displaced decays) and above 1 GeV due to a deliberately conservative tight-photon merging requirement (Δη<0.003). A dedicated ATLAS analysis with one loose + one tight photon should do better. Also, under the alternative c_W≈c_B ansatz the B→Ka bound (g_aγγ≲5×10⁻⁶ GeV⁻¹) is far stronger — so the result’s competitiveness is specific to the c_B≫c_W scenario.

item.title: Three-Loop QCD Corrections to Scattering Amplitudes of a Higgs Boson and Three Partons
item.dc:creator: Xin Guan et al.
item.description:
Guan, Mistlberger and Ruf deliver the full-color three-loop helicity amplitudes for H+3 partons (Hggg and Hqq̅g) in the heavy-top EFT, using Blade IBP reduction via block-triangular forms and canonical differential equations, with results in compact generalized-polylogarithm form (full reduction ~several hundred thousand core-hours). All checks pass: infrared pole structure, collinear/soft factorization, AMFlow numerics, agreement with the prior leading-color result (2504.06490), and the striking confirmation that the leading-transcendental part coincides with the 𝒩=4 sYM tr(ϕ²⁾ form factor — now including subleading color. These are the virtual ingredients for H+jet at N³LO and a building block toward inclusive gluon-fusion at N⁴LO.

The notable phenomenological finding: at N³LO the subleading-color contribution to the amplitude is of the same order as the leading-color term — in sharp contrast to lower loops, where subleading color is negligible. This is a direct caution against generalized-leading-color truncation at this order. The reassuring counterpoint is that, evaluated at α_s=0.118, the net three-loop impact on the tree-normalized interference is small (sub-percent shift in the cumulant on the t=u slice), so the series remains well-behaved even as its color decomposition becomes non-hierarchical.

item.title: The Neutron Electric Dipole Moment from Lattice QCD using a Background Electric Field
item.dc:creator: Thomas Blum et al.
item.description:
Blum et al. extract the θ̄-induced neutron EDM from the energy shift of a neutron in a static, imaginary-valued Euclidean electric field, arriving at d_n = -0.0050(4)_stat(8)_sys θ̅ efm at the physical point. Two methodological moves drive the precision. First, motivated by Feynman-Hellmann, they sample the topological charge density on a single time slice rather than integrating the global charge Q_top — the disconnected topological correlator is the noise bottleneck, and localizing it plus a full-volume low-mode average sharpens the signal dramatically. Second, because the background field deforms the nucleon and mixes parity, the naive positive-parity projector suffers large excited-state contamination; they instead solve a non-Hermitian (PT-symmetric, S-pseudo-Hermitian) GEVP in the space of the nucleon, its parity partner and excitations to isolate the true ground state. Reassuringly, EDM values agree across chiral-covariant and non-covariant interpolators and across gluonic vs. pseudoscalar-density definitions of the topological charge, and the global-charge method gives results consistent with (but far noisier than) the new estimator.

This is the kind of controlled number the EDM and 0νββ programs need to convert experimental limits into bounds on θ̅ and BSM CP-violating operators, and the local-charge + GEVP toolkit extends naturally to the Weinberg and chromo-EDM operators. Caveats are stated frankly: the calculation uses a single lattice spacing (a≈0.11 fm) and pion masses of 340–576 MeV, so discretization, finite-volume and chiral-extrapolation systematics are deferred to future work; the electro-quenched approximation is assumed benign (~1% for magnetic moments). It also lands amid ongoing dispute over whether the θ-term generates a nonzero nEDM at all.

item.title: On the Origins of the Strong CP Problem
item.dc:creator: Anthony G. Williams
item.description:
Williams argues that the strong CP problem is contingent, not mandatory. He defines “minimal QCD” — the standard Lagrangian plus local gauge invariance, causal locality, and the functional integral — and shows that essentially every established nonperturbative result attributed to topology follows within it without assuming the gauge-field configuration space decomposes into integer-valued sectors. The topological susceptibility emerges as χ=⟨Q̂²⟩/V=∂²ε_0/∂θ² with θ treated purely as a source parameter for the local operator q(x); the axial anomaly identifies the invariant θ̅=θ+M; and the ’t Hooft vertex, Witten–Veneziano (m_η’²⁼²N_fχ_YM/f_0²) and Leutwyler–Smilga (χ=Σ/∑_f m_f⁻¹) relations all rely only on local operators, semiclassical saddle points, or the large-N_c expansion. The integer-valued Q∈ℤ, the 2π-periodicity, the sector weighting e^iθQ, the physical θ-vacuum and hence the fine-tuning problem appear only after supplementing minimal QCD with smoothness/boundary assumptions (π_3(SU(3))=ℤ) — assumptions, he stresses, that typical distributional (non-differentiable) functional-integral configurations need not satisfy, and that lattice topology recovers only via added constructions (gradient flow, index theorem).

If this framing holds, the “problem” becomes a question about which additional structure Nature actually requires, reframing the recent Nelson-Barr/PQ solution flurry as answers to a possibly-optional question. The honest caveat is baked in: this is a foundational/logical clarification, not a new prediction. Williams explicitly does not claim a θ-term is forbidden by symmetry, does not dispute the θ↔pseudoscalar-mass equivalence, and concedes future theory or data could yet demand the global structure — in which case the entire conventional literature immediately reapplies.

item.title: Observation of new excited Σ_c⁰ states in B⁻→Λ_c⁺p̅π⁻
item.dc:creator: LHCb collaboration et al.
item.description:
An LHCb amplitude analysis of B⁻→Λ_c⁺p̅π⁻ using the full 9 fb⁻¹ Run 1+2 dataset (37.0×10³ signal decays, 5.1% combinatorial background) resolves the Λ_c⁺π⁻ spectrum into the known Σ_c(2455)⁰, Σ_c(2520)⁰ and Σ_c(2800)⁰ plus two new states, Σ_c(2900)⁰ and Σ_c(3200)⁰ — the first new excited Σ_c⁰ baryons in over two decades. The two-resonance description of the ~2.8 GeV region (splitting the old BaBar Σ_c(2800)⁰ into overlapping states) is favored at 7.5σ, and the Σ_c(3200)⁰ is observed at 12.0σ. Combining the two solution families, they measure m_Σ_c(3200)⁰⁼³.186±0.006±0.015 GeV/c², Γ=0.133±0.018±0.046 GeV. The Σ_c(2520)⁰ spin-parity is pinned to 3/2⁺ (>6σ) and the Σ_c(2455)⁰ spin to 1/2. Candidate interpretations span 2S/1P for the Σ_c(2900)⁰ and 2P/3S for the Σ_c(3200)⁰.

This materially expands the sparse Σ_c sector — only three states were previously established — providing masses and widths to confront the crowded quark-model predictions for 2S/1D/2P λ- and ρ-mode excitations, part of today’s experiment-anchored spectroscopy cluster. The central honest caveat is that spin-parity cannot be unambiguously fixed: multiple J^P assignments give nearly degenerate likelihoods, yielding two solution groups (A and B) statistically indistinguishable (2Δlnℒ<1) yet giving very different masses, widths and fit fractions for the Σ_c(2800)⁰/Σ_c(2900)⁰ pair — group A matches Belle’s Σ_c(2800)⁰ (which sees no Σ_c(2900)⁰), group B does not. Only the Σ_c(3200)⁰ parameters are robust across solutions.

(The digest’s two other “worth a look” picks — arXiv:2607.10417 and arXiv:2607.09845 — were not included in today’s full-text batch, so no deep dive is possible here.)

item.title: Revisiting bounds on neutrino dark matter interaction at spikes
item.dc:creator: Yasaman Farzan
item.description:
The finding: The much-quoted “spike” bounds on neutrino–DM scattering — derived from the attenuation of AGN neutrino fluxes traversing the dense DM cusp around supermassive black holes — collapse for light vector mediators. Farzan’s point is kinematic: the cascade equation contains both a loss term (-σΦ) and a regeneration term (the down-scattered flux re-populating each energy bin). Previous analyses (Cline et al., Cline–Puel, Dixit–Mohlabeng–Razzaque) kept only the loss term, valid only if each collision removes a neutrino from the beam. But when m_Z’²/(2m_DM)≪E_ν, the differential cross section is sharply peaked at E’_ν≃E_ν — scattering is nearly forward, energy loss negligible, and the two terms cancel. Defining an effective suppression factor f, for Φ∝E_ν⁻³.2 and m_Z’²/m_DM=2 GeV, Farzan finds 2×10⁻³<f<10⁻² across the 1.5–15 TeV NGC 1068 window — relaxing the “most stringent” bound by up to ~1000×.

Why it matters: Landing the same day as Abbaslu et al.’s paper deriving AGN flavor signals from this same scattering, it’s a clean cautionary counterpoint: “spike constraints” on σ_νDM carry hidden microphysics (mediator mass, symmetric vs. asymmetric DM, flavor structure). Farzan further notes symmetric DM can annihilate to νν̅, and flavor-selective couplings can suppress attenuation while still distorting flavor ratios — leaving room for IceCube-Gen2/KM3NeT to discover spike effects rather than merely exclude them. Caveat: the companion analysis establishing the flavor phenomenology is “work in progress,” so the positive-signal claims rest partly on unpublished results.

item.title: Neutrino-induced hyperon final-state interactions as constraints on the in-medium hyperon potential
item.dc:creator: Jaroslaw Nowak
item.description:
What they did: Nowak proposes that charged-current accelerator (anti)neutrinos on ⁴⁰Ar create Λ,Σ hyperons inside the nucleus, so their final-state interactions become a terrestrial probe of the in-medium potentials U_Y(ρ) that drive the neutron-star “hyperon puzzle.” Using the internal StrangeMC generator, three observables respond monotonically to the potentials: the trapped-Λ fraction and escaping-Λ momentum (for U_Λ), the escaping-Σ momentum, and a kaon-vetoed FSI-Σ⁺ tag (a final state the weak vertex cannot make) for U_Σ. A detector-level Fisher forecast gives δU_Λ≈0.3 MeV and δU_Σ≈3–4 MeV at fixed low-density slope γ. Fed through a GM1 relativistic mean field anchored to established depths, the same potentials yield M_max=1.94 M_⊙ and Λ_1.4=1034.

The honesty: The headline sub-MeV number is heavily caveated. Because hyperons are born below saturation, U_Λ(ρ_0) and γ are 99.8% anti-correlated; marginalizing over γ (which the data alone fix only to δγ≈0.8) degrades δU_Λ to 5.6 MeV. Two further systematics — the transport prescription (−6 MeV) and YN cross sections (−5/+2 MeV) — push the realistic U_Λ budget to ~10 MeV. Worse, the YN uncertainty biases U_Σ by 𝒪(150) MeV, not an artifact of the Σ⁺ tag but because the Λ spectrum itself is YN-sensitive. The propagated M_max is explicitly an inference dominated by the external high-density prior, not a neutrino measurement; the ~0.3 M_⊙ EOS-model systematic dwarfs the statistical reach. StrangeMC is uncommissioned against community generators — a stated next step.

item.title: Top-Antitop Production and Decay at Threshold at the LHC in QCD Perturbation Theory
item.dc:creator: Paolo Nason et al.
item.description:
What they did: Nason, Pelliccioli, Re and Rottoli deliver three NLO+PS generators (thr1, thr2, bb4l) incorporating threshold-enhanced (Coulomb/Sommerfeld) corrections in tt̅ production, extending their earlier NRR work up to (α_s/v)⁶ and, crucially, with finite-width treatment (thr2 modifies the phase space for off-shell tops; bb4l uses the full b_bbar_4l off-shell code). In the “ATLAS bin” (m_tt̅<350 GeV, p^⋆<50 GeV) they find total cross sections near 10 pb with a threshold excess over baseline NLO of ~4 pb — compatible with the Garzelli et al. NRQCD result and with the 8.5–9.3 pb “η_t” numbers CMS/ATLAS extract. The perturbative series converges: truncating at α_s³ already captures the full result to better than 1 pb, so all-orders GFRW resummation is unnecessary at LHC resolution.

Why it matters: This directly addresses the recent near-threshold “toponium” observation, and sharpens the interpretation. The authors argue forcefully that (i) the pseudoscalar dominance follows from the Landau–Yang theorem for gluon fusion regardless of bound-state formation; (ii) toponium is part of the perturbative QCD cross section, so claiming an “excess above QCD consistent with QCD-predicted toponium” is contradictory; and (iii) the genuine bound-state contribution is small (~2.6–4.5 pb depending on generator/scale) and cannot be cleanly separated from continuum given the top width smearing. A new physical effect: imposing double-top virtuality cuts suppresses the sub-threshold cross section via phase-space reduction, cutting the bound-state yield by ~1 pb — captured by thr2/bb4l but not thr1. Caveat: the exact finite-width resummation formula (Appendix A) is derived but not implemented; single-top contamination near threshold requires a full experimental signal/background study the authors defer.

item.title: The 20 GeV Galactic Halo Excess: Pixel-Level Confirmation and Consistency with Sub-TeV WIMP Annihilation
item.dc:creator: Trinity Rosebud Stenhouse et al.
item.description:
Stenhouse, Ghag & Deppisch independently reproduce Totani’s cell-aggregated Fermi-LAT halo excess and extend it to a pixel-level Poisson likelihood on native 0.125° maps with energy-dependent PSF forward-folding and bright-source masking. The two methods agree on the spectrum — a peak at ~20.8 GeV — with the pixel-level normalization ~20% higher for the ρ² halo, confirming the feature is not an artifact of 10° binning. The excess is centrally concentrated (angular profile χ²/ν≃5–7 for NFW vs 30 for isotropic), spectrally and spatially distinct from the few-GeV GCE, and stable under a foreground-systematics suite and an injection-null test (a distorted-ICS mock with no halo yields ≤10% of the observed peak). Prompt s-wave fits give mχ≃0.55 TeV (W⁺W⁻) and 0.72 TeV (bb̄) with ⟨σv⟩≃1×10⁻²⁴ cm³ s⁻¹.

Why it matters: this is exactly the independent stress-test the weekly memory flagged. The headline tension is with dwarf-spheroidal limits, ℛ≃5.1 face-value, widening to 1.6–9.3 once foreground choice (GALPROP vs GIEM dominates, halving the flux) and J-factor uncertainties are folded in — so s-wave is not excluded but not comfortable. Crucially, p/d-wave over-resolves the dwarf tension but misses relic abundance by ~7 orders of magnitude; decay is disfavored by the IGRB. Only resonant Sommerfeld/Breit-Wigner survives, supplying the needed ≈45× boost — but requiring a fine-tuned above-threshold resonance and a structured dark sector. Caveat honestly stated: χ²/ν∼8 from coherent diffuse residuals, and AMS-02 antiprotons independently disfavor direct bb̄; this is “consistency,” not detection.

item.title: A Novel Hadronic Calorimeter With A Direct Neutron Readout
item.dc:creator: I. Giomataris et al.
item.description:
Giomataris et al. simulate (Geant4, benchmarked against FLUKA) a sampling calorimeter of alternating Pb absorbers and Gd-loaded LAB scintillator that reads out both the prompt scintillation and a delayed signal from neutron moderation and capture. In a six-layer prototype (3.66 λ_I) hit by 10 GeV protons, ~197 neutrons/proton are captured with a median capture time of 11.1 μs; the delayed deposited energy is almost perfectly proportional to capture multiplicity (R²=0.9998, slope 7.97 MeV/neutron), giving direct calibration. Gadolinium’s key benefit is timing, not yield: 0.5% Gd collects >85% of captures within 20 μs versus ~10% for pure LAB. Because neutron production tracks the invisible hadronic energy, a branch-wise event-by-event correction using the delayed signal improves prompt resolution from 21.8% to 13.3% — a ~63% variance reduction — with no event rejection.

Why it matters: this is a hardware attack on the invisible-energy fluctuations that fundamentally limit hadronic resolution, complementary to dual-readout. The intrinsic neutron-counting resolution (~7%) is far below the 21.8% calorimetric resolution, confirming that neutron-production fluctuations, not the detector, dominate — and can be measured out. Events binned by fixed neutron multiplicity show resolution falling to ~6%, suggesting the method scales favorably to higher energies. Caveats are explicit: a single 10 GeV energy, a shallow preliminary geometry, and no optical-photon transport, photosensor, or electronics modeling yet — the 13.3% is a proof-of-principle, not a device spec.

item.title: Transformer-based machine learning using low-level calorimeter signals for collimated photon identification
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Matos et al.
item.description:
(Abstract only.) The authors use calorimeter cell-level information to separate highly collimated diphoton signatures — from light axion-like-particle decays — from isolated single photons, systematically comparing six architectures spanning high-level shower-shape approaches and direct cell-level methods. Cell-level ML decisively outperforms shower-shape variables, with a Transformer best overall and an MLP Mixer offering a resource-constrained option for trigger-level deployment. Beyond classification, the Transformer performs direct invariant-mass regression from cells, sharpening light-resonance characterization and adding a handle to suppress π⁰ and η fake-photon backgrounds.

Why it matters: this is the calorimetry front of the week’s ML-reconstruction arc — the same raw-input-beats-engineered-features lesson seen in flavor tagging, now applied to fine-grained EM showers. Direct mass regression from cells is the notable step beyond classification. No numerical performance figures are available in the provided text.

item.title: Single inclusive hadron and jet production in lepton-hadron scattering
item.dc:creator: Jian-Wei Qiu et al.
item.description:
The first calculation of high-p_T single-inclusive hadron (π^±,K^±) and jet production in e+h→H+X within joint QCD+QED collinear factorization, treating collision-induced QED radiation on equal footing with QCD. The cross section factorizes into hard parts (kept at NLO) convolved with universal lepton distribution functions (LDFs), PDFs (JAM20/CT18) and FFs (JAM20/MAP1.0), with DGLAP kernels carrying mixed QCD+QED splitting functions. Because a photon can split to qq̅ nonperturbatively, LDFs are genuinely nonperturbative objects; the authors start evolution at μ_0=m_c (not m_e) and build a “default” LDF set from a Beta-function ansatz constrained by number and momentum sum rules, then evolve to LHAPDF6-compatible grids. Headline numbers: collision-induced QED radiation reshapes the hadron p_T spectrum by up to ~50% (depleting high-p_T, enhancing low-p_T); jet spectra drop ~10–20%; scale uncertainty runs ~20–25%, but the LDF (μ_e) piece is only a few percent. Nuclear modification factors show EMC suppression below p_T∼10 GeV and Fermi-motion enhancement above.

Why it matters: this is the LDF program’s most concrete deliverable — a unified treatment of leptoproduction and photoproduction with no ad hoc Q² cut or “resolved photon” structure, exactly the framework the digest flags as sub-percent-precision machinery aimed at JLab and the EIC. The key caveat is honest and stated repeatedly: the LDFs are still model defaults (quark/gluon content set to zero at input, so those are lower limits), and existing data carry traditional radiative corrections and cannot be used to fit true LDFs until reanalyzed à la ZEUS. Dominant theory uncertainty is currently the FF choice, not the scales.

item.title: Search for axion-like particles decaying to two photons at Belle II
item.dc:creator: Belle II Collaboration et al.
item.description:
Using 408 fb⁻¹ of Belle II data, a search for e⁺e⁻→γa, a→γγ reconstructs the ALP as a narrow diphoton peak over 0.17<m_a<9.80 GeV/c², assuming photon-dominant coupling (ℬ(a→γγ)=1). Three-photon events are selected with a helicity-angle cut (|cosλ|<0.74) to suppress the dominant γγ(γ) background, a kinematic fit sharpening the mass resolution to 10–16 MeV/c², and a 19-feature neural-network classifier. No significant excess: the largest local significance is 3.3σ near m_a=0.22 GeV/c², reducing to 1.4σ global after look-elsewhere. The resulting 95% CL limits on g_aγγ reach ∼10⁻⁴ GeV⁻¹ and are the most restrictive to date over nearly all of 0.17<m_a<5.00 GeV/c² (except near 0.22 GeV/c²), improving on the prior Belle II result by up to a factor 9.

Why it matters: this cleanly extends the dark-sector portal coverage flagged in today’s digest, closing an intermediate-mass gap between beam-dump/forward limits and heavy-ion light-by-light constraints with a single tabletop-clean channel. Improvements over the 2020 Belle II analysis come from the kinematic fit, the NN, and the larger sample. Caveats are modest and disclosed: the coupling extraction ignores possible energy dependence of α_QED and g_aγγ, and η/ω mass windows are vetoed for peaking backgrounds. The mild 0.22 GeV/c² bump is statistically unremarkable.

item.title: Experimental access to the gluonic origin of the proton mass
item.dc:creator: Zein-Eddine Meziani et al.
item.description:
A concrete reconstruction scheme for the scalar gluonic trace form factor G_N(t) — the dominant, trace-anomaly source of the proton mass — from three measurable inputs. Their central identity (Eq. 14) writes G_N(t)=G_s,g(t)+G_s,q(t)-σ(t)/M: the quark scalar gravitational form factor from DVCS, the gluon scalar GFF from near-threshold J/ψ photoproduction (extracted via holographic QCD from JLab data), and the nucleon sigma-term form factor. At zero momentum transfer this reduces to G_N(0)=1-σ(0)/M_N. Plugging in the phenomenological A_q(0)=0.576±0.011 and lattice dipole/tripole GFF fits, the reconstructed G_N(t) falls rapidly with -t and agrees, within bands, with an independent lattice-QCD trace-anomaly determination — and, for -t≲1 GeV², with the interacting instanton liquid model, supporting a picture where the long-distance scalar gluonic structure is dominated by semiclassical topological glue.

Why it matters: this converts an abstract mass-decomposition question into a defined experimental program, tying together DVCS, near-threshold quarkonium, and σ-term measurements — exactly the gravitational-form-factor thread the digest has tracked this week. The lattice consistency is a genuine cross-check rather than an input. Caveats: the result relies on holographic-QCD modeling to extract G_s,g from J/ψ data and on lattice/phenomenological fits for the quark piece, so it is a proof-of-principle reconstruction rather than a fully data-driven extraction; ILM–lattice agreement degrades above -t≃1 GeV² where short-distance gluon dynamics enter.

item.title: Non-Unitarity Effects and Fake CP Violation in Neutrino Oscillation Experiments
item.dc:creator: Pratima Singh et al.
item.description:
Using GLoBES with a custom non-unitary probability engine, Singh et al. quantify how a single off-diagonal PMNS deviation α_21=|α_21|e^iφ_21 fakes CP violation at DUNE and Hyper-K. The headline: at each experiment’s oscillation maximum the fake asymmetry is a mild perturbation (1.7% of the genuine swing at DUNE’s 2.4 GeV, 4.5% at Hyper-K’s 0.5 GeV for |α_21|=0.01), but in suppressed-genuine windows near 1.5–1.6 GeV the fake-to-genuine ratio exceeds unity — 129% at DUNE, 134% at Hyper-K, with a second 129% window for Hyper-K at 2.0 GeV. In these bins an A_CP-only analysis cannot separate real from fake CP, and the sign of φ_21 is invisible in the broad-peak region. The degeneracy analysis shows Hyper-K alone leaves φ_21 essentially unconstrained at ≥2σ (matter effects too weak to reject the wrong ordering, χ²_min=4.4), while DUNE’s 1300 km matter lever arm pins it (χ²_min=486). Their combination shrinks the 3σ allowed (δ_CP,φ_21) area to 0.059π² — 16.3× smaller than Hyper-K alone.

Why it matters: this is the week’s reference point for “fake CP.” It concretely localizes where non-unitarity is dangerous (specific energy bins, not the oscillation maximum) and confirms the recurring prescription — combine complementary baselines rather than trusting either detector. Caveat: only the minimal single-parameter α_21=0.01 scenario is explored, and the combined 3σ area is marginally larger than DUNE alone, an honestly-flagged artifact of Hyper-K’s flat directions overlapping DUNE’s contour edge.

item.title: Probing Quasi-Dirac Neutrino Oscillations at Long Baseline Experiments
item.dc:creator: Noor-Ines Boudjema et al.
item.description:
Boudjema, Deppisch & Pattanaik embed the quasi-Dirac scenario — small lepton-number-violating Majorana mass μ splitting a near-degenerate sterile pair — in an inverse-seesaw-motivated 3+2 framework, deriving analytic ν_μ→ν_e and ν_μ→ν_μ probabilities with the sterile splitting Δm²_54∝μ driving a slow interference term. Simulating NOvA, T2K and DUNE in GLoBES with full systematics, they map sensitivity in (θ_sa,Δm²_54). Current NOvA and T2K each reach θ_sa≈0.1; combined, ≈0.08.
